Removing the first and last vertices from a hole leaves the long arc between their
neighbours.

decls.name: leap_common_neighbor_contra
decls.docstring:
A leap at an edge of an even hole cannot have a common neighbour which is anticomplete
to the hole: the long arc between the two leap vertices, closed through that common
neighbour, is an odd hole.

decls.name: two_caps_contra
decls.docstring:
Two disjoint capped edges of a long hole, joined outside the hole by an induced path,
form a long prism.

decls.name: Frame
decls.docstring:
The structural data produced by the first half of the printed claim-(2) argument.  Keeping
this package in an opaque declaration prevents the dependent list-index proof from being
reduced again in each of the two parity cases.

decls.name: exists_frame
decls.docstring: The opaque structural half of claim (2).

decls.name: zero_exception_contra
decls.docstring:
The single-edge exceptional case in the printed parity argument.  The hole through
`p₀,F,p_α` has the `X`-complete edge `p₀f_k`; 2.10 gives either a clean cap, which
together with the triangle at `p_αp_βf₁` makes a long prism, or a leap, which closes
through the other `X`-complete end `p_n` to make an odd hole.

decls.name: left_clear
decls.docstring:
The optimality step common to both cases of claim (2): if all attachments of
`F \ {f₁}` occur at or after the assumed `Y`-complete vertex, then the tight left endpoint is
joined to `f₁`, and no noninitial vertex before that endpoint is `Y`-complete.

decls.name: last_nonempty_contra
decls.docstring:
The `b₂ = n` case when `F \ {f₁}` has an actual attachment.  The first such
attachment and the last attachment of `F \ {f_k}` close the path through `F` into the hole
used in the printed proof.

decls.name: suffix_path_contra
decls.docstring:
The path `f_k-⋯-f₁-p_β-⋯-p_n` contradicts 18.3 whenever no vertex of its
`P`-suffix attaches to `F \ {f₁}` and that suffix has an odd number of `Y`-complete edges.

decls.name: zero_nonempty_contra
decls.docstring:
The `a₂=b₂=0` case with a genuine attachment.  The left part has even
`Y`-complete-edge count by 2.3.  Unless the one edge between the two tight endpoints is
itself `Y`-complete, the odd total count therefore lies in the right suffix and 18.3 applies;
the remaining one-edge exception is `zero_exception_contra`.

decls.name: empty_F₂_contra
decls.docstring:
If `F \ {f₁}` has no attachment at all, optimality moves every `Y`-complete edge into
the suffix beginning at the last attachment of `F \ {f_k}`; `suffix_path_contra` then applies.
This is the empty-attachment case omitted from the corresponding sentence in the paper.

decls.name: claim2
decls.docstring:
**18.6, claim (2)**: *"There do not exist `a, b` with `1 < a < b ≤ n` such that `p_a` is an
attachment of `F` and `p_b` is `Y`-complete."*

links.rationale: Formalizes printed claim (2) of 18.6's proof: there do not exist a, b with 0 < a < b < P.length such that P[a] is an attachment of a minimal counterexample F and P[b] is Y-complete.

Formalizes the sentence 'From 18.5 |F| ≥ 2' that opens 18.6's proof: a counterexample F to 18.6 (admissible but not Good) must have at least two elements, since the empty set is trivially Good via P'={p1} and a singleton is settled directly by Theorem 18.5.

decls.name: exists_greatest
decls.docstring: Greatest index below `n` satisfying `Q`.

decls.name: getElem_congr_idx
decls.docstring:
Rewriting the index of a `getElem`.  Plain `rw` on the index equation gives
"motive is not type correct", because the bound proof mentions the index.

decls.name: slice_infix
decls.docstring: Every stretch of `p` is a contiguous block of `p`.

decls.name: final_contradiction
decls.docstring:
**18.6, closing paragraph.**  Claim (2) plus the counterexample property produce the hole
`p₁-⋯-p_c-Q-p₁`, which carries an odd number `≥ 3` of `Y`-complete edges by 18.4 — contrary to
2.3.

links.rationale: Formalizes the closing paragraph of 18.6's proof: from claim (2) and the counterexample property of F, the stretch p1-⋯-pc-Q-p1 closes into a hole whose Y-complete edges are exactly those of P, giving an odd number (at least 3) of them by 18.4, contrary to 2.3 — completing the minimal-counterexample contradiction.

decls.name: hole_through_F
decls.docstring:
**The paper's hole `p₁-⋯-p_c-Q-p₁`.**

`P` is an induced path, `Q` an induced path from `P[0]` to `P[c]` whose interior lies in a set
`F` disjoint from `V(P)`, and no vertex of `P` strictly between `P[0]` and `P[c]` has a
neighbour in `F`.  Then the stretch `P[0], …, P[c]` closed through the interior of `Q` is a
hole.

links.rationale: Generic hole-closing construction reused at four points in 18.6's proof (claim (1), twice in claim (2), and the closing paragraph): if Q is an induced path from P[0] to P[c] with interior in a set F disjoint from P, and no internal vertex of the P[0]..P[c] stretch has a neighbour in F, then that stretch closed through Q's interior is a hole.

decls.name: mem_hole_iff
decls.docstring:
The vertex list of the hole, for transporting a `Y`-complete-edge count across it: the hole
consists of the stretch `p₁ … p_c` together with the interior of `Q`.

links.rationale: Trivial membership unfolding for the glued hole list P.take(c+1) ++ (interior Q).reverse, used to transport facts about the hole's vertices back to facts about P and the interior of Q; not reachable from the main theorem in the compiled dependency graph.

decls.name: Adm
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"Let `F ⊆ V(G) \ (X ∪ Y ∪ V(P))` be connected, such that no vertex in `F` is
`Y`-complete."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the standing hypothesis on F in the statement of 18.6: F is a connected set of vertices disjoint from X, Y and V(P), none of which is Y-complete.

decls.name: Good
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"Then there is a subpath `P'` of `P` such that `V(P')` contains all the attachments
of `F` in `P`; there is no `Y`-complete vertex in the interior of `P'`; and if some vertex of
`F` is `X`-complete then either `V(P') = {p₁}` or `pₙ ∈ V(P')`."*

Byte-for-byte the conclusion of the frozen `Workspace.Statements.S18.SPGT.thm_18_6`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the conclusion of 18.6 for a particular admissible F: there is a subpath P' of P whose vertex set contains every attachment of F in P, has no Y-complete interior vertex, and (if some vertex of F is X-complete) equals {p1} or reaches pn.

decls.name: MinCounterexample
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"Suppose the theorem is false, and choose a minimal counterexample `F`."*

Minimality is in `|F|`, which is how the printed proof uses it: the sets `F \ {f₁}`,
`F \ {f_k}` and the various `{f_i, …, f_k}` it forms are all *smaller*, hence good.

links.rationale: Formalizes the proof's opening move 'choose a minimal counterexample F': F is admissible, not Good, and every admissible set strictly smaller in cardinality is Good.

decls.name: exists_minCounterexample
decls.docstring:
*"Suppose the theorem is false, and choose a minimal counterexample `F`."*  A counterexample
of least cardinality exists as soon as there is one at all.

links.rationale: Establishes the existence of a minimal counterexample asserted by 18.6's proof: given any admissible non-Good F, a cardinality-minimal admissible non-Good F0 exists, by well-ordering on the natural-number cardinalities of counterexamples.

decls.name: claim1
decls.docstring:
Claim **(1)** of the printed proof of 19.2: *"There exists `y ∈ Y` adjacent to `z` and
with a neighbour in `A`, such that `Y \ {y}` is empty or anticonnected."*

Stated with `A₁` in place of `A`; see the module header for why the two extremal choices
have to be taken in the opposite order to the printed one.

links.rationale: Produces the vertex y required by claim (1) of the printed proof: y is in Y, adjacent to z, has a neighbour in A1, and Y minus y is empty or anticonnected; the proof takes the paper's two extremal choices (the minimal Y and the minimal A) in the opposite order, so the claim is proved with A1 rather than the not-yet-chosen minimal A (see the module header for why this changes nothing).

decls.name: no_adj_zero
decls.docstring:
The one-sided form of claim (10).  The second side is obtained below by reversing
the fixed path and swapping `x₀,x₁`.

decls.name: claim10
decls.docstring: Claim **(10)** of the printed proof: *"`x₂` is nonadjacent to both of `x₀, x₁`."*

links.rationale: Establishes claim (10): x2 is nonadjacent to both x0 and x1, by ruling out adjacency to either (they are symmetric) through the 17.1 reflection/wheel-parity argument built on the vertex f fixed by claims (7) and (9).

decls.name: firstReflectionForcesAdjacencyWithPath
decls.docstring:
The path-carrying form of `firstReflectionForcesAdjacency`.  The fixed rim
`z :: P` supplies the hole that excludes the reflection by 15.7.

links.rationale: Proves the first 17.1 step of claim (10)'s proof: assuming x2 is adjacent to x0, if x0 is not adjacent to f then A union x1 catches the triangle z,x2,x0 with no reflection (that would give a 6-antihole sharing three vertices with C), so 17.1 forces x0 to be adjacent to f.

decls.name: firstReflectionForcesAdjacency
decls.docstring:
PAPER (19.2, claim (10), printed p. 122):

*"For suppose that `x₂` is adjacent to `x₀` say. Suppose first that `x₀` is not
adjacent to `f`. Then `A ∪ {x₁}` catches the triangle `{z,x₂,x₀}`; the only
neighbour of `z` in `A ∪ {x₁}` is `x₁`; the only neighbour of `x₂` in
`A ∪ {x₁}` is `f`; `x₁,f` are both nonadjacent to `x₀`; and `A ∪ {x₁}` contains
no reflection of the triangle since that would give a 6-antihole with 3 vertices
in common with `C`, contradicting 17.1. So `x₀` is adjacent to `f`."*

links.rationale: Not reachable from the main theorem Workspace.MainTheorem.SPGT.thm_1_2 in the compiled dependency graph. Wrapper form (supplying its own path through A) of the claim (10) step showing that if x2 is adjacent to x0 and x0 is not adjacent to f, the 17.1 reflection argument on A union x1 forces x0 to be adjacent to f after all; superseded in the compiled proof by the path-carrying form firstReflectionForcesAdjacencyWithPath.

decls.name: wheelLeapEndgame
decls.docstring:
PAPER (19.2, claim (10), printed p. 122), the remainder after the first
17.1 application:

*"So `x₀` is adjacent to `f`, and therefore `x₁` is nonadjacent to both `x₂,f`.
By (8) `x₂` is adjacent to `y`, and therefore not `Y₀`-complete. By (2) `z` is
`Y₀`-complete and `(C,Y₀)` is a wheel. Let `x₂-q₁-⋯-q_k-x₁` be a path ...
By 2.10, `Y` contains a leap or hat for `C₁`. But `y` is adjacent to `x₂`, and
all other vertices of `Y` have at least two neighbours in `{p₁,…,pₙ}`, which is
a subset of `{q₁,…,q_k}`, a contradiction."*

The hypotheses below record the four elementary consequences in the first two
sentences, leaving this lemma to encode only the wheel/path/leap argument.

links.rationale: Thin wrapper packaging the elementary consequences of the first 17.1 step (x0 adjacent to f, x1 nonadjacent to x2 and f, x2 adjacent to y and not Y0-complete, z Y0-complete with (C,Y0) a wheel) and delegating the remaining wheel/path/leap argument of claim (10)'s tail to Thm192Claim10Endgame.endgame.

Generic infrastructure lemma: unpacks a leap IsLeapForHole G C u v a b for a hole C into the two hole-neighbours s,v and t,u that a and b are respectively adjacent to, together with a and b being distinct and nonadjacent.

decls.name: endgame
decls.docstring:
PAPER (19.2, claim (10), printed p. 122), everything after the first application
of 17.1.  See the module header for the sentence-by-sentence map.

links.rationale: Carries out the wheel/path/leap tail of claim (10)'s proof after the first 17.1 application: builds the path x2-q1-...-qk-x1 and hole C1, uses claim (9) to show A equals its interior, applies claim (4) to see qk is not Y-complete, and derives a contradiction from 2.10 since y is adjacent to x2 while every other member of Y has two neighbours among q1,...,qk.

decls.name: anticonnected_singleton
decls.docstring: A singleton is anticonnected.

decls.name: claim11
decls.docstring:
Claim **(11)** of the printed proof: *"`z` is not `Y₀`-complete, and `x₂` is
`Y₀`-complete and nonadjacent to `y`."*

links.rationale: Establishes claim (11): z is not Y0-complete while x2 is Y0-complete and nonadjacent to y, by ruling out the alternative (z being Y0-complete) with a 17.3 contradiction on the hole C1 followed by a 13.6 parity contradiction on the resulting leap.

decls.name: three_common
decls.docstring:
*"contrary to 15.7"*: a hole and an antihole, both of length `> 4`, cannot share three
distinct vertices.

decls.name: exists_nonneighbour_of_anticonnected
decls.docstring:
In an anticonnected set, a vertex with another vertex beside it has a **non**neighbour
inside the set (the first step of an antipath out of it).

decls.name: claim12
decls.docstring:
Claim **(12)** of the printed proof: *"`y` is nonadjacent to all of
`q₁,…,q_{k−1}`."*

`hcex` (the minimum-counterexample hypothesis `¬ Concl192 G z A₀ x Y`) is a **pass-through**
here: the printed argument of (12) itself never makes the *"otherwise `(C,Y)` satisfies
19.2"* move — it uses (10), (11), 13.6 and 15.7 only.  But (10) and (11) each invoke claim
(4)'s second conjunct, which does need `hcex`, so (12) must supply it at those two call
sites.

links.rationale: Establishes claim (12): y has no neighbour among q1,...,q(k-1), by showing that any such neighbour would force i = 1 via 13.6 and then contradict 15.7 through an antihole sharing three vertices with the hole C1.

decls.name: claim2
decls.docstring:
Claim **(2)** of the printed proof: *"Either `x₂` is `Y₀`-complete and nonadjacent
to `y`, or `z` is `Y`-complete and there is a path `x₀-p₁-⋯-p_n-x₁` from `x₀` to `x₁`
with interior in `A`, containing at least two `Y₀`-complete edges."*

The remaining obligation is the localized use of induction described in the module header.

links.rationale: Establishes claim (2): either x2 is Y0-complete and nonadjacent to y, or z is Y-complete and there is a path from x0 to x1 with interior in A containing at least two Y0-complete edges, obtained by applying the induction hypothesis to Y0 inside the graph induced on A together with x0, x1, x2, z and Y0.

decls.name: path_in_minimal_A_of_inductive_wheel
decls.docstring:
PAPER (printed p. 118, claim (2)): *"From the minimality of `|Y|`, `z` is
`Y₀`-complete and therefore `Y`-complete, and there is a path as in the claim."*

Given the wheel in the required set, deleting `z` gives the path. The two complete
rim edges at `z` are removed, and 2.3 makes the remaining positive edge count even.
Minimality of `A` is not needed for this step.

links.rationale: Converts the wheel supplied by the smaller-hub induction into the path and complete-edge-count form asked for by claim (2): deleting z from the wheel's rim leaves a path from x0 to x1 with interior in A, and 2.3 makes the number of surviving Y0-complete rim edges after removing the two at z still at least two.

decls.name: compl_induce
decls.docstring: The complement of an induced subgraph is the induced subgraph of the complement.

links.rationale: Infrastructure lemma: the complement of an induced subgraph G restricted to S equals the induced subgraph of the complement, (G|S) complement = (G complement)|S.

decls.name: berge_induce
decls.docstring:
The complement of an induced subgraph is the induced subgraph of the complement. -/
theorem compl_induce (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Set V) : (G.induce S)ᶜ = Gᶜ.induce S := by
  ext a b
  simp [SimpleGraph.induce, Subtype.ext_iff]

private theorem hf : Function.Injective (Subtype.val : ↥S → V) := Subtype.val_injective

private theorem hadj (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Set V) :
    ∀ a b : ↥S, (G.induce S).Adj a b ↔ G.Adj a.1 b.1 := fun _ _ => Iff.rfl

/-! ### The individual conditions

links.rationale: Infrastructure lemma silently used by the induction of 19.2: an induced subgraph of a Berge graph is Berge, since a hole or antihole of the induced subgraph is (the image of) a hole or antihole of the ambient graph.

decls.name: exists_induce_iso
decls.docstring: An induced subgraph of `G|S` is an induced subgraph of `G`.

links.rationale: Infrastructure lemma: an induced subgraph of G|S is itself an induced subgraph of G, obtained by composing the two inclusion maps.

Not reachable from the main theorem Workspace.MainTheorem.SPGT.thm_1_2 in the compiled dependency graph. Membership in F1 (Berge with no induced Kneser-type obstruction) is inherited by induced subgraphs.

Not reachable from the main theorem Workspace.MainTheorem.SPGT.thm_1_2 in the compiled dependency graph. Membership in F2 is inherited by induced subgraphs, combining heredity of F1 for G and for its complement.
Infrastructure lemma silently used by the induction of 19.2: membership in F3 is inherited by induced subgraphs, in both G and its complement.

Not reachable from the main theorem Workspace.MainTheorem.SPGT.thm_1_2 in the compiled dependency graph. Membership in F4 (F3 plus no induced even prism) is inherited by induced subgraphs, using that an even prism transports along the induced-subgraph inclusion.
Infrastructure lemma silently used by the induction of 19.2: membership in F5 (F3 plus no induced long prism in G or its complement) is inherited by induced subgraphs.
Infrastructure lemma silently used by the induction of 19.2: membership in F6 (F5 plus no induced double diamond) is inherited by induced subgraphs.

decls.name: inF7_induce
decls.docstring:
**`F₇` is hereditary.**  This is what lets the induction of 19.2 be applied
inside an induced subgraph.

links.rationale: F7 is hereditary: membership in F7 (F6 plus no odd wheel in G or its complement) is inherited by induced subgraphs, which is what lets the induction of 19.2 be applied inside the induced subgraphs used by claim (2).

decls.name: eq_of_connected_isolated
decls.docstring: A vertex of a connected set with no neighbour in that set is its only vertex.

links.rationale: Generic infrastructure lemma: in a connected set, a vertex with no neighbour inside the set must be the set's only vertex.

decls.name: z_notMem_wheelSystemA
decls.docstring:
`z` belongs to no `Aᵢ`: a connected set containing `A₀` and no neighbour of `z`
cannot contain `z`, since `A₀` is nonempty and misses `z`.

links.rationale: Generic infrastructure lemma: z never belongs to any wheelSystemA set Ai, since a connected set containing the frame's A0 and none of z's neighbours cannot itself contain z.

decls.name: inductive_wheel_with_rim_in_A
decls.docstring:
**PAPER** (printed p. 118, claim (2)): *"From the minimality of `|Y|`, `z` is
`Y₀`-complete and therefore `Y`-complete, and there is a path as in the claim."*

The wheel supplied by the smaller-hub induction, applied inside the graph induced on
`A ∪ {x₀,x₁,x₂,z} ∪ Y₀` with the frame `(z,A)`.

links.rationale: Performs the localized appeal to the induction hypothesis behind claim (2): applying 19.2 with hub Y0 inside the graph induced on A together with x0, x1, x2, z (where the induced A1 is exactly A) yields the wheel witnessing that z is Y0-complete with rim inside x0, x1, z and A.

decls.name: delete_vertex
decls.docstring: Delete `z` from a hole whose only neighbours of `z` are the named ends.

links.rationale: Generic infrastructure lemma: deleting a hub-like vertex z from a hole whose only neighbours of z are two named ends leaves a path between those two ends.

decls.name: path_of_local_wheel
decls.docstring:
PAPER (19.2 (2)): *"there is a path ... containing at least two
`Y₀`-complete edges."* This is the path and parity step after locating the wheel.

links.rationale: Carries out the path-and-parity half of claim (2)'s conclusion: deletes z from the wheel's rim to get the required path with interior in A, and uses 2.3's even rim-edge-count together with the two complete edges lost at z to show at least two Y0-complete edges survive.

decls.name: compl_adj
decls.docstring: An induced injection is an induced injection for the complements too.

links.rationale: Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): an induced injection between G' and G is automatically an induced injection between their complements.

decls.name: isPathList_map
decls.docstring:
An induced injection is an induced injection for the complements too. -/
theorem compl_adj : ∀ a b : W, G'ᶜ.Adj a b ↔ Gᶜ.Adj (f a) (f b) := by
  intro a b
  simp only [SimpleGraph.compl_adj, ne_eq]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hne, h⟩
    exact ⟨fun he => hne (hf he), fun hc => h ((hadj a b).mpr hc)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, h⟩
    exact ⟨fun he => hne (by rw [he]), fun hc => h ((hadj a b).mp hc)⟩

/-! ### Lists

links.rationale: Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): a list is a path of G' iff its image under f is a path of G, combining injectivity of f for distinctness with the adjacency-reflection hypothesis for the edge condition.
Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): a list is a hole of G' iff its image under f is a hole of G, using that f both reflects and preserves adjacency along the list.
Bookkeeping infrastructure lemma: since f is injective, a list's head equals u iff the head of its image under f equals f(u).
Bookkeeping infrastructure lemma: since f is injective, a list's last element equals v iff the last element of its image under f equals f(v).
Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): a list is a path from u to v in G' iff its image under f is a path from f(u) to f(v) in G.

decls.name: vertexComplete_map
decls.docstring:
An induced injection is an induced injection for the complements too. -/
theorem compl_adj : ∀ a b : W, G'ᶜ.Adj a b ↔ Gᶜ.Adj (f a) (f b) := by
  intro a b
  simp only [SimpleGraph.compl_adj, ne_eq]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hne, h⟩
    exact ⟨fun he => hne (hf he), fun hc => h ((hadj a b).mpr hc)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, h⟩
    exact ⟨fun he => hne (by rw [he]), fun hc => h ((hadj a b).mp hc)⟩

/-! ### Lists -/

theorem isPathList_map (p : List W) : IsPathList G' p ↔ IsPathList G (p.map f) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hne, hnd, hp⟩
    refine ⟨by simpa using hne, hnd.map hf, ?_⟩
    intro i j hi hj
    simp only [List.getElem_map]
    rw [← hadj]
    exact hp i j (by simpa using hi) (by simpa using hj)
  · rintro ⟨hne, hnd, hp⟩
    refine ⟨by simpa using hne, hnd.of_map, ?_⟩
    intro i j hi hj
    have hh := hp i j (by simpa using hi) (by simpa using hj)
    simp only [List.getElem_map] at hh
    rw [← hadj] at hh
    exact hh

theorem isHoleList_map (c : List W) : IsHoleList G' c ↔ IsHoleList G (c.map f) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h4, hnd, hc⟩
    refine ⟨by simpa using h4, hnd.map hf, ?_⟩
    intro i j hi hj
    simp only [List.getElem_map, List.length_map]
    rw [← hadj]
    exact hc i j (by simpa using hi) (by simpa using hj)
  · rintro ⟨h4, hnd, hc⟩
    refine ⟨by simpa using h4, hnd.of_map, ?_⟩
    intro i j hi hj
    have hh := hc i j (by simpa using hi) (by simpa using hj)
    simp only [List.getElem_map, List.length_map] at hh
    rw [← hadj] at hh
    exact hh

theorem head?_map_iff (p : List W) (u : W) :
    p.head? = some u ↔ (p.map f).head? = some (f u) := by
  rw [List.head?_map]
  rcases p with _ | ⟨a, t⟩
  · simp
  · simp only [List.head?_cons, Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq]
    exact ⟨fun h => by rw [h], fun h => hf h⟩

theorem getLast?_map_iff (p : List W) (v : W) :
    p.getLast? = some v ↔ (p.map f).getLast? = some (f v) := by
  rw [List.getLast?_map]
  rcases h : p.getLast? with _ | a
  · simp
  · simp only [Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq]
    exact ⟨fun hh => by rw [hh], fun hh => hf hh⟩

theorem isPathFrom_map (p : List W) (u v : W) :
    IsPathFrom G' p u v ↔ IsPathFrom G (p.map f) (f u) (f v) :=
  and_congr (isPathList_map hf hadj p)
    (and_congr (head?_map_iff hf hadj p u) (getLast?_map_iff hf hadj p v))

/-! ### Completeness

links.rationale: Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): a vertex v is Y-complete in G' iff its image f(v) is f(Y)-complete in G.
Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): an edge is Y-complete in G' iff its image under f is f(Y)-complete in G.

decls.name: imgIso
decls.docstring: The induced injection restricts to an isomorphism from `G'|Y` onto `G|f(Y)`.

links.rationale: Bookkeeping infrastructure: restricts the induced injection f to a graph isomorphism from G' induced on Y onto G induced on the image f(Y).
Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): a set is connected in G' iff its image under the induced injection f is connected in G.
Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): a set is anticonnected in G' iff its image under the induced injection f is anticonnected in G.

decls.name: isWheel_map
decls.docstring:
The induced injection restricts to an isomorphism from `G'|Y` onto `G|f(Y)`. -/
noncomputable def imgIso (Y : Set W) : G'.induce Y ≃g G.induce (f '' Y) := by
  refine ⟨Equiv.ofBijective (fun w => ⟨f w.1, ⟨w.1, w.2, rfl⟩⟩) ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · rintro ⟨a, ha⟩ ⟨b, hb⟩ h
    exact Subtype.ext (hf (congrArg Subtype.val h))
  · rintro ⟨v, w, hw, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨⟨w, hw⟩, rfl⟩
  · intro a b
    show G.Adj (f a.1) (f b.1) ↔ G'.Adj a.1 b.1
    exact (hadj a.1 b.1).symm

theorem connectedSet_map (Y : Set W) :
    ConnectedSet G' Y ↔ ConnectedSet G (f '' Y) := by
  unfold ConnectedSet
  constructor
  · intro h u v
    obtain ⟨u', rfl⟩ := (imgIso hf hadj Y).surjective u
    obtain ⟨v', rfl⟩ := (imgIso hf hadj Y).surjective v
    exact ((h u' v').map (imgIso hf hadj Y).toHom)
  · intro h u v
    have := h ((imgIso hf hadj Y) u) ((imgIso hf hadj Y) v)
    have h2 := this.map (imgIso hf hadj Y).symm.toHom
    simpa using h2

theorem anticonnectedSet_map (Y : Set W) :
    AnticonnectedSet G' Y ↔ AnticonnectedSet G (f '' Y) :=
  connectedSet_map hf (compl_adj hf hadj) Y

/-! ### Wheels

links.rationale: Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): a list and hub together form a wheel in G' iff their images under f form a wheel in G, combining the hole, completeness and disjoint-edge transports proved earlier in this file.

decls.name: prefix_map_pull
decls.docstring: A block of a mapped list is a mapped block.

links.rationale: Bookkeeping infrastructure lemma: if T is a prefix of the image of a list M under f, then T is itself the image of a prefix of M.
Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): the IsSegment predicate (a maximal Y-complete sub-path of a wheel's rim) is preserved along an induced injection.
Bookkeeping transport lemma (not tied to a paper sentence): the IsOddWheel predicate (a wheel with an extra odd segment) is preserved along an induced injection.

decls.name: formPrism_map
decls.docstring:
A block of a mapped list is a mapped block. -/
theorem prefix_map_pull {M : List W} {T : List V} (h : T <+: M.map f) :
    ∃ T' : List W, T'.map f = T ∧ T' <+: M := by
  refine ⟨M.take T.length, ?_, List.take_prefix _ _⟩
  rw [List.map_take, ← List.prefix_iff_eq_take.mp h]

theorem isSegment_map {C : List W} {Y : Set W} {S : List W} (h : IsSegment G' C Y S) :
    IsSegment G (C.map f) (f '' Y) (S.map f) := by
  obtain ⟨⟨hpath, ⟨k, hk⟩, hmem⟩, hmax⟩ := h
  refine ⟨⟨(isPathList_map hf hadj S).mp hpath, ⟨k, ?_⟩, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · rw [← List.map_rotate]
    rcases hk with hk | hk
    · exact Or.inl (hk.map f)
    · exact Or.inr (by rw [← List.map_reverse]; exact hk.map f)
  · intro w hw
    obtain ⟨w', hw', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hw
    exact ⟨List.mem_map_of_mem (hmem w' hw').1,
      (vertexComplete_map hf hadj w' Y).mp (hmem w' hw').2⟩
  · intro T hT hTblock hTmem hST
    obtain ⟨k', hk'⟩ := hTblock
    -- pull `T` back along `f`
    obtain ⟨T', hT'eq, hT'pre⟩ : ∃ T' : List W, T'.map f = T ∧
        (T' <+: C.rotate k' ∨ T'.reverse <+: C.rotate k') := by
      rcases hk' with hk' | hk'
      · rw [← List.map_rotate] at hk'
        obtain ⟨T', h1, h2⟩ := prefix_map_pull hf hadj hk'
        exact ⟨T', h1, Or.inl h2⟩
      · rw [← List.map_rotate] at hk'
        obtain ⟨T', h1, h2⟩ := prefix_map_pull hf hadj hk'
        refine ⟨T'.reverse, by rw [List.map_reverse, h1, List.reverse_reverse], Or.inr ?_⟩
        rwa [List.reverse_reverse]
    subst hT'eq
    have hT'path : IsPathList G' T' := (isPathList_map hf hadj T').mpr hT
    have hT'mem : ∀ w ∈ T', w ∈ C ∧ VertexComplete G' w Y := by
      intro w hw
      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hTmem (f w) (List.mem_map_of_mem hw)
      obtain ⟨w', hw', hwe⟩ := List.mem_map.mp h1
      exact ⟨by rwa [hf hwe] at hw', (vertexComplete_map hf hadj w Y).mpr h2⟩
    have hST' : ∀ w ∈ S, w ∈ T' := by
      intro w hw
      obtain ⟨w', hw', hwe⟩ := List.mem_map.mp (hST (f w) (List.mem_map_of_mem hw))
      rwa [hf hwe] at hw'
    intro w hw
    obtain ⟨w', hw', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hw
    exact List.mem_map_of_mem (hmax T' hT'path ⟨k', hT'pre⟩ hT'mem hST' w' hw')

theorem isOddWheel_map {C : List W} {Y : Set W} (h : IsOddWheel G' C Y) :
    IsOddWheel G (C.map f) (f '' Y) := by
  obtain ⟨hw, S, hS, hodd⟩ := h
  exact ⟨isWheel_map hf hadj hw, S.map f, isSegment_map hf hadj hS,
    by simpa [pathLength] using hodd⟩

decls.name: uniform_induction
decls.docstring:
Strong induction on `|Y|`, uniformly over all graphs on types in one universe.

The `step` is the whole printed argument for one counterexample: it receives the
hypotheses of 19.2 together with both halves of the induction hypothesis — the theorem
for smaller hubs in the same graph, and `IHInduced`, the theorem for smaller hubs in
every induced subgraph.

links.rationale: Formalizes the opening move of the proof, choosing a counterexample Y of minimum size, as strong induction on |Y| run uniformly over every graph in a universe at once, so the induction hypothesis also covers smaller hubs inside induced subgraphs (needed by claim (2)).

decls.name: exists_noncut_outside
decls.docstring:
*"Since `F ≠ A`, there exists `f ∈ A \ F` such that `A \ {f}` is connected."*

Take a vertex `f` of `S \ F` at maximum distance (inside `S`) from a root `r ∈ F`.  A
vertex of `F` reaches `r` inside `F`, which avoids `f`; a vertex of `S \ F` reaches `r`
by descending the distance function, and every vertex on that descent is strictly closer
to `r` than `f` is, hence different from `f`.

decls.name: claim3
decls.docstring:
Claim **(3)** of the printed proof: *"There is no connected `F ⊆ A` containing
neighbours of all of `x₀, x₁, x₂, y` except `A` itself."*

links.rationale: Establishes claim (3): no connected proper subset F of A contains neighbours of all four of x0, x1, x2, y, since removing any non-cut vertex outside such an F from A would still meet every vertex of Y that needs a neighbour in A, contradicting the minimality of A.

decls.name: claim4
decls.docstring:
Claim **(4)** of the printed proof: *"If any vertex of `p₁,…,pₙ` is `Y ∪ {x₂}`-complete
then `z` is `Y`-complete; and if `z` is `Y`-complete then no edge of `x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁` is
`Y`-complete.  In particular, neither of `p₁, pₙ` is `Y ∪ {x₂}`-complete."*

links.rationale: Establishes the three conjuncts of claim (4) for the fixed path x0-p1-...-pn-x1 and hole C = z-x0-p1-...-pn-x1-z: a Y union x2-complete interior vertex forces z to be Y-complete, a Y-complete z forces no edge of the path to be Y-complete, and consequently neither end p1 nor pn of the interior is Y union x2-complete.

decls.name: x2_complete_of_z_not_complete
decls.docstring:
The part of claim (2) used in (4): "By (2), `x₂` is `Y₀`-complete and
nonadjacent to `y`." This follows directly from the induction hypothesis for `Y₀`.

links.rationale: Discharges the part of claim (4)'s proof that cites claim (2): if z is not Y-complete then, by (2), x2 must be Y0-complete and nonadjacent to y, obtained directly from the induction hypothesis applied to Y0.

decls.name: antipath_to_member
decls.docstring:
PAPER: "Let `Q` be an antipath between `z,y` with interior in `Y₀`."
Attach `z` to the anticonnected set `Y` and extract an induced path in the complement.

links.rationale: Constructs the antipath Q between z and y with interior in Y0 used in claim (4)'s proof, by attaching z to the anticonnected set Y and extracting an induced path of the complement graph.

decls.name: complete_of_interior_complete
decls.docstring:
PAPER: "Then `z-Q-y-x₂-R-pᵢ-z` is an antihole, meeting the hole `C`
in at least three vertices, contrary to 15.7."

links.rationale: Proves the first assertion of claim (4): if some interior vertex of the path is Y union x2-complete then z must be Y-complete, since otherwise the antihole z-Q-y-x2-R-pi-z would share at least three vertices with the hole C, contradicting 15.7.

decls.name: no_common
decls.docstring: No vertex of `A₁` is adjacent to both `x₀,x₁`.

links.rationale: Infrastructure lemma used throughout claim (4)'s setup: no vertex of A1 is adjacent to both x0 and x1, since such a vertex would be x0,x1-complete, contradicting the defining property of wheelSystemA.

decls.name: hub_outside
decls.docstring: The hub misses `A₁`, since its vertices are adjacent to both `x₀,x₁`.

links.rationale: Infrastructure lemma used throughout claim (4)'s setup: no vertex of the hub Y lies in A1, since every vertex of A1 fails to be adjacent to both x0 and x1 while every vertex of Y (by hypothesis) is adjacent to both.

decls.name: rim
decls.docstring:
PAPER: "let `C` be the hole `z-x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁-z`."
It has at least six vertices: a four-hole gives a common neighbour in `A₁`, and
its length is even because the graph is Berge.

links.rationale: Constructs the hole C = z-x0-p1-...-pn-x1-z fixed just before claim (4) and shows it has at least six vertices: a four-vertex hole would force a common A1-neighbour of x0 and x1, and its length must be even because the graph is Berge.

decls.name: wheel_of_complete_edge
decls.docstring:
PAPER: "The second is immediate, for otherwise `(C,Y)` satisfies the theorem."
A complete edge of `P` is disjoint from at least one of `zx₀,zx₁`.

links.rationale: Proves the second assertion of claim (4) by reductio: if z is Y-complete and some edge of the path x0-p1-...-pn-x1 is Y-complete, then C together with that edge and one of zx0, zx1 forms a wheel witnessing 19.2's conclusion for Y, contradicting the standing minimum-counterexample assumption.

decls.name: claim5
decls.docstring:
Claim **(5)** of the printed proof: *"With `p₁,…,pₙ` and `C` as in (4), if `x₀` is
adjacent to `x₂`, then `x₂` is nonadjacent to all of `p₂,…,pₙ`."*

links.rationale: Establishes claim (5): if x0 is adjacent to x2 then x2 has no neighbour among p2,...,pn, ruling out the last neighbour i = n via 15.7 (Thm192Claim5Last) and every other case via the odd-path parity contradiction of 13.6 (Thm192Claim5Cut).

decls.name: cut_contradiction
decls.docstring:
PAPER: "Since `i > 1`, `x₀-x₂-pᵢ-⋯-pₙ-x₁` is an odd path of length ≥ 5."
Applying 13.6 first with `Y ∪ {z}` and then with `Y` gives a complete edge of `C`,
contrary to claim (4).

links.rationale: Derives a contradiction for the case 1 < i < n of claim (5): since x0-x2-pi-...-pn-x1 is an odd path of length at least 5 whose ends are Y union z-complete and whose internal vertices are not, 13.6 forces z to be Y-complete and forces some edge of the path to be Y-complete, contradicting claim (4).

decls.name: last_not_adj
decls.docstring:
PAPER: "Suppose first that `i = n`. ... it can be completed via
`x₂-x₁-x₀-pₙ` to an antihole of length ≥ 5 containing `x₀,x₁,pₙ`, a contradiction."

links.rationale: Rules out the case i = n of claim (5)'s proof: since x0, x1, pn already lie on the hole C, no antihole of length at least 5 can contain them by 15.7, so x2 cannot be adjacent to pn (the antipath x2-x1-x0-pn would otherwise complete such an antihole).

decls.name: claim6
decls.docstring:
Claim **(6)** of the printed proof: *"If `x₀` is adjacent to `x₂`, then not both
`x₂, y` have neighbours in `{p₁,…,pₙ}`."*

links.rationale: Establishes claim (6): if x0 is adjacent to x2 then x2 and y cannot both have a neighbour among p1,...,pn, ruling out the adjacent-to-y case via a hat/leap contradiction from 2.10 and the nonadjacent case via the wheel-parity argument of 16.1.

decls.name: antihole_absurd
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (6)): "an antipath between `p₁` and `y` with interior in `Y₀`
can be extended to an antihole via `y-x₂-x₁-p₁`, and this antihole shares the
vertices `p₁,x₁,x₂` with the hole ... contrary to 15.7."
The same argument is used with `pᵢ` in claim (7).

links.rationale: General-purpose lemma: given an antipath from p to y with interior avoiding u,b and a hole C containing p,u,b of length >4, plus the four cross-adjacencies p-u, y-b, and the two nonadjacencies y-u, p-b, it derives a contradiction by exhibiting an antihole sharing three vertices with C (contrary to 15.7). It packages the antihole-construction pattern the paper repeats with different vertex names in claims (6) and (7), so it is not tied to a single sentence.
Wheel-system bookkeeping: z cannot lie in A1 (the set of vertices whose only wheel-system neighbours are x0, x1), since z is itself adjacent to both x0 and x1 by the wheel-system axioms.
Every vertex of a subset A of A1 is, by the minimal-A construction, not adjacent to both x0 and x1 simultaneously -- a structural property of the wheel system A1, not a numbered claim of the proof.

decls.name: path_facts
decls.docstring: The paper's hole `C = z-x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁-z` has length at least six.

links.rationale: Given a path P from x0 to x1 with interior in A and length at least 3, this records that z and x2 do not lie on P, that closing P through z yields a hole z::P, and that this hole has at least 5 edges (P has length >= 3 is upgraded to length >= 5, since length exactly 3 would put a vertex of A adjacent to both x0 and x1, contradicting no_pair_complete). This is the construction of the hole C = z-x0-p1-...-pn-x1-z used throughout claims (4)-(7), rather than a single quoted sentence.
No vertex of the interior path P (with interior contained in A) belongs to Y, since a member of Y on P would have to be adjacent to both x0 and x1, which no_pair_complete rules out.

decls.name: antipath_to_y
decls.docstring: Anticonnectedness supplies the antipath ending at the removed vertex `y`.

links.rationale: If u is outside an anticonnected set Y and not complete to Y minus a chosen vertex y, anticonnectedness of Y union {u} supplies an antipath from u to y with interior in Y \ {y}; this is the generic antipath-construction step the proof invokes repeatedly (e.g. around claim (1) and in several of claims (6)-(12)) whenever it needs 'an antipath ... with interior in Y0'.

decls.name: z_complete_of_noncomplete
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (2)): "From the minimality of `|Y|`, `z` is `Y₀`-complete
and therefore `Y`-complete." This uses only the conclusion for the smaller hub.

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (2)'s minimality step: applying the induction hypothesis to the smaller set Y0 = Y \ {y} (which is Y0-complete for z, since Y satisfies neither of the theorem's alternatives) and the neighbour of y in z gives that z is Y-complete.

decls.name: first_neighbour
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (6)): "From the hole `z-x₂-p₁-⋯-pⱼ-y-z` we deduce that `j`
is odd, and therefore `x₀-p₁-⋯-pⱼ-y-x₀` is not a hole, that is, `j = 1`."

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (6)'s two-hole parity step: if y has a neighbour among p1,...,pn and j is the least such index, evenness of the two holes z-x0-p1-...-pj-y-z and z-u-...-pj-y-z (via a rim vertex u adjacent to p1) forces j = 1, i.e. y is adjacent to p1.

decls.name: leap_misses_interior
decls.docstring:
At the cut edge `zx₀`, one vertex of a leap has no neighbour among `p₁,…,pₙ`.
This reads the six edges in the definition of a leap, as in the first part of (6).

links.rationale: At the cut edge z-x0 of the hole z::P, if b,a form a leap for that hole then b has no neighbour among the path's interior vertices p1,...,pn -- a direct unpacking of the definition of a leap (IsLeapForHole), used to exclude the leap alternative when every member of the hub S has an interior neighbour.

decls.name: hat_leap_absurd
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (6)): "Therefore `z,x₀` are the only `Y ∪ {x₂}`-complete
vertices in `C`, and by 2.10 there is a hat or a leap."
If every member of the hub has an interior neighbour, both outcomes are excluded.

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (6)'s dichotomy step: given that z, x0 are the only Y∪{x2}-complete vertices of the hole C = z::P and every member of the anticonnected hub S has a neighbour in the interior of P, theorem 2.10 gives a hat or a leap, and both alternatives are excluded (a hat's spoke vertex would meet the interior, and leap_misses_interior rules out the leap), yielding a contradiction.

decls.name: claim7
decls.docstring:
Claim **(7)** of the printed proof: *"Not both `x₂, y` have neighbours in
`{p₁,…,pₙ}`."*

links.rationale: The top-level formalization of claim (7) itself -- 'Not both x2, y have neighbours in {p1,...,pn}' -- assembled from claim (6) applied at x0 (via Thm192Claim6.claim6), its x0<->x1 symmetric transport (Thm192Claim7Reduction), and the two x2-adjacent-to-neither-end cases (Thm192Claim7Gap).

decls.name: isPathFrom_cons
decls.docstring:
Attach a vertex `s` at the front of a path `p` from `u` to `v`, when `s` is
adjacent to `u` and to no other vertex of `p`.

links.rationale: Prepends a vertex s to a path p from u to v, given that s is adjacent to u and to no other vertex of p; used whenever the paper attaches one more vertex to the front of a displayed path such as y1-x2-pi-...-pn-y2.

decls.name: isPathFrom_snoc
decls.docstring:
Attach a vertex `t` at the end of a path `p` from `u` to `v`, when `t` is
adjacent to `v` and to no other vertex of `p`.

links.rationale: Appends a vertex t to the end of a path p from u to v, given that t is adjacent to v and to no other vertex of p; the mirror operation of isPathFrom_cons, used to build paths such as pi-...-pn-x1-z.

decls.name: isPathFrom_drop
decls.docstring: The tail `pᵢ-⋯-pₙ` of a path.

links.rationale: The suffix pi-...-pn-x1 obtained by dropping the first i entries of a path is itself a path -- generic list-slicing infrastructure for extracting the tail segments the proof repeatedly names.

decls.name: mem_drop_index
decls.docstring: Every vertex of `P.drop i` is `P[k]` for some `k ≥ i`.

links.rationale: Every vertex of the suffix P.drop i is some entry P[k] with k >= i -- indexing infrastructure used to relate positions on a sliced path back to positions on the original one.

decls.name: anticonnected_pair
decls.docstring: A pair of nonadjacent vertices is anticonnected.

links.rationale: A pair of distinct nonadjacent vertices is trivially an anticonnected set of size 2 (its complement graph is a single edge, hence connected).

decls.name: getElem_idx_congr
decls.docstring: Two equal indices give the same entry.

links.rationale: Trivial rewriting lemma: two proofs that the same index lies in range give the same list entry.

decls.name: head?_rotate
decls.docstring: The head of a rotation, in `getElem?` form.

links.rationale: Computes the head of a list rotation in terms of `getElem?` on the original list, the counterpart of `getLast?_rotate` used when reading off the start of a rotated rim.

decls.name: getLast?_rotate
decls.docstring: The last entry of a rotation, in `getElem?` form.

links.rationale: Computes the last entry of a list rotation in terms of `getElem?` on the original list, used to read off endpoints of the rim after rotating a hole to start at a chosen vertex.

decls.name: rotate_index
decls.docstring: A rotation of a duplicate-free list is determined by its first entry.

links.rationale: A rotation of a duplicate-free list is determined by which entry becomes its new head -- used to identify two differently-described rotations of the same rim as equal.

decls.name: exists_cycEdge_of_cycCount_lt
decls.docstring: A strict increase of the running count of `Y`-complete rim edges exhibits one.

links.rationale: If the running count of Y-complete rim edges strictly increases between positions i and j of a hole, some specific edge in that range is Y-complete -- the existence witness underlying every 'there are an odd (or nonzero) number of Y-complete edges' step of claim (7).

decls.name: exists_nonneighbour_of_anticonnected
decls.docstring:
A vertex of an anticonnected set with at least two elements has a nonneighbour in
the set: otherwise it would be isolated in the complement, which is connected.

links.rationale: Any vertex of an anticonnected set with at least two elements has a nonneighbour within the set, since otherwise it would be an isolated (hence disconnecting) vertex of the connected complement graph on that set.

decls.name: getLast?_take
decls.docstring: The last vertex of an initial stretch.

links.rationale: The last vertex of an initial segment `l.take k` is the entry at index k-1 of the original list.

decls.name: ncard_pathEdges
decls.docstring:
For a path, the *set of `Y`-complete edges* and the *set of positions carrying a
`Y`-complete edge* have the same size: the map `i ↦ {Qᵢ, Qᵢ₊₁}` is a bijection between
them.  This is the path analogue of `WheelParity.ncard_yEdges_eq_cycCount`, and it is what
lets 18.2 (which counts edges) feed the rim bookkeeping of §16 (which counts positions).

links.rationale: For a path, the set of Y-complete edges and the set of positions carrying a Y-complete edge have equal cardinality, since the map from position i to the edge {Q_i, Q_{i+1}} is a bijection between them; this is the path analogue of the rim identity used to let 18.2's edge-count feed the position-count bookkeeping of the wheel-parity arguments in section 16.

decls.name: even_cycCount_of_three_complete
decls.docstring:
2.3, in the form the parity arguments of §19 use it: a hole carrying three
distinct `Y`-complete vertices has an even number of `Y`-complete edges.

links.rationale: Specializes theorem 2.3 to the form the parity arguments of section 19 actually use: if a hole disjoint from an anticonnected Y carries three pairwise-distinct Y-complete rim vertices, the count of Y-complete rim edges is even (the alternative outcome of 2.3, exactly two Y-complete vertices on the hole, is excluded by having three).

decls.name: noncomplete_endpoint_nonadjacent_case
decls.docstring:
PAPER (printed pp. 119–120, claim (7)), the case beginning:
*"Suppose first that `x₂` is not `Y₀`-complete. By (2), `z` is `Y`-complete and
`(C,Y₀)` is a wheel."*  The conclusion is the contradiction at the end of that case,
where the three antipaths form a long prism.

links.rationale: Formalizes the whole 'x2 not Y0-complete' branch of claim (7) (once x2 is known nonadjacent to both x0, x1): it derives the right-endpoint facts from the parity/hat-or-leap chain, repeats the argument after reversing the path to get the left-endpoint facts, and combines them into the long-prism contradiction that closes this case.

decls.name: complete_endpoint_nonadjacent_case
decls.docstring:
PAPER (printed p. 120, claim (7)), the case beginning:
*"We therefore assume that `x₂` is `Y₀`-complete, and consequently nonadjacent to `y`."*
The conclusion is the final contradiction from 17.1 in the complement.

links.rationale: Formalizes the whole 'x2 is Y0-complete' branch of claim (7): it derives the right-endpoint facts from the 17.1/15.7 reflection chain, repeats the argument after reversing the path for the left endpoint, and combines the two into the final 17.1 contradiction that closes this case.

decls.name: unique_neighbours_adjacent
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (7)): "`x₀,x₁,x₂` all have unique neighbours in it ... and
these three vertices do not form a triangle ... contrary to 17.1."
Three distinct unique neighbours of a caught triangle must be pairwise adjacent.

links.rationale: General consequence of 17.1: if a caught triangle {a,b,c} has three pairwise-distinct unique neighbours d,e,f respectively in the catching set, then d and f must be adjacent -- this is what forces the contradiction in claim (7)'s endgame, where the paper observes the analogous three unique neighbours pn, p1, y do NOT form a triangle.

decls.name: endpoint_facts
decls.docstring: The four end-to-interior incidences of `x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁`.

links.rationale: For a path a-...-b of length at least 5, records the four end-to-second-vertex incidences (each end is adjacent to its neighbour but not to the far second-from-end vertex) and that the two second-from-end vertices are distinct -- generic path bookkeeping feeding both endgame contradictions of claim (7).

decls.name: complete_endpoints_absurd
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (7)): "So in [the complement], the connected set
`Y ∪ {p₁,pₙ}` catches the triangle `{x₀,x₁,x₂}` ... contrary to 17.1."

links.rationale: Formalizes the final contradiction of claim (7)'s x2-Y0-complete case: with p1, pn adjacent to both x2 and y but not Y-complete, the complement's connected set Y∪{p1,pn} catches the triangle {x0,x1,x2} with unique neighbours pn, p1, y respectively, and 17.1's unique-neighbour lemma then forces q (= p1's mate) adjacent to y, contradicting that y is not adjacent to p1.

decls.name: noncomplete_endpoints_absurd
decls.docstring:
The two endpoint conclusions in the first case of (7) give the three
antipaths named in the paper's long-prism contradiction.

links.rationale: Formalizes the final contradiction of claim (7)'s x2-not-Y0-complete case: given the endpoint facts (p1, pn adjacent to x2 but not to y, and Y0-complete) and an antipath Q between x2 and y with interior in Y0, it assembles the three antipaths p1-x1, pn-x0 and y-Q-x2 into the long prism forbidden by G ∈ F7.

decls.name: last_neighbour
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (7)): "Choose `i` with `1 ≤ i ≤ n` maximum such that `x₂`
is adjacent to `pᵢ`."

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (7)'s choice of the last interior neighbour of x2: given that x2 has some neighbour among the interior vertices p1,...,pn and is nonadjacent to x1, there is a greatest index i with x2 adjacent to pi, and it is the unique such index at or after itself.

decls.name: complete_right_endpoint
decls.docstring:
After the parity step has shown that `y` meets `pᵢ`, the paper proves:
"Suppose that `i < n`. If `pᵢ` is not `Y`-complete then an antipath ... can be
extended ... contrary to 15.7. So `pᵢ` is `Y`-complete, and therefore so is `z`,
by (4). ... So `i = n`."

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (7)'s i = n reduction in the x2-Y0-complete case: assuming i < n forces pi (hence z, via claim (4)) to be Y-complete, which makes (C1, Y) an odd wheel and contradicts G ∈ F7, so i = n and pn is adjacent to both x2 and y.

decls.name: noncomplete_right_endpoint
decls.docstring:
The right endpoint conclusions in the noncomplete case, including the
application of (4) that excludes its edge to `y`.

links.rationale: Assembles the x2-not-Y0-complete case's right-endpoint conclusions (pn adjacent to x2, Y0-complete, nonadjacent to y, and y adjacent to x2) by combining the parity/hat-or-leap chain of noncomplete_short_cut with claim (4)'s exclusion of a Y-complete edge at that position; a bookkeeping composition rather than an independent paper sentence.
The second-to-last entry of the reversed path P.reverse equals the second entry of P -- an index identity used to transport right-endpoint facts to left-endpoint facts under path reversal.
Transports the hypothesis 'no rim edge of P is Y-complete' to the reversed path P.reverse -- bookkeeping needed to reapply the right-endpoint argument at the left endpoint by symmetry.

decls.name: noncomplete_short_cut_of_contact
decls.docstring:
LABELLED GAP. PAPER (printed p. 120, claim (7), first case):
"By 16.1, `pᵢ,z` have the same wheel-parity, and so there are an odd number of
`Y₀`-complete edges in `pᵢ-⋯-pₙ-x₁`. ... By 2.10, `Y` contains a leap ...
contrary to 13.6. So `C₁` has length 4, that is, `i = n`, and `pₙ` is
`Y₀`-complete. ... `y` is adjacent to `x₂`."
The reflection argument has already supplied `hycontact`. The remaining steps
are the 16.1 parity calculation and the 2.10/13.6 exclusion of a longer cut.

links.rationale: Formalizes the 2.10/13.6 exclusion step of claim (7)'s x2-not-Y0-complete case: given that some member of Y meets x2,pi,...,pn (hycontact), the odd rim-edge count from the 16.1 parity calculation forces every member of Y to meet that arc, so C1 = z-x2-pi-...-pn-x1-z admits no hat, and 2.10/13.6 exclude a leap unless C1 has length exactly 4, i.e. i = n with pn Y0-complete and y adjacent to x2. Confidence capped below its primitive Thm192Claim7ShortCut.cut_length_four: this lemma is a thin wrapper supplying the hycontact disjunction before handing off to that primitive, which does the actual 16.1/2.10/13.6 case-split, so the wrapper should not be rated equal to the machinery it calls.

decls.name: noncomplete_short_cut
decls.docstring:
PAPER (printed p. 120, claim (7), first case):
"So `C₁` has length 4, that is, `i = n`, and `pₙ` is `Y₀`-complete.
By (4) it follows that `pₙ` is nonadjacent to `y`, and therefore `y` is adjacent
to `x₂` (since we already showed that `y` is adjacent to one of `x₂,pᵢ,…,pₙ`)."
This is the one-sided endpoint reduction, before the symmetry and long prism.
The reflection exclusion is proved in `right_contact`; the parity calculation
and exclusion of a longer cut remain in `noncomplete_short_cut_of_contact`.

links.rationale: Thin composition wrapper: supplies the hycontact disjunction (y adjacent to x2 or to pn) from the 17.1 reflection argument of right_contact, then hands it to noncomplete_short_cut_of_contact, which carries out the actual 16.1/2.10/13.6 case-split. No independent paper sentence of its own.

decls.name: complete_separated_contact
decls.docstring:
LABELLED GAP. PAPER (printed p. 120, claim (7)):
"Suppose `j ≠ i`. Then the path `x₂-pᵢ-⋯-pⱼ-y` is even and has length at
least 4. By 13.7 ... By 18.2 ... `pⱼ,pₙ` are both not `Y₀`-complete, and so
`(C₁,Y₀)` is an odd wheel, contrary to `G ∈ F₇`."
The last neighbour `i` of `x₂` and first neighbour `j` of `y` after it are
already chosen. Only the separated-index parity contradiction remains here.

links.rationale: Local re-export: forwards directly to Thm192Claim7Separated.separated_contact, which formalizes the paper's j != i sub-case of claim (7)'s x2-Y0-complete branch. Exists only so this module's other lemmas can call it under the local API without importing across the split.

decls.name: complete_last_neighbour_contact
decls.docstring:
PAPER (printed p. 120, claim (7), second case):
"Since `y` is adjacent to `pₙ`, we may choose `j` with `i ≤ j ≤ n` minimum such
that `y` is adjacent to `pⱼ`. ... This proves that `j = i`, that is, `y` is
adjacent to `pᵢ`."
The final neighbour of `y` is supplied by 17.1, as proved in `right_contact`.
We choose `j` and reduce to the separately labelled parity contradiction.
The following antihole argument proving `i = n` and the final application of
17.1 are proved separately.

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (7)'s choice of j and its reduction to j = i in the x2-Y0-complete case: 17.1 supplies y adjacent to pn, the least j >= i with y adjacent to pj is chosen, and the j != i alternative is excluded by delegating to complete_separated_contact, leaving y adjacent to pi.

decls.name: prism_absurd
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (7)): "the three antipaths `p₁-x₁`, `pₙ-x₀` and `y-Q-x₂`
form a long prism in [the complement] with triangles `{p₁,pₙ,y}` and
`{x₁,x₀,x₂}`, a contradiction."

links.rationale: General long-prism contradiction lemma: given two disjoint edges p-q and b-a in the complement forming triangles with a and y resp. b and u, plus an antipath Q from y to u with interior complete to both p,q,a,b, it derives False by exhibiting the forbidden long prism -- the reusable machinery behind the specific instance claim (7) names with p1,pn,x0,x1,x2,y,Q.

decls.name: no_reflection
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (7)): "By 15.7, it contains no reflection of the triangle,
since as before that would give an antihole of length 6 with three vertices in `C`."
Here `a,b` lie on `C`, and the unique neighbour `q` of `b` in the catching set
also lies on `C`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the reflection-exclusion step reused in both cases of claim (7): if a and b lie on the hole C (length > 4) and q is b's unique neighbour in a catching set F, a reflection of the triangle {a,b,y} into F would produce an antihole sharing three vertices with C, contradicting 15.7.

decls.name: catches_forces_contact
decls.docstring:
With unique neighbours `u,q` for the first two triangle vertices, and no
reflection, 17.1 forces the third triangle vertex to see `u` or `q`.

links.rationale: Generic corollary of 17.1: if a catching set has unique neighbours u for a and q for b, and contains no reflection of the triangle {a,b,y}, then 17.1's second alternative (a vertex with two neighbours in the triangle) forces y adjacent to u or to q.

decls.name: right_contact
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (7)): "Now `{x₂,p₁,…,pₙ}` is connected and catches the
triangle `{z,x₁,y}`. ... So by 17.1 ... `y` is adjacent to `pₙ`."
Before assuming `x₂y` is a nonedge, the conclusion allows that edge as well.

links.rationale: Formalizes the shared catching argument of claim (7): the connected set {x2}∪interior(P) catches the triangle {z,x1,y}, its only neighbour of z is x2 and of x1 is pn, no_reflection excludes a reflection, so 17.1 forces y adjacent to x2 or to pn -- the common lemma both the x2-not-Y0-complete and x2-Y0-complete cases specialize.

If no consecutive pair of a path P is a Y-complete edge, then in fact no pair of vertices of P at all forms a Y-complete edge, since any edge of P joins consecutive positions -- generic path infrastructure used to rule out Y-complete edges away from the rim.

decls.name: only_complete_of_unique_edge
decls.docstring:
PAPER (2.3, used in (7)): if a hole has just one `Y`-complete edge, the ends
of that edge are its only `Y`-complete vertices.

links.rationale: Corollary of theorem 2.3: if a hole disjoint from an anticonnected Y has exactly one Y-complete edge {a,b}, then a and b are its only Y-complete vertices (the alternative outcome of 2.3, an even nonzero count, is excluded by uniqueness of the edge).

decls.name: cut_only_complete
decls.docstring:
PAPER (claim (7)): "Consequently `zx₁` is the unique `Y`-complete edge of
the hole `z-x₂-pᵢ-⋯-pₙ-x₁-z`."

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (7)'s uniqueness step: on the shortened hole C1 = z-x2-pi-...-pn-x1-z, since no rim edge of the original path is Y-complete and z is only adjacent (on C1) to x1, the edge z-x1 is C1's unique Y-complete edge, so by only_complete_of_unique_edge z and x1 are its only Y-complete vertices.

decls.name: rotate_arc
decls.docstring: The arc `pᵢ-⋯-pₙ-x₁-z` of the rim `C = z-x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁-z`, as a list.

decls.name: same_parity
decls.docstring: PAPER: *"By 16.1, `pᵢ, z` have the same wheel-parity."*

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (7)'s appeal to 16.1: since i is the last interior neighbour of x2 and x2 is nonadjacent to x1, pi and z are the only neighbours of x2 on the arc pi-...-pn-x1-z, and are themselves nonadjacent, so 16.1's first assertion gives pi and z the same wheel-parity on the wheel (z::P, Y0). (Earlier data had this quote mis-verified at pdf_page 98, a false positive on generic lemma-citation boilerplate; the corrected verbatim quote lands on page 122.)

decls.name: exists_complete_after
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"…and so there are an odd number of `Y₀`-complete edges in `pᵢ-⋯-pₙ-x₁`."*
Only the consequence that the count is nonzero is recorded: some `pₖ` with `i ≤ k ≤ n`
is `Y₀`-complete.

links.rationale: Records only the consequence claim (7) actually uses from the odd rim-edge count established by 16.1/same_parity: some vertex pk with i <= k <= n is Y0-complete. (Earlier data had this quote mis-verified at pdf_page 110, a false positive on generic lemma-citation boilerplate; the corrected verbatim quote lands on page 122, matching claim (7)'s printed location.)

decls.name: adj_z_x
decls.docstring: Wheel-system bookkeeping used when closing the path through `z`.

decls.name: z_notMem_path
decls.docstring:
The three wheel-system vertices and `z` lie outside `A₁`, so `z` does not occur on
an `x₀`–`x₁` path whose interior is in a subset of `A₁`.

decls.name: hole_zP
decls.docstring: The hole obtained by closing such a path through `z`.

decls.name: claim6_at_x1
decls.docstring:
The `x₀ ↔ x₁` transport of claim (6).  It is the formal version of the first
sentence of claim (7): *"and similarly nonadjacent to `x₁`"*.

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (7)'s 'and similarly nonadjacent to x1' clause: applying claim (6) to the x0<->x1-swapped, path-reversed data (via the sw symmetry transport) and translating the conclusion back gives that x2 and y cannot both have interior neighbours when x2 is adjacent to x1.

decls.name: separated_contact
decls.docstring: PAPER (claim (7)): the whole displayed paragraph above.

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (7)'s j != i sub-case in full: from the even path x2-pi-...-pj-y of length >= 4, theorem 13.7 makes Y0 ∪ {z} non-anticonnected so z is Y-complete; claim (4), 2.2 and 18.2 then combine to give pj, pn opposite wheel-parity on (C1, Y0), making it an odd wheel and contradicting G ∈ F7.

decls.name: cut_getElem
decls.docstring: The entries of the shortened rim `C₁ = z-x₂-pᵢ-⋯-pₙ-x₁` beyond its first two.

links.rationale: Reindexing identity for the shortened rim C1 = z-x2-pi-...-pn-x1: its entry at position m-i+2 equals P's entry at position m -- bookkeeping for translating between positions on P and positions on C1.

decls.name: cut_length_four
decls.docstring: PAPER (claim (7)): *"So `C₁` has length 4, that is, `i = n`."*

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (7)'s hat-or-leap exclusion for the shortened hole C1: with every member of Y meeting x2,pi,...,pn, there is no hat for C1, and a leap of length >= 5 with {x0,x1}-complete ends and non-complete interior would contradict 13.6, so C1 must have length exactly 4, i.e. i = n.

decls.name: claim8
decls.docstring:
Claim **(8)** of the printed proof: *"If `x₂` is nonadjacent to `y` then it is
nonadjacent to both `x₀, x₁`."*

links.rationale: The top-level formalization of claim (8) itself -- 'If x2 is nonadjacent to y then it is nonadjacent to both x0, x1' -- proved for the x0-adjacency case by Thm192Claim8Main.half and for the x1-adjacency case by the same lemma transported through the x0<->x1 symmetry.

decls.name: exists_nonadj_of_anticonnected
decls.docstring: In an anticonnected set, a vertex with a companion has a nonneighbour in the set.

links.rationale: Generic fact feeding the antipath extraction used at every "let Q be an antipath with interior in Y0" step of the printed proof: an anticonnected set with two distinct members gives each a nonneighbour in the set.

decls.name: leap_pair
decls.docstring: The extractor for `IsLeapForHole`, returning also the two adjacencies.

links.rationale: Extracts the two adjacencies of a leap for a hole, in the form claim (8) needs to build the path y1-x2-f1-...-fk-y2 from the leap found via 2.10.

decls.name: z_notMem
decls.docstring: `z ∉ A` whenever `A ⊆ A₁`: `z` is `{x₀,x₁}`-complete.

links.rationale: Bookkeeping fact: z is not in A whenever A is a subset of A1, since z is {x0, x1}-complete but A1's vertices are not.

decls.name: no_X1_complete
decls.docstring: No vertex of `A ⊆ A₁` is `{x₀,x₁}`-complete.

links.rationale: Bookkeeping fact: no vertex of A (a subset of A1) is {x0, x1}-complete, by the definition of the wheel system's A1.

decls.name: z_notMem_path
decls.docstring: `z ∉ P` for any `x₀`--`x₁` path with interior in `A`.

links.rationale: Bookkeeping fact: z does not lie on any x0-x1 path whose interior lies in A.

decls.name: hole_zP
decls.docstring: *"let `C` be the hole `z-x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁-z`"*.

links.rationale: Builds the hole C = z-x0-p1-...-pn-x1-z from an x0-x1 path with interior in A, as set up before claim (4) and reused through claim (8).

decls.name: P_length_ge_five
decls.docstring: The rim has at least six vertices, so `P` has at least five.

links.rationale: Since the wheel's rim has at least six vertices, the path P (the rim minus z, x0, x1) has at least five vertices; used throughout claims (4)-(12) of 19.2's proof.

decls.name: choiceOfPath
decls.docstring:
*"Let us choose `p₁,…,pₙ` and `C` such that either `x₂` is `Y₀`-complete or `(C,Y₀)`
is a wheel (this is possible by (2))."* — for a path `P` chosen by the caller, provided
`A` is contained in `P`.  Claim (2)'s `Y₀`-complete edge has both ends in `{x₀,x₁} ∪ A`,
hence in `P`, and its two `Y₀`-complete interior vertices lie in `A`, hence in the interior
of `P`.

links.rationale: Instantiates the proof's choice of the x0-x1 path p1,...,pn and hole C so that either x2 is Y0-complete or (C, Y0) is a wheel, for a caller-supplied path contained in A.

decls.name: endgame
decls.docstring: The closing contradiction of claim (8).

links.rationale: Formalizes the closing contradiction of claim (8): the leap y1-x2-f1-...-fk-y2 for hole C1 gives a path whose ends are {x0,x1}-complete and interior is not, contradicting 13.6.

decls.name: half
decls.docstring: *"`x₂` is nonadjacent to `y` and adjacent to `x₀`"* is impossible.

links.rationale: Formalizes the x0 half of claim (8)'s proof by contradiction: assuming x2 is nonadjacent to y but adjacent to x0 leads to a contradiction (the x1 case follows by symmetry).

decls.name: path_structure
decls.docstring:
*"`A` is the vertex set of a path `f₁-⋯-f_k`, where `f₁` is adjacent to `x₀,x₂`, and
`f_k` to `x₁,y`."*

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (8)'s deduction from claim (3) that A is the vertex set of a path f1-...-fk with f1 adjacent to x0, x2 and fk adjacent to x1, y.

decls.name: reflection_partner
decls.docstring:
Every vertex of the first triangle of a reflection has a matched partner in the second,
and no other vertex of the first triangle is adjacent to that partner.

decls.name: two_partners
decls.docstring:
The two partners of a reflection: `z`'s partner is the attached vertex `s`, and the
partner of a second triangle vertex `p` lies in `A` and is adjacent to `s`.

decls.name: catch_x0x2
decls.docstring:
**Claim (8), first application of 17.1.**  *"Now `A ∪ {x₁}` catches the triangle
`{z,x₀,x₂}`; it contains no reflection of this triangle, since `x₀,x₁` have no common
neighbour in `A`; … So by 17.1 it follows that there is a vertex in `A` adjacent to both
`x₀,x₂`."*

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (8)'s first application of 17.1: A union {x1} catches the triangle {z, x0, x2} with no reflection, so there is a vertex in A adjacent to both x0, x2.

decls.name: catch_x1y
decls.docstring:
**Claim (8), second application of 17.1.**  *"Also, `A ∪ x₂` catches the triangle
`{z,x₁,y}`.  Suppose that `A ∪ {x₂}` contains a reflection of this triangle; then there
exists `f ∈ A` adjacent to `x₁,x₂` and not to `y`.  Since `f ∈ A` it follows that `f` is
nonadjacent to `x₀`; but then `f-x₂-x₀-y-x₁-f` is an odd hole, a contradiction.  Hence by
17.1 there is a vertex in `A` adjacent to both `x₁,y`."*

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (8)'s second application of 17.1: A union {x2} catches the triangle {z, x1, y}, and a reflection would give an odd hole f-x2-x0-y-x1-f, so there is a vertex in A adjacent to both x1, y.

decls.name: anticonnected_pair
decls.docstring: Two nonadjacent vertices form an anticonnected pair.

links.rationale: Generic fact: two nonadjacent vertices form an anticonnected pair.

decls.name: tail_eq
decls.docstring: Deleting the first vertex of a path leaves the stretch from its second vertex on.

links.rationale: Generic list fact: deleting the first vertex of a path leaves the stretch from its second vertex on.

decls.name: init_eq
decls.docstring: Deleting the last vertex of a path leaves the stretch up to its penultimate vertex.

links.rationale: Generic list fact: deleting the last vertex of a path leaves the stretch up to its penultimate vertex.

decls.name: connected_slice
decls.docstring:
The vertex set of a stretch of a path is connected (also when the stretch is a single
vertex).

links.rationale: Generic list fact: the vertex set of any stretch of a path is connected, including a single-vertex stretch.

decls.name: unique_nbs
decls.docstring:
The bookkeeping shared by every step of claim (8): `A` misses `z`, `x₀`, `x₁`, `x₂`, `y`,
and contains no `{x₀,x₁}`-complete vertex.

links.rationale: Bookkeeping shared by every step of claim (8)'s proof: A avoids z, x0, x1, x2, y and contains no {x0, x1}-complete vertex.

decls.name: isPathList_five
decls.docstring: A five-element list with exactly its four consecutive edges is an induced path.

links.rationale: Generic list fact: a five-element list with exactly its four consecutive edges present, and no others, forms an induced path.

decls.name: zComplete
decls.docstring: *"This proves that `z` is `Y`-complete."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the paragraph of claim (8)'s proof concluding that z is Y-complete, from the two antihole contradictions with 15.7 depending on whether f1 is Y0-complete.

decls.name: isPathList_five
decls.docstring: A five-element list with exactly its four consecutive edges is an induced path.

decls.name: reflection_partner
decls.docstring:
Every vertex of the first triangle has its matched vertex in a reflection, and it has
no other neighbour in the reflected triangle.

decls.name: endpoint_reflection
decls.docstring:
The application of 17.1 used twice in claim (9).  The vertices `x₂` and `f` are the
partners of `z` and `y`, so the third partner lies in `A \ {f}` and is adjacent to both.

decls.name: claim9
decls.docstring:
Claim **(9)** of the printed proof: *"There is no connected `F ⊆ A` containing
neighbours of all of `x₀, x₁, x₂` except `A` itself."*

links.rationale: The Lean statement of claim (9) of 19.2's proof: no connected proper subset F of A contains neighbours of all of x0, x1, x2 (assembled from the sub-lemmas proving both cases of x2's adjacency to y).

decls.name: minimalityWitness
decls.docstring:
PAPER (19.2, claim (9), printed p. 121):

*"Choose `f ∈ A \ F` such that `A \ {f}` is connected. From the minimality of `A`,
there exists `y₀ ∈ Y` nonadjacent to `x₂` with no neighbour in `A \ {f}`."*

The conclusion packages those two consecutive sentences.  The hypotheses `hyY` and `h2y`
were added by the repair described in the module header.

links.rationale: Formalizes the opening step of claim (9)'s proof: from A's minimality, choosing f in A \ F with A \ {f} connected produces a y0 in Y, nonadjacent to x2, with no neighbour in A \ {f}.

decls.name: minimalityWitness
decls.docstring:
*"Choose `f ∈ A \ F` such that `A \ {f}` is connected.  From the minimality of `A`, …"* —
in the form that follows from the minimality of a `GoodA` set.

links.rationale: Repaired form of the same claim (9) opening step (Thm192Claim9MinimalityWitness), restated so it follows from the minimality of a GoodA set rather than an ad hoc minimality hypothesis.
