decls.docstring: A five-element list with exactly its four consecutive edges is an induced path.

decls.name: reflection_partner
decls.docstring:
Every vertex of the first triangle has its matched vertex in a reflection, and it has
no other neighbour in the reflected triangle.

decls.name: endpoint_reflection
decls.docstring:
The application of 17.1 used twice in claim (9).  The vertices `x₂` and `f` are the
partners of `z` and `y`, so the third partner lies in `A \ {f}` and is adjacent to both.

decls.name: claim9_of_not_x2_adj_y
decls.docstring:
Claim **(9)** of the printed proof: *"There is no connected `F ⊆ A` containing
neighbours of all of `x₀, x₁, x₂` except `A` itself."*

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (9)'s proof in the y0 = y (y not adjacent to x2) branch: the x2-not-adjacent-to-f case contradicts 17.3 directly, and the x2-adjacent-to-f case is handled via 17.1 and the reflection argument that closes claim (9).

decls.name: minimalHubContradiction
decls.docstring:
The configuration of claim (9) in which `f` is the unique neighbour of `y` in `A`,
`x₂` is adjacent to `y`, and the hub cannot be shrunk.

PAPER (19.2, claim (9), printed p. 121): *"… and therefore `f` is the unique neighbour of
`y₀` in `A`.  If `y₀ ∈ Y₀`, then … a contradiction.  So `y₀ = y`, and therefore `y` is not
adjacent to `x₂`."*

`hminhub` says that no proper subset of `Y` still contains `y`, is still anticonnected and
still has a vertex nonadjacent to `x₂`.  Two consequences pin the configuration down:

* `x₂` has exactly one nonneighbour `w` in `Y`, and `Y \ {w}` is anticonnected.  Indeed,
  `Y` is anticonnected with at least two elements (it contains `y`, adjacent to `x₂`, and a
  nonneighbour of `x₂`), so two of its vertices `u` have `Y \ {u}` anticonnected
  (`NonCutVertices.exists_two_nonanticut`); for such a `u` other than `y`, `hminhub`
  applied to `Y \ {u}` says that `u` is the *only* nonneighbour of `x₂` in `Y`.  At most
  one of the two can be `y`, so at least one of them is that unique nonneighbour `w`.
* So `w` is a vertex of the hub which the printed claim (1) could have chosen instead of
  `y`: it lies in `Y`, is adjacent to `z`, has `Y \ {w}` anticonnected, and is nonadjacent
  to `x₂`.

Running the printed proof of 19.2 for `w` and a cardinality-minimal `GoodA` set for it —
which is legitimate because every claim of the printed proof is available for `w`, claim
(9) included (`Thm192Claim9NotAdjX2`, the branch `¬ G.Adj (x 2) w`) — reaches claim (11)
and its first sentence *"`z` is not `Y₀`-complete"*, here *"`z` is not
`Y \ {w}`-complete"* (`Thm192Claim9YAdjX2Rerun.z_not_Y0_complete`).  But `x₂` is adjacent
to `y`, so claim (2) gives its second alternative, and in particular `z` **is**
`Y`-complete, hence `Y \ {w}`-complete.  That is the contradiction.

links.rationale: The configuration of claim (9), x2-adjacent-to-y branch, in which f is the unique neighbour of y in A and the hub Y cannot be shrunk to a smaller anticonnected set still containing y with a nonneighbour of x2.

decls.name: uniqueNeighbourContradiction
decls.docstring:
The configuration in which `f` is the unique neighbour of `y` in `A` and `x₂` is
adjacent to `y`.

PAPER (19.2, claim (9), printed p. 121): *"… and therefore `f` is the unique neighbour of
`y₀` in `A`. … So `y₀ = y`, and therefore `y` is not adjacent to `x₂`."*

The proof shrinks the hub instead.  Let `Y₀ ⊆ Y` be anticonnected, contain `y`, contain a
vertex nonadjacent to `x₂`, and be smaller than `Y`.  The hypotheses of 19.2 hold for `Y₀`,
so the induction on `|Y|` applies to it, and localized to `A` it returns a wheel with rim
in `{x₀,x₁,z} ∪ A` whose two disjoint `Y₀`-complete edges put two distinct `Y₀`-complete
vertices inside `A` (`Thm192Claim9YAdjX2TwoComplete.two_complete_in_A`).  This is the
printed sentence of claim (1), *"by the minimality of `|Y|` … there is a `Y \ {y₂}`-complete
vertex in `A`"*, read for the hub `Y₀`.  Both vertices are adjacent to `y`, because
`y ∈ Y₀`, so both equal `f`, a contradiction.  So no such `Y₀` is smaller than `Y`, which
is the hypothesis of `minimalHubContradiction`.

links.rationale: Closes the x2-adjacent-to-y branch of claim (9) by shrinking the hub to a smaller anticonnected Y0 containing y and applying the induction on |Y| to derive two distinct Y0-complete vertices in A, contradicting f's uniqueness.

decls.name: claim9_of_x2_adj_y
decls.docstring:
Claim **(9)** of the printed proof of 19.2, in the case `G.Adj (x 2) y`.

Everything here is the printed text: the minimality of `A` produces `f`, the printed
argument *"If `y₀ ∈ Y₀`, then `x₂` is not `Y₀`-complete, and therefore by (2) there are two
`Y₀`-complete vertices in `A`, a contradiction"* rules out `y₀ ∈ Y \ {y}`, and `y₀ = y` is
impossible here because `y` is adjacent to `x₂`.  So the only surviving alternative of
`Thm192Claim9MinimalityWitnessRepaired.minimalityWitness` is that `f` is the unique
neighbour of `y` in `A`, which is `uniqueNeighbourContradiction`.

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (9)'s proof in the x2-adjacent-to-y case: y0 in Y0 is ruled out by claim (2), so f must be the unique neighbour of y in A, which is then shown impossible.

decls.name: anticonnected_singleton
decls.docstring: A singleton is anticonnected.

decls.name: claim11
decls.docstring:
Claim **(11)** of the printed proof: *"`z` is not `Y₀`-complete, and `x₂` is
`Y₀`-complete and nonadjacent to `y`."*

links.rationale: The Lean statement of claim (11) of 19.2's proof, used in the x2-adjacent-to-y branch of claim (9): z is not Y0-complete, and x2 is Y0-complete and nonadjacent to y.

decls.name: z_notMem_path
decls.docstring:
The three vertices of the wheel system, and `z`, all lie outside `A₁`, hence outside
any `A ⊆ A₁`.

decls.name: hole_zP
decls.docstring: *"let `C` be the hole `z-x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁-z`"*.

decls.name: P_len_ge_five
decls.docstring:
The hole `z-x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁-z` has at least six vertices: `n = 1` would make `p₁`
an `{x₀,x₁}`-complete vertex of `A₁`, and `n = 2` would make the hole odd.

decls.name: exists_pathA
decls.docstring:
*"Let `x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁` be a path from `x₀` to `x₁` with interior in `A`"* — such a path
exists because `A` is connected and both `x₀, x₁` have neighbours in it.

decls.name: isWheel_congr
decls.docstring:
Transport of `IsWheel` along a re-listing of the rim with the same vertices and the
same length (used for the `x₀ ↔ x₁` symmetry, where the rim `z-x₀-P-x₁-z` is read backwards
as `z-x₁-P̄-x₀-z`).

decls.name: interludeChoice
decls.docstring:
*"Let us choose `p₁,…,pₙ` and `C` such that either `x₂` is `Y₀`-complete or `(C,Y₀)` is
a wheel (this is possible by (2))."*

**The right disjunct carries a second conjunct**: `{p₁,…,pₙ}` contains *two distinct*
`Y₀`-complete vertices.  This is not decoration — it is the fact claims (6) and (10) need
(*"all other vertices of `Y` have at least two neighbours in `{p₁,…,pₙ}`"*), and it is
**not recoverable from `IsWheel G (z :: P) (Y \ {y})`**: `IsWheel` has no clause giving a
hub vertex a rim neighbour, and its two-disjoint-edges clause yields at most *one*
`Y₀`-complete interior vertex, since `z` absorbs one of the two edges.

The fact is available all the same, from the *other* conjunct of claim (2): the count
`2 ≤ #{Y₀-complete edges of P}`, converted by `Thm192Infra.two_complete_in_interior`.  The
paper cites claim (2) in exactly this form at claims (3) and (9) and shorthands it as
*"is a wheel"* only at (6) and (10); the shorthand is a citation slip in the exposition,
not a gap in the mathematics.  An earlier revision of this file destructured `hedges` and
then threw the second edge away via `Set.nonempty_of_ncard_ne_zero`, which is what made
(6) and (10) look unprovable.  Do not weaken it back.

The conjunct is attached to the **right disjunct only**.  That is sound because `Or.inr` is
produced solely in the branch where claim (2) returned its own right disjunct with
`Y₀ ≠ ∅`, and that branch returns claim (2)'s own `P` — the very path the edge count speaks
about.  The two `Or.inl` branches return an unrelated `P₀` with no edge data.

decls.name: path_ends_attached
decls.docstring: The two ends of the path `x₀-p₁-⋯-pₙ-x₁` are attached to its interior.

decls.name: hx2_noP
decls.docstring: *"By (7) and (9), `x₂` has no neighbour in `{p₁,…,pₙ}`."*

decls.name: interludeF
decls.docstring:
*"From (7) and (9), it follows that there exists `f ∈ A` such that `A \ {f}` is
connected, `f` does not belong to `C`, and `f` is the unique neighbour of `x₂` in `A`."*

decls.name: interludeUnique
decls.docstring:
*"From (7) and (9), it follows that there exists `f ∈ A` such that `A \ {f}` is
connected, `f` does not belong to `C`, and `f` is the unique neighbour of `x₂` in `A`."* -/
private theorem interludeF {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : InF7 G) {z : V} {A₀ : Set V}
    (hframe : IsFrame G z A₀) {x : ℕ → V} (hws : IsWheelSystem G z A₀ x 2)
    {Y : Set V} (hHyp : Hyp192 G z A₀ x Y)
    (ih : (∀ Y' : Set V, Y'.ncard < Y.ncard → Hyp192 G z A₀ x Y' → Concl192 G z A₀ x Y') ∧
      Workspace.ProofLemmas.Thm192Setup.IHInduced G Y.ncard)
    {y : V} (hyY : y ∈ Y) (hyz : G.Adj y z)
    (hY0 : Y \ {y} = ∅ ∨ AnticonnectedSet G (Y \ {y}))
    {A : Set V} (hA : GoodA G z A₀ x Y y A)
    (hAmin : ∀ B : Set V, GoodA G z A₀ x Y y B → A.ncard ≤ B.ncard)
    (hcex : ¬ Thm192Setup.Concl192 G z A₀ x Y)
    {P : List V} (hP : IsPathFrom G P (x 0) (x 1))
    (hPint : ∀ w ∈ SPGT.interior P, w ∈ A) (hPlen : 3 ≤ P.length)
    (hx2noP : ∀ w ∈ SPGT.interior P, ¬ G.Adj (x 2) w)
    (h2y : ¬ G.Adj (x 2) y) :
    ∃ f : V, f ∈ A ∧ ConnectedSet G (A \ {f}) ∧ f ∉ P ∧ G.Adj (x 2) f ∧
      (∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj (x 2) a → a = f) := by
  obtain ⟨hAsub, hAconn, hA0, hA1, hA2, hAY, hAy⟩ := hA
  set B : Set V := {v : V | v ∈ SPGT.interior P} with hBdef
  have hBsub : B ⊆ A := fun v hv => hPint v hv
  have hBconn : ConnectedSet G B := MinimalConnectedIsPath.connectedSet_interior hP
  obtain ⟨hnb0, hnb1⟩ := path_ends_attached hP hPlen
  have hABne : (A ∩ B).Nonempty := by
    obtain ⟨a, haB, -⟩ := hnb0
    exact ⟨a, hBsub haB, haB⟩
  have hx2B : x 2 ∉ B := fun h => x_notMem_A1 hws (by omega) (hAsub (hBsub h))
  obtain ⟨p, hpAB, R, hR, hRpos, hRmem, hRB⟩ :=
    FirstTargetInducedPathInConnectedSet.firstTargetInducedPathInConnectedSet G A B (x 2)
      hAconn hA2 hABne hx2B
  have hRlen2 : 2 ≤ R.length := by have := PathBasics.pathLength_eq R; omega
  have hRnd : R.Nodup := PathBasics.path_nodup hR.1
  have hR0 : R[0]'(by omega) = x 2 := PathBasics.getElem_zero_of_head? hR.2.1 (by omega)
  have hRlast : R[R.length - 1]'(by omega) = p :=
    PathBasics.getElem_last_of_getLast? hR.2.2 (by omega)
  set f : V := R[1]'(by omega) with hfdef
  have hfadj : G.Adj (x 2) f := by
    have := PathBasics.path_adj_succ hR.1 (show 0 + 1 < R.length by omega)
    rwa [hR0] at this
  have hfmemR : f ∈ R := List.getElem_mem _
  have hfne2 : f ≠ x 2 := by
    rw [hfdef, ← hR0]
    exact PathBasics.path_ne_of_ne_index hR.1 (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)
  have hfA : f ∈ A := hRmem f hfmemR hfne2
  have hfB : f ∉ B := fun h => hx2noP f h hfadj
  have hfp : f ≠ p := fun h => hfB ((hRB f hfmemR).mpr h)
  have hpB : p ∈ B := hpAB.2
  have hpR : p ∈ R := by
    rw [← hRlast]; exact List.getElem_mem _
  have hpne2 : p ≠ x 2 := fun h => hx2B (h ▸ hpB)
  have hRlen3 : 3 ≤ R.length := by
    by_contra hcon
    have h2 : R.length = 2 := by omega
    exact hfp (by rw [hfdef, ← hRlast]; congr 1; omega)
  -- membership in the two tails of `R`
  have htake1 : R.take 1 = [x 2] := by
    rw [List.take_one, hR.2.1]; rfl
  have htake2 : R.take 2 = [x 2, f] := by
    rw [show (2 : ℕ) = 1 + 1 from rfl, List.take_succ, htake1,
      List.getElem?_eq_getElem (show 1 < R.length by omega)]
    rfl
  have hmem1 : ∀ a : V, a ∈ R.drop 1 ↔ (a ∈ R ∧ a ≠ x 2) := by
    intro a
    constructor
    · intro ha
      have hdisj : ∀ u ∈ R.take 1, ∀ v ∈ R.drop 1, u ≠ v := by
        have hnd := hRnd
        rw [← List.take_append_drop 1 R] at hnd
        exact (List.nodup_append.mp hnd).2.2
      refine ⟨(List.drop_sublist 1 R).subset ha, ?_⟩
      intro hc
      exact hdisj (x 2) (by rw [htake1]; simp) _ ha hc.symm
    · rintro ⟨ha, hane⟩
      have : a ∈ R.take 1 ++ R.drop 1 := by rwa [List.take_append_drop]
      rcases List.mem_append.mp this with h | h
      · rw [htake1] at h; simp at h; exact absurd h hane
      · exact h
  have hmem2 : ∀ a : V, a ∈ R.drop 2 ↔ (a ∈ R ∧ a ≠ x 2 ∧ a ≠ f) := by
    intro a
    constructor
    · intro ha
      have haR : a ∈ R := (List.drop_sublist 2 R).subset ha
      have hdisj : ∀ u ∈ R.take 2, ∀ v ∈ R.drop 2, u ≠ v := by
        have hnd := hRnd
        rw [← List.take_append_drop 2 R] at hnd
        exact (List.nodup_append.mp hnd).2.2
      refine ⟨haR, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro hc; exact hdisj (x 2) (by rw [htake2]; simp) _ ha hc.symm
      · intro hc; exact hdisj f (by rw [htake2]; simp) _ ha hc.symm
    · rintro ⟨ha, h2, hf⟩
      have : a ∈ R.take 2 ++ R.drop 2 := by rwa [List.take_append_drop]
      rcases List.mem_append.mp this with h | h
      · rw [htake2] at h
        simp only [List.mem_cons, List.mem_singleton, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at h
        rcases h with h | h
        · exact absurd h h2
        · exact absurd h hf
      · exact h
  have hR1conn : ConnectedSet G {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 1} :=
    InducedPathExtraction.connectedSet_setOf_mem_of_isPathList
      (PathBasics.isPathList_drop hR.1 (by omega))
  have hR2conn : ConnectedSet G {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 2} :=
    InducedPathExtraction.connectedSet_setOf_mem_of_isPathList
      (PathBasics.isPathList_drop hR.1 (by omega))
  have hfdrop1 : f ∈ R.drop 1 := (hmem1 f).mpr ⟨hfmemR, hfne2⟩
  have hpdrop1 : p ∈ R.drop 1 := (hmem1 p).mpr ⟨hpR, hpne2⟩
  have hpdrop2 : p ∈ R.drop 2 := (hmem2 p).mpr ⟨hpR, hpne2, fun h => hfp h.symm⟩
  -- `F = interior(P) ∪ (R \ x₂)` is connected, lies in `A`, and catches all of `x₀,x₁,x₂`
  have hFconn : ConnectedSet G (B ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 1}) :=
    ConnectedSetUnionAttach.connectedSet_union hBconn hR1conn (Or.inl ⟨p, hpB, hpdrop1⟩)
  have hFsub : B ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 1} ⊆ A := by
    rintro v (hv | hv)
    · exact hBsub hv
    · exact hRmem v ((hmem1 v).mp hv).1 ((hmem1 v).mp hv).2
  have hFeq : B ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 1} = A := by
    refine Thm192Claim9NotAdjX2.claim9_of_not_x2_adj_y G hG z A₀ hframe x hws Y hHyp ih y
      hyY hyz hY0 A ⟨hAsub, hAconn, hA0, hA1, hA2, hAY, hAy⟩ hAmin hcex h2y _ hFsub hFconn
      ?_ ?_ ?_
    · obtain ⟨a, haB, hadj⟩ := hnb0
      exact ⟨a, Or.inl haB, hadj⟩
    · obtain ⟨a, haB, hadj⟩ := hnb1
      exact ⟨a, Or.inl haB, hadj⟩
    · exact ⟨f, Or.inr hfdrop1, hfadj⟩
  -- uniqueness of `f`
  have huniq : ∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj (x 2) a → a = f := by
    intro a haA hadj
    rw [← hFeq] at haA
    rcases haA with hv | hv
    · exact absurd hadj (hx2noP a hv)
    · obtain ⟨haR, -⟩ := (hmem1 a).mp hv
      obtain ⟨k, hk, hka⟩ := List.mem_iff_getElem.mp haR
      have hadj' : G.Adj (R[0]'(by omega)) (R[k]'hk) := by rw [hR0, hka]; exact hadj
      have hk1 : k = 1 := by
        rcases (PathBasics.path_adj_iff hR.1 (show 0 < R.length by omega) hk).mp hadj' with h | h
        · omega
        · omega
      rw [hfdef, ← hka]
      congr 1
  -- `A \ {f}` is connected
  have hAf : A \ {f} = B ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 2} := by
    ext a
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨haA, haf⟩
      rw [← hFeq] at haA
      rcases haA with hv | hv
      · exact Or.inl hv
      · obtain ⟨haR, hane⟩ := (hmem1 a).mp hv
        exact Or.inr ((hmem2 a).mpr ⟨haR, hane, by simpa using haf⟩)
    · rintro (hv | hv)
      · exact ⟨hBsub hv, by simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff]; rintro rfl; exact hfB hv⟩
      · obtain ⟨haR, hane, hanef⟩ := (hmem2 a).mp hv
        exact ⟨hRmem a haR hane, by simpa using hanef⟩
  refine ⟨f, hfA, ?_, ?_, hfadj, huniq⟩
  · rw [hAf]
    exact ConnectedSetUnionAttach.connectedSet_union hBconn hR2conn (Or.inl ⟨p, hpB, hpdrop2⟩)
  · intro hfP
    have hf0 : f ≠ x 0 := by
      intro h; exact x_notMem_A1 hws (Nat.zero_le 2) (h ▸ hAsub hfA)
    have hf1 : f ≠ x 1 := by
      intro h; exact x_notMem_A1 hws (by omega) (h ▸ hAsub hfA)
    exact hfB ((PathBasics.mem_interior_iff_of_pathFrom hP).mpr ⟨hfP, hf0, hf1⟩)

/-! ### The interlude before (11): *"From (9) one of `x₀, x₁` has a unique neighbour in `A`"*

decls.name: endgameAt
decls.docstring:
*"From (7) and (9), it follows that there exists `f ∈ A` such that `A \ {f}` is
connected, `f` does not belong to `C`, and `f` is the unique neighbour of `x₂` in `A`."* -/
private theorem interludeF {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : InF7 G) {z : V} {A₀ : Set V}
    (hframe : IsFrame G z A₀) {x : ℕ → V} (hws : IsWheelSystem G z A₀ x 2)
    {Y : Set V} (hHyp : Hyp192 G z A₀ x Y)
    (ih : (∀ Y' : Set V, Y'.ncard < Y.ncard → Hyp192 G z A₀ x Y' → Concl192 G z A₀ x Y') ∧
      Workspace.ProofLemmas.Thm192Setup.IHInduced G Y.ncard)
    {y : V} (hyY : y ∈ Y) (hyz : G.Adj y z)
    (hY0 : Y \ {y} = ∅ ∨ AnticonnectedSet G (Y \ {y}))
    {A : Set V} (hA : GoodA G z A₀ x Y y A)
    (hAmin : ∀ B : Set V, GoodA G z A₀ x Y y B → A.ncard ≤ B.ncard)
    (hcex : ¬ Thm192Setup.Concl192 G z A₀ x Y)
    {P : List V} (hP : IsPathFrom G P (x 0) (x 1))
    (hPint : ∀ w ∈ SPGT.interior P, w ∈ A) (hPlen : 3 ≤ P.length)
    (hx2noP : ∀ w ∈ SPGT.interior P, ¬ G.Adj (x 2) w)
    (h2y : ¬ G.Adj (x 2) y) :
    ∃ f : V, f ∈ A ∧ ConnectedSet G (A \ {f}) ∧ f ∉ P ∧ G.Adj (x 2) f ∧
      (∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj (x 2) a → a = f) := by
  obtain ⟨hAsub, hAconn, hA0, hA1, hA2, hAY, hAy⟩ := hA
  set B : Set V := {v : V | v ∈ SPGT.interior P} with hBdef
  have hBsub : B ⊆ A := fun v hv => hPint v hv
  have hBconn : ConnectedSet G B := MinimalConnectedIsPath.connectedSet_interior hP
  obtain ⟨hnb0, hnb1⟩ := path_ends_attached hP hPlen
  have hABne : (A ∩ B).Nonempty := by
    obtain ⟨a, haB, -⟩ := hnb0
    exact ⟨a, hBsub haB, haB⟩
  have hx2B : x 2 ∉ B := fun h => x_notMem_A1 hws (by omega) (hAsub (hBsub h))
  obtain ⟨p, hpAB, R, hR, hRpos, hRmem, hRB⟩ :=
    FirstTargetInducedPathInConnectedSet.firstTargetInducedPathInConnectedSet G A B (x 2)
      hAconn hA2 hABne hx2B
  have hRlen2 : 2 ≤ R.length := by have := PathBasics.pathLength_eq R; omega
  have hRnd : R.Nodup := PathBasics.path_nodup hR.1
  have hR0 : R[0]'(by omega) = x 2 := PathBasics.getElem_zero_of_head? hR.2.1 (by omega)
  have hRlast : R[R.length - 1]'(by omega) = p :=
    PathBasics.getElem_last_of_getLast? hR.2.2 (by omega)
  set f : V := R[1]'(by omega) with hfdef
  have hfadj : G.Adj (x 2) f := by
    have := PathBasics.path_adj_succ hR.1 (show 0 + 1 < R.length by omega)
    rwa [hR0] at this
  have hfmemR : f ∈ R := List.getElem_mem _
  have hfne2 : f ≠ x 2 := by
    rw [hfdef, ← hR0]
    exact PathBasics.path_ne_of_ne_index hR.1 (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)
  have hfA : f ∈ A := hRmem f hfmemR hfne2
  have hfB : f ∉ B := fun h => hx2noP f h hfadj
  have hfp : f ≠ p := fun h => hfB ((hRB f hfmemR).mpr h)
  have hpB : p ∈ B := hpAB.2
  have hpR : p ∈ R := by
    rw [← hRlast]; exact List.getElem_mem _
  have hpne2 : p ≠ x 2 := fun h => hx2B (h ▸ hpB)
  have hRlen3 : 3 ≤ R.length := by
    by_contra hcon
    have h2 : R.length = 2 := by omega
    exact hfp (by rw [hfdef, ← hRlast]; congr 1; omega)
  -- membership in the two tails of `R`
  have htake1 : R.take 1 = [x 2] := by
    rw [List.take_one, hR.2.1]; rfl
  have htake2 : R.take 2 = [x 2, f] := by
    rw [show (2 : ℕ) = 1 + 1 from rfl, List.take_succ, htake1,
      List.getElem?_eq_getElem (show 1 < R.length by omega)]
    rfl
  have hmem1 : ∀ a : V, a ∈ R.drop 1 ↔ (a ∈ R ∧ a ≠ x 2) := by
    intro a
    constructor
    · intro ha
      have hdisj : ∀ u ∈ R.take 1, ∀ v ∈ R.drop 1, u ≠ v := by
        have hnd := hRnd
        rw [← List.take_append_drop 1 R] at hnd
        exact (List.nodup_append.mp hnd).2.2
      refine ⟨(List.drop_sublist 1 R).subset ha, ?_⟩
      intro hc
      exact hdisj (x 2) (by rw [htake1]; simp) _ ha hc.symm
    · rintro ⟨ha, hane⟩
      have : a ∈ R.take 1 ++ R.drop 1 := by rwa [List.take_append_drop]
      rcases List.mem_append.mp this with h | h
      · rw [htake1] at h; simp at h; exact absurd h hane
      · exact h
  have hmem2 : ∀ a : V, a ∈ R.drop 2 ↔ (a ∈ R ∧ a ≠ x 2 ∧ a ≠ f) := by
    intro a
    constructor
    · intro ha
      have haR : a ∈ R := (List.drop_sublist 2 R).subset ha
      have hdisj : ∀ u ∈ R.take 2, ∀ v ∈ R.drop 2, u ≠ v := by
        have hnd := hRnd
        rw [← List.take_append_drop 2 R] at hnd
        exact (List.nodup_append.mp hnd).2.2
      refine ⟨haR, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro hc; exact hdisj (x 2) (by rw [htake2]; simp) _ ha hc.symm
      · intro hc; exact hdisj f (by rw [htake2]; simp) _ ha hc.symm
    · rintro ⟨ha, h2, hf⟩
      have : a ∈ R.take 2 ++ R.drop 2 := by rwa [List.take_append_drop]
      rcases List.mem_append.mp this with h | h
      · rw [htake2] at h
        simp only [List.mem_cons, List.mem_singleton, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at h
        rcases h with h | h
        · exact absurd h h2
        · exact absurd h hf
      · exact h
  have hR1conn : ConnectedSet G {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 1} :=
    InducedPathExtraction.connectedSet_setOf_mem_of_isPathList
      (PathBasics.isPathList_drop hR.1 (by omega))
  have hR2conn : ConnectedSet G {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 2} :=
    InducedPathExtraction.connectedSet_setOf_mem_of_isPathList
      (PathBasics.isPathList_drop hR.1 (by omega))
  have hfdrop1 : f ∈ R.drop 1 := (hmem1 f).mpr ⟨hfmemR, hfne2⟩
  have hpdrop1 : p ∈ R.drop 1 := (hmem1 p).mpr ⟨hpR, hpne2⟩
  have hpdrop2 : p ∈ R.drop 2 := (hmem2 p).mpr ⟨hpR, hpne2, fun h => hfp h.symm⟩
  -- `F = interior(P) ∪ (R \ x₂)` is connected, lies in `A`, and catches all of `x₀,x₁,x₂`
  have hFconn : ConnectedSet G (B ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 1}) :=
    ConnectedSetUnionAttach.connectedSet_union hBconn hR1conn (Or.inl ⟨p, hpB, hpdrop1⟩)
  have hFsub : B ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 1} ⊆ A := by
    rintro v (hv | hv)
    · exact hBsub hv
    · exact hRmem v ((hmem1 v).mp hv).1 ((hmem1 v).mp hv).2
  have hFeq : B ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 1} = A := by
    refine Thm192Claim9NotAdjX2.claim9_of_not_x2_adj_y G hG z A₀ hframe x hws Y hHyp ih y
      hyY hyz hY0 A ⟨hAsub, hAconn, hA0, hA1, hA2, hAY, hAy⟩ hAmin hcex h2y _ hFsub hFconn
      ?_ ?_ ?_
    · obtain ⟨a, haB, hadj⟩ := hnb0
      exact ⟨a, Or.inl haB, hadj⟩
    · obtain ⟨a, haB, hadj⟩ := hnb1
      exact ⟨a, Or.inl haB, hadj⟩
    · exact ⟨f, Or.inr hfdrop1, hfadj⟩
  -- uniqueness of `f`
  have huniq : ∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj (x 2) a → a = f := by
    intro a haA hadj
    rw [← hFeq] at haA
    rcases haA with hv | hv
    · exact absurd hadj (hx2noP a hv)
    · obtain ⟨haR, -⟩ := (hmem1 a).mp hv
      obtain ⟨k, hk, hka⟩ := List.mem_iff_getElem.mp haR
      have hadj' : G.Adj (R[0]'(by omega)) (R[k]'hk) := by rw [hR0, hka]; exact hadj
      have hk1 : k = 1 := by
        rcases (PathBasics.path_adj_iff hR.1 (show 0 < R.length by omega) hk).mp hadj' with h | h
        · omega
        · omega
      rw [hfdef, ← hka]
      congr 1
  -- `A \ {f}` is connected
  have hAf : A \ {f} = B ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R.drop 2} := by
    ext a
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨haA, haf⟩
      rw [← hFeq] at haA
      rcases haA with hv | hv
      · exact Or.inl hv
      · obtain ⟨haR, hane⟩ := (hmem1 a).mp hv
        exact Or.inr ((hmem2 a).mpr ⟨haR, hane, by simpa using haf⟩)
    · rintro (hv | hv)
      · exact ⟨hBsub hv, by simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff]; rintro rfl; exact hfB hv⟩
      · obtain ⟨haR, hane, hanef⟩ := (hmem2 a).mp hv
        exact ⟨hRmem a haR hane, by simpa using hanef⟩
  refine ⟨f, hfA, ?_, ?_, hfadj, huniq⟩
  · rw [hAf]
    exact ConnectedSetUnionAttach.connectedSet_union hBconn hR2conn (Or.inl ⟨p, hpB, hpdrop2⟩)
  · intro hfP
    have hf0 : f ≠ x 0 := by
      intro h; exact x_notMem_A1 hws (Nat.zero_le 2) (h ▸ hAsub hfA)
    have hf1 : f ≠ x 1 := by
      intro h; exact x_notMem_A1 hws (by omega) (h ▸ hAsub hfA)
    exact hfB ((PathBasics.mem_interior_iff_of_pathFrom hP).mpr ⟨hfP, hf0, hf1⟩)

/-! ### The interlude before (11): *"From (9) one of `x₀, x₁` has a unique neighbour in `A`"* -/

private theorem interludeUnique {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : InF7 G) {z : V} {A₀ : Set V}
    (hframe : IsFrame G z A₀) {x : ℕ → V} (hws : IsWheelSystem G z A₀ x 2)
    {Y : Set V} (hHyp : Hyp192 G z A₀ x Y)
    (ih : (∀ Y' : Set V, Y'.ncard < Y.ncard → Hyp192 G z A₀ x Y' → Concl192 G z A₀ x Y') ∧
      Workspace.ProofLemmas.Thm192Setup.IHInduced G Y.ncard)
    {y : V} (hyY : y ∈ Y) (hyz : G.Adj y z)
    (hY0 : Y \ {y} = ∅ ∨ AnticonnectedSet G (Y \ {y}))
    {A : Set V} (hA : GoodA G z A₀ x Y y A)
    (hAmin : ∀ B : Set V, GoodA G z A₀ x Y y B → A.ncard ≤ B.ncard)
    (hcex : ¬ Thm192Setup.Concl192 G z A₀ x Y)
    {P : List V} (hP : IsPathFrom G P (x 0) (x 1))
    (hPint : ∀ w ∈ SPGT.interior P, w ∈ A) (hPlen : 3 ≤ P.length)
    {f : V} (hfA : f ∈ A) (hfP : f ∉ P)
    (h2y : ¬ G.Adj (x 2) y) :
    (∃ f₁, f₁ ∈ A ∧ G.Adj (x 0) f₁ ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj (x 0) a → a = f₁) ∨
    (∃ f₁, f₁ ∈ A ∧ G.Adj (x 1) f₁ ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj (x 1) a → a = f₁) := by
  obtain ⟨hnb0, hnb1⟩ := path_ends_attached hP hPlen
  -- `A` has at least two vertices: `f ∉ P`, while `p₁ ∈ P`
  have hAns : ¬ A.Subsingleton := by
    obtain ⟨a, haInt, -⟩ := hnb0
    intro hsub
    exact hfP (hsub hfA (hPint a haInt) ▸ PathBasics.interior_subset haInt)
  -- by (9), every non-cut vertex of `A` is the unique neighbour in `A` of one of `x₀,x₁,x₂`
  have key : ∀ v ∈ A, ConnectedSet G (A \ {v}) →
      (G.Adj (x 0) v ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj (x 0) a → a = v) ∨
      (G.Adj (x 1) v ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj (x 1) a → a = v) ∨
      (G.Adj (x 2) v ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj (x 2) a → a = v) := by
    intro v hvA hconn
    by_cases h0 : ∃ a ∈ A \ {v}, G.Adj (x 0) a
    · by_cases h1 : ∃ a ∈ A \ {v}, G.Adj (x 1) a
      · by_cases h2 : ∃ a ∈ A \ {v}, G.Adj (x 2) a
        · exfalso
          have heq : A \ {v} = A :=
            Thm192Claim9NotAdjX2.claim9_of_not_x2_adj_y G hG z A₀ hframe x hws Y hHyp ih y hyY hyz hY0 A hA hAmin hcex h2y
              (A \ {v}) Set.diff_subset hconn h0 h1 h2
          have hvv : v ∈ A \ {v} := by rw [heq]; exact hvA
          exact hvv.2 rfl
        · push_neg at h2
          obtain ⟨a, haA, hadj⟩ := hA.2.2.2.2.1
          have hav : a = v := by
            by_contra hne
            exact h2 a ⟨haA, by simpa using hne⟩ hadj
          exact Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hav ▸ hadj, fun b hbA hbadj => by
            by_contra hne; exact h2 b ⟨hbA, by simpa using hne⟩ hbadj⟩)
      · push_neg at h1
        obtain ⟨a, haA, hadj⟩ := hA.2.2.2.1
        have hav : a = v := by
          by_contra hne
          exact h1 a ⟨haA, by simpa using hne⟩ hadj
        exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hav ▸ hadj, fun b hbA hbadj => by
          by_contra hne; exact h1 b ⟨hbA, by simpa using hne⟩ hbadj⟩)
    · push_neg at h0
      obtain ⟨a, haA, hadj⟩ := hA.2.2.1
      have hav : a = v := by
        by_contra hne
        exact h0 a ⟨haA, by simpa using hne⟩ hadj
      exact Or.inl ⟨hav ▸ hadj, fun b hbA hbadj => by
        by_contra hne; exact h0 b ⟨hbA, by simpa using hne⟩ hbadj⟩
  obtain ⟨a, haA, b, hbA, hab, hAa, hAb⟩ := NonCutVertices.exists_two_noncut hA.2.1 hAns
  rcases key a haA hAa with ha | ha | ha
  · exact Or.inl ⟨a, haA, ha⟩
  · exact Or.inr ⟨a, haA, ha⟩
  · rcases key b hbA hAb with hb | hb | hb
    · exact Or.inl ⟨b, hbA, hb⟩
    · exact Or.inr ⟨b, hbA, hb⟩
    · exact absurd (ha.2 b hbA hb.1).symm hab

decls.name: inductive_wheel_with_rim_in_A
decls.docstring:
**PAPER** (printed p. 118, claim (2)): *"From the minimality of `|Y|`, `z` is
`Y₀`-complete and therefore `Y`-complete, and there is a path as in the claim."*

`A ∪ {x₀,x₁,x₂,z} ∪ Y₀` with the frame `(z,A)`.

decls.name: two_complete_in_A
decls.docstring:
**Two distinct vertices of `A` are `Y₀`-complete**, for every anticonnected
`Y₀ ⊆ Y` that is smaller than `Y` and to which `x₂` is not complete.

PAPER (19.2, claim (1), printed p. 118): *"By the minimality of `|Y|`, `z` is
`Y \ {y₂}`-complete and there is a `Y \ {y₂}`-complete vertex in `A`."*  The printed
sentence is used with the hub `Y \ {y₂}`; the statement below is the same step for an
arbitrary smaller hub, and it produces *two* such vertices, exactly as claim (2) does
for the hub `Y \ {y}` (`Thm192Infra.two_complete_in_interior`).

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (1)'s use of the minimality of |Y| to produce two distinct Y0-complete vertices in A, for any anticonnected Y0 subset of Y smaller than Y to which x2 is not complete.

decls.name: endgame
decls.docstring:
The closing paragraph of the printed proof of 19.2: *"To conclude, `A ∪ {x₂}` catches
`{y,z,x₁}` … Thus there is no such choice of `Y`.  This proves 19.2."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the closing paragraph of 19.2's proof: A union {x2} catches {y, z, x1}, forcing y adjacent to f1 = qk and a final parity contradiction, so no counterexample Y exists.

Generic infrastructure: a finite connected set strictly containing a nonempty subset has a vertex outside the subset whose removal keeps it connected, used for the many "choose f in A minus F such that A minus {f} is connected" steps.
Generic infrastructure: builds a hole from a cut vertex and two paths meeting only there, used to assemble the various holes C, C1 constructed throughout 19.2's proof.

Generic infrastructure: an antipath with given endpoint adjacencies extends by one edge on each side to an antihole; feeds the many "can be completed to an antihole via ..." steps throughout 19.2's proof.
Generic infrastructure: restates "the only neighbour of v in F is w" as the set-equality form {f in F | Adj v f} = {w}, used pervasively in the printed proof's unique-neighbour hypotheses.
Generic infrastructure: assembles an odd wheel from parity data about complete edges, feeding the repeated "(C, Y) is an odd wheel, a contradiction, since G is in F7" steps.
Generic infrastructure: if all members of a set W have at least two neighbours in a path's interior, then two distinct W-complete vertices exist in the interior.

decls.name: Concl192

decls.name: IHInduced
decls.docstring:
The induction hypothesis carried by the printed proof of 19.2.

PAPER (printed p. 118): *"If possible, choose `Y` not satisfying the theorem, with
`|Y|` minimum."*

The counterexample minimised over is a whole tuple `(G, (z,A₀), x₀x₁x₂, Y)`, not just
the set `Y` inside one fixed graph: nothing in the printed proof keeps the graph fixed.
Claim (2) uses exactly that extra freedom.  It applies the theorem to the graph induced
on `A ∪ {x₀,x₁,x₂,z} ∪ Y₀` with the frame `(z,A)`, where the set called `A₁` is `A`
itself, and so obtains a wheel whose rim lies in `{x₀,x₁,z} ∪ A` rather than merely in
`{x₀,x₁,z} ∪ A₁`; see `Thm192Claim2Localization.inductive_wheel_with_rim_in_A`.

`IHInduced G n` is that half of the induction hypothesis: 19.2 holds in every induced
subgraph of `G`, for every frame and wheel system there, and every hub of size less
than `n`.  (The other half — 19.2 in `G` itself for hubs smaller than `Y` — is the
`∀ Y'` clause that accompanies it in every lemma of the proof.)  Only the vertex set
shrinks, so the recursion is on `n` alone; `Thm192Claim2Uniform.uniform_induction`
runs it.

links.rationale: Packages the induction hypothesis carried by the printed proof of 19.2: the theorem's conclusion holds for every anticonnected Y of strictly smaller cardinality satisfying the same hypotheses.

decls.name: IHInduced_mono
decls.docstring:
`IHInduced` is antitone in the bound: an induction hypothesis for hubs smaller
than `n` is one for hubs smaller than any `m ≤ n`.

links.rationale: Not reachable from the main theorem Workspace.MainTheorem.SPGT.thm_1_2 in the compiled dependency graph. IHInduced is antitone in its bound: an induction hypothesis valid for hubs smaller than n is also valid for hubs smaller than any m <= n.

decls.name: wheel_complete_vertex_in_A1
decls.docstring:
A wheel `(C, W)` whose rim lies in `{x₀,x₁,z} ∪ A₁` has a `W`-complete vertex
in `A₁`: the wheel supplies two *disjoint* `W`-complete edges of `C`, i.e. four
distinct `W`-complete vertices of the rim, and `{x₀,x₁,z}` has only three
elements.

links.rationale: A wheel (C, W) whose rim lies in {x0, x1, z} union A1 has a W-complete vertex in A1, since a wheel supplies two disjoint W-complete rim edges, hence four distinct W-complete rim vertices and at least one outside {x0, x1, z}.

decls.name: exists_minimal_goodA

*"For fixed `Y` choose `A ⊆ A₁` minimal with the properties that …"* — the second
extremal choice of the printed proof, taken (see the module header) *after* claim (1)
and with the extra clause *"`y` has a neighbour in `A`"*.

links.rationale: Formalizes the proof's second extremal choice: for fixed Y, choose A contained in A1 minimal with the properties defining GoodA.

decls.name: isWheel_congr

same length (used for the `x₀ ↔ x₁` symmetry, where the rim `z-x₀-P-x₁-z` is read backwards
as `z-x₁-P̄-x₀-z`).

decls.name: sw
decls.docstring: The sequence `x₁, x₀, x₂, x₃, …`.

links.rationale: Defines the swapped wheel-system sequence x1, x0, x2, x3, ... used to formalize "from the symmetry between x0, x1" arguments in the printed proof.
Bookkeeping: the swapped sequence's index 0 is the original x1.
Bookkeeping: the swapped sequence's index 1 is the original x0.
Bookkeeping: the swapped sequence's index 2 is the original x2, unchanged by the x0-x1 swap.
Bookkeeping: applying the swapped sequence sw at an index gives the corresponding original index with 0 and 1 exchanged.
Swapping the sequence twice returns the original sequence.
The swapped wheel system's X1 set coincides with the original X1 = {x0, x1}.
The swapped wheel system's A1 set coincides with the original A1, since A1 only depends on {x0, x1} as a set.

decls.name: sw_ws
decls.docstring: *"`x₁, x₀, x₂,…,x_t` is another wheel system"*.

links.rationale: The swapped sequence x1, x0, x2, ..., xt is again a wheel system, formalizing the printed proof's repeated appeals to symmetry between x0 and x1.
The hypothesis Hyp192 transports along the x0-x1 swap, since its clauses only depend on {x0, x1} as a set.
The conclusion Concl192 transports along the x0-x1 swap, since it only depends on {x0, x1} as a set together with A1.
The GoodA predicate transports along the x0-x1 swap, since its defining properties only depend on {x0, x1} as a set.

decls.name: sw_ih
decls.docstring:
The induction hypothesis of 19.2 transports too: this is the shape every carve-out needs,
since `ih` is one of their binders.

links.rationale: The induction hypothesis of 19.2 transports along the x0-x1 swap, since every claim carved out of the proof takes it as a binder.

decls.name: sw_goodA_min
decls.docstring: Minimality of `A` transports as well.

links.rationale: Minimality of a GoodA set transports along the x0-x1 swap as well.

decls.name: vertexComplete_mono
decls.docstring: `VertexComplete` is monotone downward in its set argument.

links.rationale: Shows VertexComplete is monotone downward in its target set: completeness to Y' implies completeness to any subset Y ⊆ Y'. Pure bookkeeping supporting wheel_hub_mono, with no distinct paper sentence of its own.

decls.name: edgeComplete_mono
decls.docstring: `EdgeComplete` is monotone downward in its set argument.

links.rationale: Shows EdgeComplete is monotone downward in the hub set: an edge that is Y'-complete remains Y-complete for any Y ⊆ Y'. Pure bookkeeping supporting wheel_hub_mono, with no distinct paper sentence of its own.

decls.name: wheel_hub_mono
decls.docstring:
A wheel with hub `Y'` is a wheel with hub any nonempty anticonnected
`Y ⊆ Y'`.  (The paper's "annoying wastage" remark, printed p. 126.)

links.rationale: Anchors to the paper's own authorial aside after the proof of 20.2 (printed p. 125): ‘There is some annoying wastage in 20.2; we produce a wheel with hub Y ∪ {x3}, and all we use in proving 20.1 is that there is a wheel with hub Y.’ The aside itself only remarks on the mismatch between what 20.2 proves and what 20.1 needs; it does not state the monotonicity fact. wheel_hub_mono is the general lemma the aside points at -- a wheel (C, Y') restricts to a wheel (C, Y) for any nonempty anticonnected Y ⊆ Y' -- which the induction in 20.1 leans on tacitly whenever it passes from 'there is a wheel with hub Y′' to 'there is a wheel with hub Y'.

decls.name: hub_avoids_frame_of_wheelSystem
decls.docstring:
If `x₀,…,x_t` is a wheel system (with `t ≥ 2`), `z ∉ Y`, and `x₀,…,x_{t−1}`
are all `Y`-complete, then `Y ⊆ V(G) \ (A₀ ∪ {z})`.

links.rationale: Derives that a hub Y disjoint from z and complete to x0,...,x_{t-1} of a wheel system must also avoid A0 and z themselves. This is an implicit side condition the printed proof of 20.1 silently relies on when it feeds 20.3's output set Y' back into the induction, but the paper never states it as its own sentence, so it stays an internal bookkeeping fact.

decls.name: anticonnected_compl
decls.docstring: `Ḡ`-anticonnectedness is `G`-connectedness.

links.rationale: Translates connectedness in G into anticonnectedness in the complement Ḡ; a bookkeeping bridge needed because 20.3's argument invokes 2.2 and 13.6 (stated for connected/anticonnected sets of G) inside the complement graph. No distinct paper sentence.

decls.name: vertexComplete_compl_iff
decls.docstring:
Being `Ḡ`-complete to `S` means being distinct from and nonadjacent to every vertex
of `S`.

links.rationale: Unwinds Ḡ-completeness to a set S into the elementary G-condition (distinct from and nonadjacent to every vertex of S); a routine translation lemma with no distinct paper sentence.

decls.name: noedge
decls.docstring:
Only the ends of the antipath can be `Ḡ`-complete to `T`, and they are `G`-adjacent, so
there is no `T`-complete edge of `Ḡ` inside the antipath.

decls.name: exists_end_nbr_of_odd_antipath
decls.docstring:
**2.2 applied in `Ḡ`.**  An odd antipath whose internal vertices all have neighbours in
the connected set `T`, and to whose interior `z` is complete while being anticomplete to
`T`, must have an end with a neighbour in `T`.

links.rationale: Formalizes 2.2 applied inside the complement graph to the repeated antipath argument of 20.3's proof: an odd antipath whose internal vertices all have neighbours in a connected set T, with z complete to its interior and anticomplete to T, must have an end with a neighbour in T. Matches the printed sentence 'Since all internal vertices of Q have neighbours in At−3, ... it follows from 2.2 applied in Ḡ that one end of Q has a neighbour in At−3' (p. 128).

decls.name: antipath_middle_of_odd
decls.docstring:
**13.6 applied in `Ḡ`.**  An odd antipath whose ends have no neighbours in the
connected set `T` while all its internal vertices do has length exactly `3`, and its two
internal vertices are joined by an **odd path of `G`** with interior in `T` — that is
13.6's second alternative read in `Ḡ`, and it is the *"and there is an odd path `P` between
`q, x_i` with interior in `A_{t−3} ∪ V(R \ q)`"* of printed p. 127.

links.rationale: Formalizes 13.6 applied inside the complement graph to the repeated antipath argument of 20.3's proof: an odd antipath whose ends have no neighbour in a connected set T while all internal vertices do must have length exactly 3, with its two internal vertices joined by an odd G-path with interior in T. Matches the printed instance ending 'and there is an odd path P between q, xi with interior in At−3 ∪ V(R \\ q)' (p. 129).

decls.name: antipath_length_three_of_odd
decls.docstring: The length-only form.

links.rationale: Convenience corollary that keeps only the length-3 conclusion of antipath_middle_of_odd, discarding its accompanying odd-path witness. A trivial projection, not separately tied to one paper sentence.

decls.name: ysquare_truncate_union
decls.docstring:
**The `Y`-square truncation** (printed pp. 126, 127): *"But then `x₀,…,x_{t−1}` is a
`Y ∪ {x_t}`-square of height `t − 1`."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the Y-square conclusion that both symmetric arguments of step (3) reach once xt−2 is shown adjacent to xt−1: x0,...,xt−1 becomes a Y ∪ {xt}-square of height t−1, the Y-square counterpart of YDiamondTruncation.ydiamond_truncate_union used to feed the contradiction back into 20.3's hypothesis hnone.

decls.name: anticonnected_compl
decls.docstring: `Ḡ`-anticonnectedness is `G`-connectedness.

links.rationale: Translates connectedness in G into anticonnectedness in the complement Ḡ; a bookkeeping bridge needed to invoke 2.2/13.6 inside the complement graph. No distinct paper sentence.

decls.name: vertexComplete_compl_iff
decls.docstring:
Being `Ḡ`-complete to `S` means being distinct from and nonadjacent to every vertex
of `S`.

links.rationale: Unwinds Ḡ-completeness to a set S into the elementary G-condition (distinct from and nonadjacent to every vertex of S); a routine translation lemma with no distinct paper sentence.

decls.name: q_has_nbr_in_A3
decls.docstring: **The final paragraph of 20.3**, up to *"hence `q` has a neighbour in `A_{t−3}`"*.

links.rationale: Formalizes the opening of 20.3's closing paragraph: from (3) and the choice of R, xt has no neighbour in At−3 ∪ V(R \ q); the antipath z-q-Q-xt−1-xt built from an Xt−2-interior antipath Q between q and xt−1 is shown even length by 13.6, making xt-xt−1-Q-q odd, so 2.2 gives q a neighbour in At−3.

decls.name: q_is_X3_complete
decls.docstring:
**The last sentence of the paragraph**: *"From the maximality of `A_{t−3}` it follows
that `q` is `X_{t−3}`-complete and therefore nonadjacent to `x_{t−2}`."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the last sentence of 20.3's closing paragraph: since q has a neighbour in At−3 (from q_has_nbr_in_A3), maximality of At−3 forces q to be Xt−3-complete, hence nonadjacent to xt−2 -- the fact 20.3's final case split (exists_diamond_endgame) needs to build the polished Y-diamond or truncated Y-diamond that finishes the proof.

Unfolds wheelSystemX at i+1 as wheelSystemX at i together with the single new vertex x(i+1); a definitional recursion fact used throughout this file's induction arguments, with no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: anticonnected_wheelSystemX
decls.docstring:
**Every `Xᵢ` is anticonnected.**  Induction on `i`: `X₀ = {x₀}` is a singleton, and
`xᵢ₊₁` is not `Xᵢ`-complete, so it has a `Ḡ`-neighbour in `Xᵢ`.

links.rationale: Shows every Xi is anticonnected, by induction using that x_{i+1} is not X_i-complete (clause 3 of the wheel-system definition). This is what makes phrases like 'an antipath with interior in X_{t-2}' meaningful, but the paper never states the fact itself as a sentence.

decls.name: A₀_no_complete
decls.docstring: No vertex of `A₀` is `Xᵢ`-complete, for `i ≥ 1`.

links.rationale: Shows no vertex of A0 is Xi-complete for i ≥ 1, unwinding the wheel-system clause that no vertex of A0 is complete to {x0,x1}. Structural bookkeeping used silently throughout, not itself a paper sentence.

decls.name: A₀_subset_wheelSystemA'
decls.docstring: `A₀ ⊆ Aᵢ` for `i ≥ 1`.

links.rationale: Shows A0 ⊆ Ai for every i ≥ 1, combining A₀_no_complete with the maximality characterization of Ai. Structural bookkeeping used silently throughout, not itself a paper sentence.

decls.name: notMem_wheelSystemA_of_adj_z
decls.docstring: A neighbour of `z` never lies in `Aᵢ`.

links.rationale: Shows a neighbour of z is never in Ai, immediate from Ai's defining anticompleteness-to-z clause. Elementary bookkeeping, not itself a paper sentence.

decls.name: x_notMem_wheelSystemA
decls.docstring: No `xⱼ` lies in any `Aᵢ`: `z` is adjacent to every `xⱼ`.

links.rationale: Shows no xj lies in any Ai, since z is adjacent to every xj while Ai is by definition anticomplete (in G) to z's neighbours. Elementary bookkeeping, not itself a paper sentence.

decls.name: z_notMem_wheelSystemA
decls.docstring: `z ∉ Aᵢ` for `i ≤ t`: `z` is `Xᵢ`-complete, and `Aᵢ` has no `Xᵢ`-complete vertex.

links.rationale: Shows z ∉ Ai for i ≤ t: z is Xi-complete, while Ai (by its maximality characterization) contains no Xi-complete vertex. Elementary bookkeeping, not itself a paper sentence.

decls.name: exists_nbr_wheelSystemA
decls.docstring:
**Condition 2 of the wheel-system definition, in `Aᵢ` form.**  `xᵢ` has a neighbour in
`A_{i−1}`, hence in every `A_k` with `k ≥ i − 1` (and `k ≥ 1`).  For `i = 0, 1` the
neighbour is supplied by the frame clause and `A₀ ⊆ A_k`.

links.rationale: Shows xi has a neighbour in Ak for every k ≥ max(i-1,1): condition 2 of the wheel-system definition supplies a neighbour in A_{i-1}, and A_{i-1} ⊆ Ak monotonically extends it. Restates a defining clause in Ai form; no distinct paper sentence.

decls.name: Y_notMem_wheelSystemA
decls.docstring:
**The hub misses every `Aⱼ` with `j < t`.**  Every `y ∈ Y` is adjacent to `x₀,…,x_{t−1}`
(that is what *"`x₀,…,x_{t−1}` are `Y`-complete"* says), hence is `Xⱼ`-complete for `j < t`,
hence is not in `Aⱼ`.  The paper uses this silently whenever it needs a vertex of `A_{t−2}`
to lie outside the hub.

links.rationale: Shows the hub Y is disjoint from every Aj with j < t: since x0,...,x_{t-1} are Y-complete, every y ∈ Y is Xj-complete for j < t and so cannot lie in Aj. Used silently whenever the proof needs a vertex of A_{t-2} to lie outside the hub; no single paper sentence states it.

decls.name: vertexComplete_of_nbr_of_notMem
decls.docstring:
**The maximality of `Aᵢ`.**  If `v ∉ Aᵢ`, `z` is not adjacent to `v`, and `v` has a
neighbour in `Aᵢ`, then `v` is `Xᵢ`-complete — otherwise `Aᵢ ∪ {v}` would be a member of
the family whose union is `Aᵢ`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the maximality property of Ai that the proof of 20.3 invokes verbatim three times for i = t-3: if v ∉ Ai, z is not adjacent to v, and v has a neighbour in Ai, then v must be Xi-complete, since otherwise Ai ∪ {v} would itself belong to the family whose union defines Ai. Matches the printed 'From the maximality of At−3 it follows that q is Xt−3-complete' pattern (first occurrence p. 128).

decls.name: exists_diamond_of_both_nbrs
decls.docstring: **20.3 step (1)**, in positive form.

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (1) of 20.3 in positive form: if both xt and xt−1 have a neighbour in At−3, then either x0,...,xt−1 is a Y ∪ {xt}-diamond of height t−1 (when xt−1 is Xt−3-complete) or x0,...,xt−3,xt−1,xt is a Y-diamond of height t−1 (when it is not) -- feeding either conclusion to 20.3's hypothesis hnone is claim (1)'s stated contradiction.

decls.name: exists_diamond_endgame
decls.docstring:
**The last sentence of the proof of 20.3** (printed p. 127).

> *"If `x_{t−1}` is not `X_{t−3}`-complete, then `x₀,…,x_t` is a polished
> `Y`-diamond of height `t`; while if `x_{t−1}` is `X_{t−3}`-complete, then
> `x₀,…,x_{t−1}` is a `Y ∪ {x_t}`-diamond of height `t − 1`, in both cases a
> contradiction.  This proves 20.3."*

The three data the earlier steps supply are the hypotheses `hno` (`x_t` has no
neighbour in `A_{t−3}`, from (3) and the choice of `R`), `hnbr1` (`x_{t−1}` has
one, which is (3)) and `hq` (the vertex `q ∈ A_{t−2}` of (2), adjacent to both
`x_t, x_{t−1}` and with a neighbour in `A_{t−3}`).

links.rationale: Formalizes the sentence that closes the proof of 20.3: given that xt has no neighbour in At−3 (from the endgame paragraph), xt−1 has one (claim (3)), and q ∈ At−2 witnesses adjacency to both xt, xt−1 with a further neighbour in At−3, either xt−1 is not Xt−3-complete and x0,...,xt is a polished Y-diamond of height t, or xt−1 is Xt−3-complete and x0,...,xt−1 is a Y ∪ {xt}-diamond of height t−1 -- in both cases a contradiction, which is exactly 20.3's conclusion.

decls.name: exists_antipath_to_A2
decls.docstring:
Given a vertex `w ∈ A_{t−2}` adjacent to `x_{t−1}`, there **is** an antipath between
`x_{t−1}` and `w` with interior in `X_{t−2}`.

links.rationale: Produces the antipath witness the paragraph of step (3) takes for granted ('let Q be such an antipath'): given w ∈ A_{t-2} adjacent to xt−1, builds an antipath between xt−1 and w with interior in X_{t-2} from the anticonnectedness of X_{t-2}. Existence bookkeeping, not a distinct paper sentence.

decls.name: square_from_all_odd
decls.docstring: **The `Y`-square paragraph of step (3)**, in positive form.

links.rationale: Formalizes the first Y-square sub-argument of step (3) in positive form: assuming every antipath between xt−1 and w (∈ A_{t−2}, adjacent to xt−1) with interior in X_{t−2} is odd, 2.2 gives w a neighbour in At−3, maximality of At−3 makes w Xt−3-complete and hence nonadjacent to xt−2, and the assumption then forces xt−2 adjacent to xt−1, so x0,...,xt−1 becomes a Y ∪ {xt}-square of height t−1 -- the contradiction the paper feeds to hnone.

decls.name: exists_even_antipath
decls.docstring:
**The conclusion the paper draws**: *"So we may assume some antipath `Q` between
`x_{t−1}` and `w` with interior in `X_{t−2}` is even."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the paper's contrapositive step in claim (3): if 20.3's hypothesis hnone rules out the Y ∪ {xt}-square that square_from_all_odd would build, then not every antipath between xt−1 and w with interior in X_{t−2} is odd, so some such antipath is even.

decls.name: case_no_nbr
decls.docstring: **Step (3), case `x_{t−1}` has no neighbour in `A_{t−3} ∪ V(R \ q)`.**

links.rationale: Formalizes the second branch of step (3) -- the case where xt−1 has no neighbour in At−3 ∪ V(R \ q): builds the hole C = z-xt−1-q-P-xi-z of length ≥ 6 from the odd antipath z-q-Q-xt−1 (13.6 gives Q length 2 with middle vertex xi and an odd G-path P between q, xi), rules out a length-≥6 antihole on q, xi, xt−1 via 15.7, deduces q and z are both Y-complete, and concludes the hole C carries at least three Y-complete edges -- directly establishing 20.3's conclusion that z is Y-complete and G contains a wheel with hub Y.

decls.name: common_nonneighbor
decls.docstring:
PAPER (21.1, printed p. 131): "Since ... `n ≥ 5`, and `p₁, pₙ` are
both complete to the interior of `Q`, it follows from 15.4 that `Q` has length
2, that is, there exists `x ∈ X` nonadjacent to both `pᵢ₊₁, pᵢ₊₂`."

links.rationale: The step of the printed proof of 21.1 (p. 131) that applies 15.4 to force the antipath Q joining p_i+1, p_i+2 to have length 2, producing a common nonneighbour x ∈ X of p_i, p_i+1.

decls.name: hole_through_gap
decls.docstring:
PAPER (21.1, printed p. 131): "Choose `h` with `1 ≤ h ≤ i` maximum
such that `x` is adjacent to `pₕ`, and choose `j` with `i + 3 ≤ j ≤ n`
minimum such that `x` is adjacent to `pⱼ`. Then `x-pₕ-⋯-pⱼ-x` is a hole
of length ≥ 6, say `C`, and `x, pᵢ, pᵢ₊₁, pᵢ₊₂, pᵢ₊₃` are all vertices
of it." The length bound uses that a Berge graph has no hole of length five.

links.rationale: The step of the printed proof of 21.1 (p. 131) that builds the length ≥ 6 hole C through x by extending outward from the gap at p_i, p_i+1 to the nearest neighbours of x on the path.

decls.name: wheel_of_isolated_complete_edge
decls.docstring:
PAPER (21.1, printed p. 131): "In the third case, 2.3 implies that
`(C, Y)` is a wheel." The third complete vertex excludes the exceptional
outcome of 2.3. Thus there is a second complete edge. The first edge has no
other complete neighbor at either end, so the two edges are disjoint.

links.rationale: The third-case step of the printed proof of 21.1 (p. 131): an isolated Y-complete edge on the hole, with a third complete vertex elsewhere, forces (C, Y) to be a wheel by 2.3.

decls.name: Setup
decls.docstring:
The standing hypothesis package of **21.2**, verbatim from the frozen statement:
*"Let `G ∈ F₇`, and let `Y ⊆ V(G)`, such that there do not exist `X, P` so that `(X, Y, P)` is
a pseudowheel.  Let `(z, A₀)` be a frame, and let `x₀,…,x_{t+1}` be a wheel system with hub
`Y`, and with `t ≥ 2`.  Define `Xᵢ, Aᵢ` as usual.  Suppose that `x_{t+1}` has no neighbour in
`A_{t−1}`; and moreover that at most one member of `Y` has no neighbour in
`A_{t−1} ∪ {x_{t+1}}`, and any such vertex has a neighbour in `A_t`."*

links.rationale: The standing hypothesis package of 21.2 (p. 131), verbatim from the frozen statement.

decls.name: Concl
decls.docstring: The conclusion of **21.2**: *"Then there is a wheel in `G` with hub `Y`."*

links.rationale: The Prop-valued statement of 21.2's conclusion (p. 131): there is a wheel in G with hub Y.

decls.name: GoodPath
decls.docstring:
The path built in the paragraph after claim (1):

PAPER: *"Since `x_{t+1}` has a neighbour in `A_t` and none in `A_{t−1}`, there is a path from
`x_{t+1}` to `A_{t−1}` with interior in `A_t \ A_{t−1}`.  Hence there is a path
`x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_m` such that `p₁,…,p_m ∈ A_t \ A_{t−1}` and `p_m` is the unique vertex of this
path with a neighbour in `A_{t−1}`.  (Hence `m ≥ 1`, and `p_m` is `X_{t−1}`-complete.)"*

The printed path is the Lean list `x (t + 1) :: p`; *"`p_m` is the unique vertex of this path
with a neighbour in `A_{t−1}`"* is the last clause (`x_{t+1}` itself has no such neighbour by
the hypothesis of 21.2, so quantifying over the entries of `p` is the whole content).

links.rationale: Constructs the path x_{t+1}-p_1-⋯-p_m of 21.2's proof (p. 131) from x_{t+1} to A_{t-1} with interior in A_t \ A_{t-1}, whose unique A_{t-1}-neighbour p_m is X_{t-1}-complete.

decls.name: SpanY
decls.docstring:
*"every member of `Y` has a neighbour in `A_{t−1} ∪ {x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_m}`"* — the property
by which the path of `GoodPath` is chosen *"if possible"*, and the content of claim (3).

links.rationale: The Prop-valued statement of claim (3) of the printed proof of 21.2 (p. 132): every member of Y has a neighbour in A_{t-1} ∪ {x_{t+1}, p_1,…,p_m}.

decls.name: NoOddLeapPath
decls.docstring:
Claim **(1)**: *"There do not exist `xᵢ, x_j ∈ X_t` joined by an odd path
`xᵢ-x_{t+1}-P-x_j` of length ≥ 5 such that `xᵢ, x_j ∈ X_t` and `P` has interior in `A_t`."*

The printed path is `x i :: x (t+1) :: P` where `P` lists `p₁,…,p_n, x j`; *"`P` has interior
in `A_t`"* is therefore *"every entry of `P` other than `x j` lies in `A_t`"*.

links.rationale: The Prop-valued statement of claim (1) of the printed proof of 21.2 (p. 131): no odd path of length ≥ 5 from x_i to x_j through x_{t+1} has both ends in X_t and interior in A_t.

decls.name: Claim2
decls.docstring:
Claim **(2)**: *"We may assume that one of `x₀,…,x_t` is nonadjacent to both
`x_{t+1}, p₁`."*

links.rationale: The Prop-valued statement of claim (2) of the printed proof of 21.2 (p. 132): one of x_0,…,x_t is nonadjacent to both x_{t+1}, p_1.

decls.name: Extended
decls.docstring:
The paragraph after claim (3):

PAPER: *"Since `x_t, p_m` have neighbours in `A_{t−1}` and none of `x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_{m−1}` have
neighbours in `A_{t−1}`, we can extend the path `x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_m` to a path
`x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_m-p_{m+1}-⋯-p_n` containing neighbours of all members of `X_t`.  By (2), we can
choose `i` with `2 ≤ i ≤ n` maximum such that some vertex of `X_t` is nonadjacent to all of
`x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_{i−1}`; and choose `s` with `0 ≤ s ≤ t` such that `x_s` is nonadjacent to all
of `x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_{i−1}`.  Since every vertex in `X_t` has a neighbour in
`{x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_n}`, it follows from the maximality of `i` that every vertex in `X_t` is
adjacent to one of `x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_i`."*

Here `q` is the extended list `p₁,…,p_n` (so `p <+: q`), and
`(x (t + 1) :: q).take i = [x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_{i−1}]`,
`(x (t + 1) :: q).take (i + 1) = [x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_i]`.

links.rationale: Constructs the extended path of 21.2's proof (p. 133) reaching neighbours of all of X_t, with the maximal index i and vertex x_s of claims (1)-(2) at hand.

decls.name: Cand
decls.docstring:
Auxiliary: the family of *candidate* paths minimised over in `exists_goodPath_aux`.  A
candidate is an induced path `x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_k` with all of `p₁,…,p_k` in `A_t`, whose last
vertex either lies in `A_{t−1}` or has a neighbour there.

decls.name: exists_goodPath_aux
decls.docstring:
**Existence of the path of the paragraph after claim (1)**, without the extremal clause:

PAPER: *"Since `x_{t+1}` has a neighbour in `A_t` and none in `A_{t−1}`, there is a path from
`x_{t+1}` to `A_{t−1}` with interior in `A_t \ A_{t−1}`.  Hence there is a path
`x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_m` such that `p₁,…,p_m ∈ A_t \ A_{t−1}` and `p_m` is the unique vertex of this
path with a neighbour in `A_{t−1}`."*

Implemented as the paper's *"hence"*: take a shortest candidate path.  A candidate exists
because `A_t` is connected, contains `A_{t−1} ⊇ A₀ ≠ ∅` and a neighbour of `x_{t+1}`, while
`x_{t+1} ∉ A_t` (it is adjacent to `z`).  Minimality then forces both *"`p₁,…,p_m ∉ A_{t−1}`"*
and *"`p_m` is the unique vertex with a neighbour in `A_{t−1}`"*: any earlier vertex with a
neighbour in `A_{t−1}` would give a strictly shorter candidate.

decls.name: exists_goodPath
decls.docstring:
**Construction of the path, with its extremal choice** (printed p. 131, the paragraph
following claim (1)):

*"Since `x_{t+1}` has a neighbour in `A_t` and none in `A_{t−1}`, there is a path from
`x_{t+1}` to `A_{t−1}` with interior in `A_t \ A_{t−1}`.  Hence there is a path
`x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_m` such that `p₁,…,p_m ∈ A_t \ A_{t−1}` and `p_m` is the unique vertex of this
path with a neighbour in `A_{t−1}`. …  Choose such a path such that if possible, every member
of `Y` has a neighbour in `A_{t−1} ∪ {x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_m}`."*

The *"if possible"* is discharged by cases: if some good path spans `Y` in that sense, take
it; otherwise the extremal clause is vacuous and any good path (`exists_goodPath_aux`) will
do.

links.rationale: Constructs the extremal path of 21.2's proof (p. 131, the paragraph following claim (1)), chosen to span Y when possible.

decls.name: claim1

links.rationale: Auxiliary declaration for claim (1) of the printed proof of 21.2 (p. 131).

decls.name: claim2
decls.docstring:

`x₀,…,x_t` is nonadjacent to both `x_{t+1}, p₁`."*  The *"we may assume"* is the printed
alternative that *"`x₀,…,x_{t+1}` is a `Y`-square, and the theorem holds by 20.1"*, i.e. the
conclusion of 21.2 itself.

links.rationale: Proves claim (2) of the printed proof of 21.2 (p. 132), the case split needed to reach the theorem's conclusion via 20.1.

links.rationale: Step within the proof of claim (3) of 21.2 (p. 132): once one member of Y is excepted, every other member has a neighbour in {x_{t+1}} ∪ A_{t-1}, so a path meeting the exceptional y meets all of Y.

decls.name: claim3_common_neighbor_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap: the first paragraph of 21.2(3), p. 132.
PAPER: "Since `y` has no neighbour in `A_{t-1} ∪ {p₁,…,p_m}`, it follows
from the minimality of `F` that `y` has a unique neighbour in `F`, say `f` ...
So `R` has length 2, and therefore `x_{t+1}` is adjacent to `f`."
Only the common neighbour furnished by this paragraph is retained.

links.rationale: Step within claim (3) of 21.2's proof (p. 132): the minimality of F gives y a unique neighbour f in F, forcing R to have length 2 and x_{t+1} adjacent to f.

decls.docstring:

links.rationale: Step within the proof of claim (3) of 21.2 (p. 132): the common neighbour f has no neighbour in A_{t-1}, since x_{t+1}-f would otherwise be a better path.

decls.name: goodPath_prepend_suffix
decls.docstring:
A replacement `x_{t+1}-f-p_j-⋯-p_m`, with `j ≥ 2`, remains a good path

links.rationale: A replacement path x_{t+1}-f-p_j-⋯-p_m, with j ≥ 2, remains a good path when p_j is the last neighbour of f on the old path.

decls.name: claim3_common_neighbor_avoids_tail
decls.docstring:
PAPER (21.2(3), p. 132): "`f` is nonadjacent to `p₂,…,p_m`, since
otherwise there would be a better choice of path using `f`."

links.rationale: Step within the proof of claim (3) of 21.2 (p. 132): f is nonadjacent to p_2,…,p_m, since otherwise a better choice of path using f would exist.

decls.name: claim3_counterexample_reflection_gap
decls.docstring:
**Labelled gap for the counterexample argument in Claim (3)** (printed pp. 132–133).

PAPER: *"For suppose some `y ∈ Y` has no such neighbour. ... Consequently,
`{z,y,x,p₂,…,p_m} ∪ A_{t−1}` catches the triangle `{x_{t+1},f,p₁}`. ... By 17.1,
`F'` contains a reflection of the triangle ... a contradiction.  This proves (3)."*

The conclusion is stated as the impossibility of the single counterexample `y`.  Thus the gap
contains exactly the minimal-connected-set, antipath, and final reflection argument in that
quoted paragraph; the outer quantifier bookkeeping remains in `claim3`.

links.rationale: Step within claim (3) of 21.2's proof (pp. 132-133): the connected set {z,y,x,p_2,…,p_m} ∪ A_{t-1} catches the triangle {x_{t+1},f,p_1}, and 17.1's reflection gives the contradiction proving (3).

decls.name: claim3

**Claim (3)** of the printed proof (printed pp. 132–133): *"Every vertex in `Y` has a
neighbour in `A_{t−1} ∪ {x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_m}`."*

links.rationale: Proves claim (3) of the printed proof of 21.2 (pp. 132-133): every vertex of Y has a neighbour in A_{t-1} ∪ {x_{t+1}, p_1,…,p_m}.

decls.docstring:
The path `z-x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_k` has the common hypotheses of 21.1
when `p_k` is the first `X_{t-1}`-complete vertex after `z`.

links.rationale: The prefix path z-x_{t+1}-p_1-⋯-p_k satisfies the common hypotheses of 21.1 when p_k is the first X_{t-1}-complete vertex after z.

decls.name: OddReturnPaths
decls.docstring:
PAPER (21.2(5), pp. 133–134): the odd return paths from `x_t` to the
first `X_{t-1}`-complete vertex.

links.rationale: Auxiliary declaration for 21.2's proof: the odd return paths from x_t to the first X_{t-1}-complete vertex (claim (5), pp. 133-134).

decls.name: extended_index_odd
decls.docstring:
PAPER (21.2(4), p. 133): "`z-x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_i-x_s-z` is a hole ...
and so `i` is odd." This part uses only the induced path and the choice of `s`.

links.rationale: Step within claim (4) of 21.2's proof (p. 133): the hole z-x_{t+1}-p_1-⋯-p_i-x_s-z forces the index i to be odd.

decls.name: claim4_hat_outcome
decls.docstring:
Shared hole construction for the hat argument of 21.2(4), printed p. 133.

PAPER: *"let `p_i-r₁-⋯-r_k-y` be a path from `p_i` to `y` with interior in
`A_{t−1} ∪ {p_{i+1},…,p_m}`.  Then `z-x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_i-r₁-⋯-r_k-y-z` is a hole of length `≥ 6`,
and the only `X_t`-complete vertices in this hole are `z, y`.  By 2.10 `X_t` contains a hat or
a leap for this hole."*

The conclusion packages the outcome of 2.10 for `J = min(i, m)`: some `x_j ∈ X_t` has no
neighbour in `{x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_J}`, and moreover either it also misses the whole connecting
path `r₁-⋯-r_k` (the hat case) or some member of `X_t` is adjacent to `x_{t+1}` and not to
`p_J` (the leap case).

links.rationale: Step within claim (4) of 21.2's proof (p. 133): the path p_i-r_1-⋯-r_k-y closes the hole z-x_{t+1}-p_1-⋯-p_i-r_1-⋯-r_k-y-z, to which 2.10 applies, giving a hat or leap in X_t.

decls.name: claim4_hat_large_index_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for the **second** case of the hat argument of 21.2(4), printed p. 133.

PAPER: *"Now suppose that `i > m`, and so `s = t`.  Let `p_m-r₁-⋯-r_k-y` be a path from `p_m`
to `y` with interior in `A_{t−1}`.  Again, `z-x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_m-r₁-⋯-r_k-y-z` is a hole of
length `≥ 6`, and its only `X_t`-complete vertices are `z, y`.  By 2.10 `X_t` contains a hat or
leap.  By (1) it contains no leap, so there exists `x ∈ X_t` nonadjacent to all
`x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_m, r₁,…,r_k`.  Since `p_m` is `X_{t−1}`-complete, it follows that `x = x_t`.
Now `{x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_i, r₁,…,r_k}` (`= F` say) is connected, and catches the triangle
`{y, z, x_t}`; the only neighbour of `z` in `F` is `x_{t+1}`; the only neighbour of `y` in `F`
is `r_k` (because `y` is nonadjacent to `x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_i`); and the only neighbour of `x_t`
in `F` is `p_i` (because `x_t` is a hat).  Since `x_{t+1}` is not adjacent to `p_i`, this
contradicts 17.1."*

The hypothesis `hbig` is the printed *"suppose that `i > m`"*; the case `i ≤ m` of the same
paragraph is proved in `claim4_hat_gap`.

links.rationale: Step within claim (4) of 21.2's proof (p. 133): the large-index case i > m, where the hat y is reached from p_m and 17.1 applied to the connected catching set F gives the contradiction.

decls.name: claim4_hat_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for the *hat* case of 21.2(4), p. 133.

PAPER: *"So `Y` contains a hat, that is, there exists `y ∈ Y` nonadjacent to
`x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_i`.  By (3), `y` has a neighbour in `A_{t−1} ∪ {p_j : i+1 ≤ j ≤ m}`.
Suppose first that `i ≤ m`, and let `p_i-r₁-⋯-r_k-y` be a path from `p_i` to `y` with interior
in `A_{t−1} ∪ {p_{i+1},…,p_m}`.  Then `z-x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_i-r₁-⋯-r_k-y-z` is a hole of length
`≥ 6`, and the only `X_t`-complete vertices in this hole are `z, y`. … so some `x ∈ X_t` has
no neighbour in `{x_{t+1},p₁,…,p_i}`, contrary to the choice of `i`.  Now suppose that
`i > m`, and so `s = t`. … Since `x_{t+1}` is not adjacent to `p_i`, this contradicts 17.1.
This proves (4)."*

`hyp` is *"`y` is nonadjacent to `p₁,…,p_i`"* (the entries of `q.take i` are `p₁,…,p_i`).

links.rationale: Step within claim (4) of 21.2's proof (p. 133): the hat y ∈ Y produces, via the small- and large-index cases, a hole of length ≥ 6 whose X_t-completeness forces a contradiction with 17.1.

decls.name: endgame_claim4_hub_complete_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for the second assertion of 21.2(4), p. 133.
PAPER: "Suppose `p_i` is not `Y`-complete ... This proves (4)."
The remaining argument excludes the leap and the two hat cases.

links.rationale: Discharges claim (4) of 21.2's proof (p. 133): if p_i were not Y-complete, 2.10 forces a leap or hat in the hole C, and both alternatives lead to a contradiction (via 13.6, resp. 17.1).

decls.name: endgame_claim4_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for 21.2(4), p. 133.
PAPER: "`i` is odd, and `p_i` is `Y`-complete."
The hole, hat, and leap argument in that claim proves these two assertions.

links.rationale: States claim (4) of 21.2's printed proof (p. 133): i is odd, and p_i is Y-complete; discharged by the hole/hat/leap argument.

decls.name: claim5_even_middle_in_path
decls.docstring:
The first case of the middle-vertex analysis in the proof of 21.2(5), printed p. 133.

PAPER: *"Suppose first that `q ∈ {p₁,…,p_m}`; then it follows that `q = p_{m−1}`.  Hence
`q-Q-x_t-p_m` is an even antipath of length `≥ 4`; `q` is its only vertex that is anticomplete
to `A_{t−1}`, and `p_m` is its only vertex that is anticomplete to
`{z, x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_{m−2}}`.  Since the sets `A_{t−1}`, `{z, x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_{m−2}}` are each
connected and anticomplete to each other, this contradicts 13.7 applied in `Ḡ`."*

Here `qm` is the paper's `q`, `pm` its `p_m`, and `Q` the odd antipath produced by 13.6.

links.rationale: Step within claim (5) of 21.2's proof (p. 133): when the middle vertex q of R lies among p_1,…,p_m, it must equal p_{m-1}, and the resulting even antipath contradicts 13.7 in the complement.

decls.name: claim5_even_middle_in_A_gap
decls.docstring:
The second case of the middle-vertex analysis in the proof of 21.2(5), printed p. 134.

PAPER: *"So `q ∈ A_{t−1}`, and in particular `x_t` is nonadjacent to `p_m, p_{m−1}`.  Let `R'`
be a path between `x_t, p_m` with interior in `{z, x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_m}`; then
`x_t-R-p_m-R'-x_t` is a hole of length `≥ 6` sharing the vertices `x_t, q, p_m` with the
antihole `q-Q-x_t-p_m-z-q`, contrary to 15.7."*

Here `qm` is the paper's `q`, `pm` its `p_m`, and `Q` the odd antipath produced by 13.6.  The
companion case `q ∈ {p₁,…,p_m}` is discharged by `claim5_even_middle_in_path`.

Two remarks on the printed argument.  First, *"a hole of length ≥ 6"* is exactly *"`R'` has
length ≥ 3"*, and the only middle vertices a length-2 `R'` could have are `p_{m−1}` and
`x_{t+1}`.  The first is excluded by the printed remark *"and in particular `x_t` is
nonadjacent to `p_m, p_{m−1}`"*, which is proved here without circularity: `x_t ∼ p_{m−1}`
makes `z-x_t-p_{m−1}-p_m` an odd path whose ends are `X_{t−1}`-complete and whose internal
vertices are not, so 13.6 (`Thm212Claim5Antipath.exists_odd_antipath`) yields an odd antipath
between `x_t` and `p_{m−1}` with interior in `X_{t−1}`, and `claim5_even_middle_in_path`
applies to it.  Second, the vertex `x_{t+1}` is a possible middle vertex only when `m = 1` and
`x_t` is adjacent to `x_{t+1}`, which is why the hypothesis `hc2` — claim (2) of the printed
proof, available at this point of the paper — is needed: with `m = 1` the vertex `x_s` it
provides is nonadjacent to `p₁ = p_m`, which is `X_{t−1}`-complete, so `s = t` and
`x_t` is nonadjacent to `x_{t+1}`.

links.rationale: Step within claim (5) of 21.2's proof (p. 134): when the middle vertex q of R lies in A_{t-1}, the hole x_t-R-p_m-R'-x_t shares three vertices with the antihole q-Q-x_t-p_m-z-q, contrary to 15.7.

decls.name: claim5_odd_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for the parity assertion of 21.2(5), pp. 133–134.

PAPER: *"Let `R` be a path from `x_t` to some vertex `r`, such that `r` is the unique
`X_{t−1}`-complete vertex in `R`, and `V(R \ x_t) ⊆ A_{t−1} ∪ {p₁,…,p_m}`.  Then `R` is odd
… For assume that `R` is even.  Then the path `z-x_t-R-r` is odd, and its ends are
`X_{t−1}`-complete, and its internal vertices are not, so by 13.6, it has length 3, that is,
`R` has length 2.  Let `q` be the middle vertex of `R`. … Suppose first that
`q ∈ {p₁,…,p_m}`; then it follows that `q = p_{m−1}` … contradicts 13.7 applied in the
complement.  So `q ∈ A_{t−1}` … contrary to 15.7.  So `R` is odd."*

links.rationale: Proves the second half of claim (5) of 21.2's proof (p. 133): the path R from x_t to the first X_{t-1}-complete vertex r is odd, using 13.6, 13.7 and 15.7.

decls.name: endgame_claim5_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for 21.2(5), pp. 133–134.
PAPER: "Then `R` is odd, and has length ≥ 3." The argument uses 13.6,
13.7 in the complement, and the hole–antihole intersection bound 15.7.

links.rationale: Discharges claim (5) of 21.2's proof (p. 133): the path R from x_t to the first X_{t-1}-complete vertex has length ≥ 3.

decls.name: claim6_hub_not_complete_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for the last part of 21.2(6), printed p. 134.

PAPER: *"Now assume that `x_{t+1}` is `X_{t−1}`-complete.  Since `x_{t+1}` is nonadjacent to
`x_s` it follows `s = t`.  Let `R` be a path between `x_t, p_m` with interior in `A_{t−1}`.
By (5), `R` is odd, and so the path `x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_i-x_t-R-p_m` is odd, of length `≥ 5`, its
ends are `X_{t−1}`-complete, and its internal vertices are not, contrary to 13.6."*

`hnone` is the first half of (6), already proved: none of `p₁,…,p_{i−1}` (the entries
`q[l]` with `l + 2 ≤ i`) is `X_{t−1}`-complete.

links.rationale: Step within claim (6) of 21.2's proof (p. 134): if x_{t+1} were X_{t-1}-complete, the odd path x_{t+1}-p_1-⋯-p_i-x_t-R-p_m would contradict 13.6.

decls.name: endgame_claim6_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for 21.2(6), p. 134.
PAPER: "We may assume that none of `x_{t+1},p₁,…,p_{i-1}` is
`X_{t-1}`-complete, and in particular `i ≤ m`."
The discarded case supplies 21.1's first alternative on the reversed path
`z-x_t-p_i-⋯-p_h`, which is the witness on the left.

links.rationale: Discharges claim (6) of 21.2's proof (p. 134): none of x_{t+1},p_1,…,p_{i-1} is X_{t-1}-complete, so in particular i ≤ m.

decls.name: claim8_count
decls.docstring:
The counting-and-17.1 half of 21.2(8), printed p. 134.

PAPER: *"The path `z-x_t-S-p_k` is odd, and its ends are `X_{t−1}`-complete, so by 2.3 it
contains an odd number of `X_{t−1}`-complete edges.  Since `x_t` is not `X_{t−1}`-complete, all
these `X_{t−1}`-complete edges belong to `S` and hence to `C`, and there are no further
`X_{t−1}`-complete edges in `C`.  Thus an odd number of edges of `C` are `X_{t−1}`-complete,
and so by 2.3 there is exactly one, and exactly two `X_{t−1}`-complete vertices.  Since `p_k`
is `X_{t−1}`-complete, the second such vertex is the neighbour of `p_k` in `S`.  This therefore
does not belong to `A_{t−1}`, and so `k < m`, and `p_{k+1}` is the second `X_{t−1}`-complete
vertex of `C`.  By 2.10 applied to `C`, `X_{t−1}` contains a leap or hat, and in either case
some `x ∈ X_{t−1}` is nonadjacent to all of `x_t, x_{t+1}, p₁`, and adjacent to `p_k`.  Hence
`(V(C) \ {x_t, x_{t+1}}) ∪ {x}` (`= F` say) catches the triangle `{z, x_t, x_{t+1}}`; the only
neighbour of `z` in `F` is `x`; the only neighbour of `x_{t+1}` in `F` is `p₁`; and `x, p₁` are
nonadjacent, and are both nonadjacent to `x_t`, contrary to 17.1."*

The hole `C` of the paper is the list `S ++ (x_{t+1} :: p₁-⋯-p_{k−1}).reverse`, i.e. the cycle
`x_t-x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_k-S-x_t` read from `x_t` along `S` first.  `hSc` is the sentence *"by (5),
some internal vertex of `S` is `X_{t−1}`-complete"*, which is proved in `claim8_hole_gap`.

links.rationale: Step within claim (8) of 21.2's proof (p. 134): parity counting on C and 2.10 produce a vertex x ∈ X_{t-1} whose catching set F contradicts 17.1.

decls.name: claim8_hole_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for the hole argument inside 21.2(8), printed p. 134.

PAPER: *"Let `S` be a path between `x_t, p_k` with interior in `A_{t−1} ∪ {p_{k+1},…,p_m}`,
and let `C` be the hole `x_t-x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_k-S-x_t`.  Since `C` is even and `k` is odd, it
follows that `S` is even, and so by (5), some internal vertex of `S` is `X_{t−1}`-complete.
The path `z-x_t-S-p_k` is odd, and its ends are `X_{t−1}`-complete, so by 2.3 it contains an
odd number of `X_{t−1}`-complete edges. … By 2.10 applied to `C`, `X_{t−1}` contains a leap or
hat, and in either case some `x ∈ X_{t−1}` is nonadjacent to all of `x_t, x_{t+1}, p₁`, and
adjacent to `p_k`.  Hence `(V(C) \ {x_t, x_{t+1}}) ∪ {x}` (`= F` say) catches the triangle
`{z, x_t, x_{t+1}}`; the only neighbour of `z` in `F` is `x`; the only neighbour of `x_{t+1}`
in `F` is `p₁`; and `x, p₁` are nonadjacent, and are both nonadjacent to `x_t`, contrary to
17.1."*

`hnone` is the assumption for contradiction of (8), and `hadj` is the sentence *"From the
definition of `i` it follows that `x_t` is adjacent to `x_{t+1}`"*, which is proved below.

links.rationale: Step within claim (8) of 21.2's proof (p. 134): builds the hole C = x_t-x_{t+1}-p_1-⋯-p_k-S-x_t and, via 2.10 and 17.1, derives the contradiction proving (8).

decls.name: endgame_claim8_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for 21.2(8), p. 134.
PAPER: "`x_t` is adjacent to one of `p₁,…,p_k`."
Here `p_k` is the first complete vertex, and the prefix has even length by (7).

links.rationale: Discharges claim (8) of 21.2's proof (p. 134): x_t is adjacent to one of p_1,…,p_k.

decls.name: parity_oddRun_gap
decls.docstring:
Labelled gap for the edge count in 21.2's final paragraph, printed p. 135.

PAPER: *"So we may assume that `p_j` is not `Y`-complete.  Now the path `x_t-p_j-⋯-p_k` has odd
length `≥ 3`, and both its ends are `Y`-complete, and the `Y`-complete vertex `z` has no
neighbour in its interior, so by 2.2 and 2.3, an odd number of its edges are `Y`-complete.
Since `p_j` is not `Y`-complete, an odd number of edges of `p_j-⋯-p_k` are `Y`-complete.  The
path `z-x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_k` (`= P` say) is even, by (7), and since its ends are `Y`-complete, it
follows that an even number of its edges are `Y`-complete, by 2.3.  We deduce that an odd
number of edges of `z-x_{t+1}-p₁-⋯-p_j` are `Y`-complete.  There is therefore a `Y`-segment
`P'` of this path that has odd length.  Since `p_j` is not `Y`-complete, it follows that `P'`
is also a `Y`-segment of `P`."*

The paper's `p_j` is the entry `p[J]` with `J = j - 1`; `hJmax` is the maximality of `j`,
`hJodd` is *"`k − j` is even"* from (5), and the conclusion is the `Y`-segment `P'`, which
`Thm212EndgameTools.alternatives_of_oddRun` then feeds to 21.1.

links.rationale: Step in the final paragraph of 21.2's proof (p. 135): parity counting on x_t-p_j-⋯-p_k and z-x_{t+1}-p_1-⋯-p_k shows P' is also a Y-segment of the full path P.

decls.name: endgame
decls.docstring:
**Claims (4)–(9) and the concluding paragraph** (printed pp. 133–135), which between them
produce the wheel with hub `Y`:

*"(4) `i` is odd, and `pᵢ` is `Y`-complete.  (5) Let `R` be a path from `x_t` to some vertex
`r`, such that `r` is the unique `X_{t−1}`-complete vertex in `R`, and
`V(R \ x_t) ⊆ A_{t−1} ∪ {p₁,…,p_m}`.  Then `R` is odd, and has length ≥ 3. …  (6) We may assume
that none of `x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_{i−1}` is `X_{t−1}`-complete, and in particular `i ≤ m`. …
(7) None of `x_{t+1}, p₁,…,p_{k−1}` is `X_{t−1}`-complete, and `k` is odd.  (8) `x_t` is
adjacent to one of `p₁,…,p_k`.  (9) `p_k` is `Y`-complete. …  and again 21.1 applied to `P`
implies there is a wheel with hub `Y`.  This proves 21.2."*

links.rationale: Carries out claims (4)-(9) and the concluding paragraph of the printed proof of 21.2 (pp. 133-135), producing the wheel with hub Y via 21.1. The anchor quote is claim (4) alone; endgame_claim4_gap already states that printed step verbatim, so this entry is a packaged/aggregate form covering the remaining claims and the closing paragraph, not an independent anchor to (4).

decls.name: wheel_of_r_eq_one
decls.docstring:
**"By 19.2, `r > 1`."**  If the minimal `r` were `1`, then `x₀, x₁, x_{t+1}` is a wheel system
of height `2` to which 19.2 applies — its hypothesis *"every `y ∈ Y` nonadjacent to `x₂` has a
neighbour in `A₁`, and is adjacent to `z`"* is exactly what the hypothesis of 21.3 gives at `r = 1`
together with `z` being `Y`-complete — and 19.2 produces a wheel with hub `Y`.

links.rationale: Step within 21.3's proof (p. 135): by 19.2, the minimal r cannot be 1, since x_0,x_1,x_{t+1} would then be a height-2 wheel system to which 19.2 directly applies, producing the wheel.

decls.name: nbr_in_prev
decls.docstring:
**"it follows from 21.2 that `x_{t+1}` has a neighbour in `A_{r−1}`"**.  Applied to the wheel
system `x₀,…,x_r,x_{t+1}` (whose height is `r+1`, so 21.2 is used with its `t` equal to `r`):
if `x_{t+1}` had no neighbour in `A_{r−1}` then, since at most one member of `Y` has no neighbour
in `A_{r−1} ∪ {x_{t+1}}` (because at most one has no neighbour in `A₁ ⊆ A_{r−1}`) and any such
member has a neighbour in `A_r` (by the hypothesis of 21.3 at `r`), 21.2 would give a wheel with
hub `Y`.

links.rationale: Step within 21.3's proof (p. 135): 21.2, applied to the wheel system x_0,…,x_r,x_{t+1} with t = r, gives x_{t+1} a neighbour in A_{r-1}.

decls.name: not_complete_prev
decls.docstring:
**"Since no wheel has hub `Y`, 20.1 implies that `x₀,…,x_r,x_{t+1}` is not a `Y`-diamond, and
so `x_{t+1}` is not `X_{r−1}`-complete."**  All the other clauses of the definition of a
`Y`-diamond are already available for `x₀,…,x_r,x_{t+1}` — the height is `r+1 ≥ 3`, `Y` is a hub
for it, and by the previous step `x_{t+1}` has a neighbour in `A_{r−1}` — so `X_{r−1}`-completeness
of `x_{t+1}` is the only thing that could still be missing.

links.rationale: Step within 21.3's proof (p. 135): since no wheel has hub Y, 20.1 rules out x_0,…,x_r,x_{t+1} being a Y-diamond, forcing x_{t+1} to fail X_{r-1}-completeness.
