decls.name: rev_get
decls.docstring:
**The prefix-jump contradiction.**

PAPER (proof of 6.1(9), printed p. 32): *"Hence the track `T` with edge-set
`{h₁, …, h_{i-1}, f}` has even length, at least 4 …; and yet in `G` the `Y'`-complete vertex
`h_{n-1}` has no neighbour in the interior of the odd path `L(T)`, contrary to 2.2."*

Used twice: once with `z = pⱼ` (both ends of `f` on `P`), and once with `z` the end of `f` off
`P` (the paragraph *"In `G`, `h₁-⋯-h_{i-1}-f` is a path; … so by 2.2, this path is even"*). -/
private theorem prefix_jump_contra (hG : Berge G)
    (Y2 : Set V) (hanti : AnticonnectedSet G Y2) (hYK : ∀ y ∈ Y2, y ∉ K)
    (P : List (Fin n)) (hP : IsTrackList H P) (hPlen : 5 ≤ P.length)
    (he0 : s(P[0]'(by omega), P[1]'(by omega)) ∈ completeEdges G H K φ Y2)
    (hel : s(P[P.length - 2]'(by omega), P[P.length - 1]'(by omega))
      ∈ completeEdges G H K φ Y2)
    (hint : ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → ∀ _hm : m + 2 < P.length,
      s(P[m]'(by omega), P[m + 1]'(by omega)) ∉ completeEdges G H K φ Y2)
    (a : ℕ) (ha3 : 3 ≤ a) (haodd : a % 2 = 1) (haP : a + 3 ≤ P.length)
    (z : Fin n) (hadj : H.Adj (P[a]'(by omega)) z)
    (hz : ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ _hk : k < P.length, k ≤ a → P[k]'(by omega) ≠ z)
    (hfz : s(P[a]'(by omega), z) ∈ completeEdges G H K φ Y2) : False := by
  classical
  have hnd : P.Nodup := hP.2.1
  have hslen : (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a).length = a + 1 := by
    have := TrackSlice.length_slice P (show a < P.length by omega) (Nat.zero_le a)
    omega
  have hsget : ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : k < (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a).length) (hk' : k < P.length),
      (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a)[k]'hk = P[k]'hk' := by
    intro k hk hk'
    rw [TrackSlice.getElem_slice P hk (show 0 + k < P.length by omega)]
    exact geq P (by omega) _ _
  have hsfrom : IsTrackFrom H (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a) (P[0]'(by omega)) (P[a]'(by omega)) :=
    TrackSlice.isTrackFrom_slice hP (show a < P.length by omega) (Nat.zero_le a)
  have hznot : z ∉ TrackSlice.slice P 0 a := by
    intro hzs
    obtain ⟨k, hk, hkz⟩ := List.mem_iff_getElem.mp hzs
    exact hz k (by omega) (by omega) ((hsget k hk (by omega)).symm.trans hkz)
  have hTfrom : IsTrackFrom H (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z]) (P[0]'(by omega)) z :=
    TrackSlice.isTrackFrom_concat hsfrom hadj hznot
  have hTlen : (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z]).length = a + 2 := by
    simp only [List.length_append, List.length_cons, List.length_nil, hslen]
  have hTget : ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : k < (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z]).length)
      (hk' : k < P.length), k ≤ a → (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z])[k]'hk = P[k]'hk' := by
    intro k hk hk' hka
    rw [List.getElem_append_left (show k < (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a).length by omega)]
    exact hsget k (by omega) hk'
  have hTlast : (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z])[a + 1]'(by omega) = z := by
    rw [List.getElem_append_right (show (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a).length ≤ a + 1 by omega)]
    simp only [hslen]
    norm_num
  refine far_edge_contra hG Y2 hanti hYK (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z]) hTfrom.1
    (by omega) (by omega) ?_ ?_ ?_
    (s(P[P.length - 2]'(by omega), P[P.length - 1]'(by omega))) hel ?_
  · rw [hTget 0 (by omega) (by omega) (by omega), hTget 1 (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)]
    exact he0
  · rw [geq (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z])
        (show (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z]).length - 2 = a by omega) (by omega) (by omega),
      geq (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z])
        (show (TrackSlice.slice P 0 a ++ [z]).length - 1 = a + 1 by omega) (by omega) (by omega),
      hTget a (by omega) (by omega) (by omega), hTlast]
    exact hfz
  · intro m hm1 hm2
    rw [hTget m (by omega) (by omega) (by omega),
      hTget (m + 1) (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)]
    exact hint m hm1 (by omega)
  · intro m hm1 hm2 hmeet
    rw [hTget m (by omega) (by omega) (by omega),
      hTget (m + 1) (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)] at hmeet
    have hmeet' : MeetEdges (s(P[P.length - 2]'(by omega), P[(P.length - 2) + 1]'(by omega)))
        (s(P[m]'(by omega), P[m + 1]'(by omega))) := by
      rw [geq P (show (P.length - 2) + 1 = P.length - 1 by omega)
        (show (P.length - 2) + 1 < P.length by omega) (show P.length - 1 < P.length by omega)]
      exact hmeet
    have := meet_indices hnd (show P.length - 2 + 1 < P.length by omega)
      (show m + 1 < P.length by omega) hmeet'
    omega

decls.name: prefix_sub_contra
decls.docstring:
**The suffix-jump contradiction** — `prefix_jump_contra` read on the reversed track. -/
private theorem suffix_jump_contra (hG : Berge G)
    (Y2 : Set V) (hanti : AnticonnectedSet G Y2) (hYK : ∀ y ∈ Y2, y ∉ K)
    (P : List (Fin n)) (hP : IsTrackList H P) (hPlen : 5 ≤ P.length)
    (he0 : s(P[0]'(by omega), P[1]'(by omega)) ∈ completeEdges G H K φ Y2)
    (hel : s(P[P.length - 2]'(by omega), P[P.length - 1]'(by omega))
      ∈ completeEdges G H K φ Y2)
    (hint : ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → ∀ _hm : m + 2 < P.length,
      s(P[m]'(by omega), P[m + 1]'(by omega)) ∉ completeEdges G H K φ Y2)
    (b : ℕ) (hb : b + 4 ≤ P.length) (hb2 : 2 ≤ b)
    (hbodd : (P.length - 1 - b) % 2 = 1)
    (z : Fin n) (hadj : H.Adj (P[b]'(by omega)) z)
    (hz : ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ _hk : k < P.length, b ≤ k → P[k]'(by omega) ≠ z)
    (hfz : s(P[b]'(by omega), z) ∈ completeEdges G H K φ Y2) : False := by
  have hrlen : P.reverse.length = P.length := by simp
  obtain ⟨hRT, hRlen, hRe0, hRel, hRint⟩ := rev_pkg Y2 P hP hPlen he0 hel hint
  have hRb : P.reverse[P.length - 1 - b]'(by simp only [List.length_reverse]; omega)
      = P[b]'(by omega) := by
    rw [rev_get P (by simp only [List.length_reverse]; omega)
      (show P.length - 1 - (P.length - 1 - b) < P.length by omega)]
    exact geq P (by omega) _ _
  refine prefix_jump_contra hG Y2 hanti hYK P.reverse hRT hRlen hRe0 hRel hRint
    (P.length - 1 - b) (by omega) hbodd (by omega) z ?_ ?_ ?_
  · rw [hRb]; exact hadj
  · intro k hk hka
    rw [rev_get P hk (show P.length - 1 - k < P.length by omega)]
    exact hz (P.length - 1 - k) (by omega) (by simp only [List.length_reverse] at hk; omega)
  · rw [hRb]; exact hfz

decls.name: external_edge_meets_branch_only_at_ends
decls.docstring:
An edge outside a branch cannot meet it at an internal vertex: that would make the
internal vertex have degree at least three.

links.rationale: An edge outside a branch cannot meet it at an internal vertex, since that would give the internal vertex degree at least three; general subdivision-theory fact.

decls.name: external_edge_inter_branch_only_at_ends
decls.docstring:
A convenient vertex version of `external_edge_meets_branch_only_at_ends`: every
intersection of an external edge with a nontrivial branch is one of the named ends.

links.rationale: Vertex version of external_edge_meets_branch_only_at_ends: every intersection of an external edge with a nontrivial branch is one of the branch's named ends.

decls.name: edge_track_from_incident
decls.docstring: The two-vertex list associated with an edge at `a`, with the edge itself remembered.

decls.name: branchChoice_basic

decls.name: branch_edge_avoids_other_branchVertex
decls.docstring: A branch edge avoids every branch-vertex other than the two ends of the branch.

decls.name: branch_length_one_of_adj

decls.name: trackEdges_eq_singleton_of_length_one

decls.name: trackLength_le_two_of_end_edges_meet
decls.docstring: If the end-edges of a nontrivial track meet, the track has at most two edges.

links.rationale: If the end-edges of a nontrivial track meet, the track has at most two edges; elementary track bookkeeping fact.

decls.name: other_incident_edges_subsingleton
decls.docstring:
Suppose that `d₁,d₂` are the two displayed edges at `v`, joining it respectively to
`b₁,b₂`, while `b-b₂-v` is a two-edge path.  If every further edge at `v` meets the first
edge `e₃` of a branch from `b` to `b₃`, then there is at most one such further edge.

This is the elementary bipartite/branch-theoretic content of the sentence in (12) saying
that all further edges at `v` are incident with `b₃`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the elementary bipartite/branch-theoretic content of the sentence in claim (12) that all further edges at v are incident with b₃: at most one further edge at v can meet the first edge e₃ of the branch from b to b₃.

decls.name: identify_cross_meeting
decls.docstring:
The basic branch-identification move used in (11): an edge at the far end of one branch
which meets the first edge of another branch must join the two far ends, and the latter branch
has length one.

links.rationale: The basic branch-identification move used in claim (11): an edge at the far end of one branch meeting the first edge of another branch must join the two far ends, forcing the latter branch to have length one.

decls.name: claim11_failure_shape
decls.docstring:
If the first half of (11) failed, the unique complete edge at `b₁` would be `b₁b₃`,
`B₃` would have length one, and `B₁` would have length at least two.  This is the first
paragraph of the printed proof of (11), before it invokes maximality.

links.rationale: Formalizes the first paragraph of the printed proof of claim (11), before it invokes maximality: if the first half of (11) failed, the unique complete edge at b₁ would be b₁b₃, B₃ would have length one, and B₁ would have length at least two.

decls.name: other_incident_is_complete
decls.docstring:
At the centre of a branch choice, every incident edge other than the distinguished
`X₁`- and `X₂`-edges is in `X`.

links.rationale: At the centre of a branch choice, every incident edge other than the distinguished X₁- and X₂-edges lies in X; bookkeeping fact about the chosen configuration.

decls.name: original_degree_le_subdivision_degree
decls.docstring:

subdividing tracks.

links.rationale: Subdivision preserves the degree of an old vertex in the direction needed by the endgame: distinct neighbours in the original graph yield distinct first neighbours on the subdividing tracks.

decls.name: original_adj_of_branch_ends

decls.name: four_vertices_of_two_degree_three

decls.name: subdivision_track_length_two_of_adj

decls.name: subdivision_track_isBranch

decls.name: iso_top_of_four_vertices

decls.name: six_vertices_of_alternating_degree_three_cycle

four-cycle as a closed connected component, so there can be no further vertex.

links.rationale: Four degree-three vertices forming a cycle whose third neighbours alternate between two further vertices exhaust a 3-connected graph; used to bound the size of the small configurations 6.1 produces.

decls.name: claim12_v_eq_b3_conclusion
decls.docstring:
The first terminal case of 6.1(12), exactly the paper sentence:

> *"If `v = b₃`, then `B₃` has length 2 and both its edges belong to `X`, and the fourth
> outcome of the theorem holds."*

The preceding helper `claim12_v_eq_b3_short_complete` proves the first two clauses.  The open
part is the cardinal count and the identification of the original graph with `K₄`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the first terminal case of claim (12)'s proof verbatim (v = b₃): completes the cardinal count and identification of H with K₄ that the preceding helper claim12_v_eq_b3_short_complete leaves open.

decls.name: claim12_degree_three_conclusion
decls.docstring:
The degree-three terminal case of 6.1(12), exactly the paper sentence:

> *"If `v ≠ b₃` and `v` has degree 3, then the third edge incident with `v` is `vb₃`, and `b`
> is a triad, and `H` consists of the vertices `b,b₁,b₂,b₃,v` and a branch `B` with ends `b₃`
> and `u`; but then `J = K₃,₃`, and if `B` has length 1 then the second outcome of the theorem
> holds, and otherwise the first outcome holds."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the degree-three terminal case of claim (12)'s proof verbatim: when v ≠ b₃ has degree 3, H consists of five named vertices and a branch B, forcing J = K₃,₃ and the first or second outcome of the theorem.

decls.name: even_final_claim13
decls.docstring:
The bridging paragraph and claim (13), starting with the oriented parity choice
`B₁` even and `B₂` odd.  The conclusion records the branch `B₄` introduced by the paper and
the four assertions of (13).

links.rationale: Proves claim (13) of the printed proof of 6.1, starting from the oriented parity choice (B₁ even, B₂ odd): b₄ = b₃, B₃ has length 1, H is a subdivision of K₄, and B₄ is even.

decls.name: even_final_closing
decls.docstring:
The closing paragraph after 6.1(13), exactly from *"Let `B₅` be the branch of `H` between
`b₁,b₃`"* through *"But then the fourth outcome of the theorem holds. This proves 6.1."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the closing paragraph of the printed proof of 6.1, from the introduction of branch B₅ through "But then the fourth outcome of the theorem holds. This proves 6.1."

decls.name: even_final_oriented
decls.docstring: The oriented form of the final even-case argument.

links.rationale: The oriented form of the final even-case argument (fixing which of B₁, B₂ is even); assembly step combining even_final_claim13 and even_final_closing, no standalone paper quote of its own.

decls.name: BranchChoiceMaximal
decls.docstring:
**The refinement of the choice of `b`** (printed p. 32, preceding (11)):

> *"Earlier (preceding (4)) we chose `b` such that at least two edges of `H` incident with `b`
> did not belong to `X`.  Let us refine this choice; now in addition we choose `b` such that
> `B₃` is as long as possible."*

`B₃` is as long as possible over **all** configurations, i.e. over all choices of `b`, of the
two edges `e₁ ∈ X₁`, `e₂ ∈ X₂` at `b`, and of the third edge `e₃` at `b` — this is the form the
printed proof of (11) uses when it says *"`b₂` and `B` contradict the choice of `b` and `B₃`"*,
where the competing configuration is centred at a different branch-vertex.

links.rationale: Names the printed refinement of the choice of b (preceding claim (11)): the configuration is additionally chosen so that B₃ is as long as possible.

decls.name: exists_maximal_branchChoice
decls.docstring:
**The configuration exists with `B₃` as long as possible** (printed p. 32, preceding (11)).

Existence of *some* configuration is `Thm61BranchChoice.exists_branchChoice`; the refinement is
then a maximum of a set of natural numbers which is nonempty and bounded above (every `B₃` is a
`Nodup` list of vertices of `H`, so `trackLength B₃ < n`).

links.rationale: Proves existence of the configuration with B₃ as long as possible (a maximum over a nonempty, bounded set of track lengths), witnessing the printed refinement of the choice of b.

decls.name: thm_6_1_claim_11
decls.docstring:
**6.1(11)** *"For `i = 1, 2` there is an edge `fᵢ ∈ X` incident with `bᵢ` that does not meet
`e₃`."*

links.rationale: States claim (11) of the printed proof of 6.1 verbatim.

decls.name: thm_6_1_claim_12
decls.docstring:
**6.1(12)** *"If there exist `f₁, f₂` as in (11) with `f₁, f₂ ≠ b₁b₂` then the theorem
holds."*

links.rationale: States claim (12) of the printed proof of 6.1 verbatim.

decls.name: branch_parity
decls.docstring:
**Exactly one of `B₁`, `B₂` is even, once `b₁b₂` is an edge.**

This is what licenses the unargued *"From the symmetry we may assume that `B₁` is even and `B₂`
is odd"* of the paragraph following (12).  `B₁`, followed by the edge `b₁b₂`, followed by the
reverse of `B₂`, is a cycle of `H` through `b` of length `trackLength B₁ + trackLength B₂ + 1`;
since `H` is bipartite that length is even, so `trackLength B₁ + trackLength B₂` is odd.

links.rationale: Proves exactly one of B₁, B₂ is even once b₁b₂ is an edge (via the cycle B₁-b₁b₂-B₂ and bipartiteness of H), which licenses the printed proof's unargued "from the symmetry we may assume B₁ is even and B₂ is odd"; supporting fact, not itself a printed sentence.

decls.name: thm_6_1_even_final
decls.docstring:
**6.1, even case: the bridging paragraph, claim (13) and the closing paragraph.**

> *"From (11) and (12) we may therefore assume that `b₁, b₂` are adjacent, and the edge
> `b₁b₂ ∈ X`.  From the symmetry we may assume that `B₁` is even and `B₂` is odd.  Let `T` be
> the track formed by `B₁` and the edges `e₃, b₁b₂` …"*

and everything down to *"But then the fourth outcome of the theorem holds.  This proves 6.1."*

The *"from the symmetry"* reduction is internal to this statement: exchanging the indices `1, 2`
exchanges `y₁, y₂` (reverse the antipath `Q`), `e₁, e₂`, `X₁, X₂`, `B₁, B₂` and `b₁, b₂`, and
`BranchChoice`, `BranchChoiceMaximal`, `Claim8` and `Claim9` are all invariant under that
exchange, while `Claim10` and the conclusion do not mention the indices at all.  `branch_parity`
supplies the parity dichotomy the symmetry is applied to.

links.rationale: Discharges the bridging paragraph, claim (13) and the closing paragraph of 6.1's proof (from the point where b₁b₂ ∈ X is assumed, down to "This proves 6.1"), with the printed 'from the symmetry' step handled internally.

decls.name: no_complete_left
decls.docstring:
The application of (10) in the bridging paragraph: a complete edge at `b₂`,
other than `b₁b₂` and missing `e₃`, forces `B₁` to have no complete edge.

links.rationale: The application of claim (10) in the bridging paragraph: a complete edge at b₂ other than b₁b₂ and missing e₃ forces B₁ to have no complete edge; proof step without a standalone quotable sentence.

decls.name: b2_triad
decls.docstring:
Printed bridging paragraph: "So there is no such edge `f`, and therefore `b₂` is a triad."
The supposed second complete edge first excludes complete edges on `B₁` by (10), then
contradicts (9) on `T`.

links.rationale: Formalizes a sentence of the bridging paragraph of 6.1's proof: a supposed second complete edge at b₂ is ruled out by (10) excluding complete edges on B₁ and then contradicting (9) on T, so b₂ is a triad.

decls.name: b2_short
decls.docstring:
The next bridging sentence: "Since it is not incident with `e₁`, it follows that
`E(B₂) = {e₂}`." Apply (8) to the `X₂` edge at the triad `b₂`; bipartiteness forces
its common end with `e₁` to be `b`.

links.rationale: Formalizes a sentence of the bridging paragraph of 6.1's proof: applying claim (8) to the X₂ edge at the triad b₂, bipartiteness forces its common end with e₁ to be b, so E(B₂) = {e₂}.

decls.name: not_triad_away
decls.docstring:
The opening of (13): "no edge in `X₂` is incident with `b₄`. Consequently `b₄`
is not a triad." The same argument works at any branch-vertex outside `b,b₁,b₂`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the opening of claim (13)'s proof at a general branch-vertex outside b, b₁, b₂: no X₂ edge is incident with it, so it is not a triad.

decls.name: no_extra2_away
decls.docstring: The edge form of the first assertion of (13): no `X₂` edge is incident with this branch-vertex.

links.rationale: The edge form of the first assertion of claim (13): no X₂ edge is incident with the branch-vertex under consideration; proof step feeding not_triad_away, no standalone quote.

decls.name: complete_at_fourth_meets
decls.docstring:
"By (10) (applied to three tracks with common end `b₂`), each of them meets either
`b₁b₂` or `e₃`." The three arms are `B₄` extended through the complete edge,
the edge `b₂b₁`, and the two-edge track through `b` and `e₃`.

links.rationale: Formalizes verbatim the sentence from claim (13)'s proof (6.1, printed p. 33): "By (10) (applied to three tracks with common end b₂), each of them meets either b₁b₂ or e₃." The three arms are B₄ extended through the complete edge, the edge b₂b₁, and the two-edge track through b and e₃.

decls.name: fourth_end_incident
decls.docstring:
The middle of (13): "So `b₄` is incident with `e₃`, that is, `b₄ = b₃` and `B₃`
has length 1." If `b₄` misses `e₃`, its complete edges force two adjacent degree-three
vertices with the same remaining neighbors. Cyclic 3-connectivity then excludes `b₃`.

links.rationale: Formalizes verbatim the middle sentence of claim (13)'s proof (6.1, printed p. 33): "So b₄ is incident with e₃, that is, b₄ = b₃ and B₃ has length 1." If b₄ misses e₃, its complete edges force two adjacent degree-three vertices with the same remaining neighbors; cyclic 3-connectivity then excludes b₃.

decls.name: even_final_claim13
decls.docstring: The bridge and all four assertions of printed claim (13).

links.rationale: Proves claim (13) of the printed proof of 6.1, starting from the oriented parity choice (B₁ even, B₂ odd): b₄ = b₃, B₃ has length 1, H is a subdivision of K₄, and B₄ is even. (Byte-identical duplicate of Workspace.ProofLemmas.Thm61EvenEndgameRemaining.even_final_claim13; same link.)

decls.name: even_final_closing
decls.docstring:

links.rationale: Formalizes the closing paragraph of the printed proof of 6.1, from the introduction of branch B₅ through "But then the fourth outcome of the theorem holds. This proves 6.1." (Byte-identical duplicate of Workspace.ProofLemmas.Thm61EvenEndgameRemaining.even_final_closing; same link.)

decls.name: exists_minimal_anticonnected_nonsaturating

**6.1, first sentence.**  *"We may assume that `Y` is minimal such that it is anticonnected
and its common neighbours do not saturate `L(H)`."*

subset of `Y₀` that is anticonnected *does* have a saturating set of common neighbours.

links.rationale: Discharges 6.1's opening reduction sentence: finds a minimal anticonnected `Y₀ ⊆ Y` whose common neighbours still fail to saturate `L(H)`, by finite-cardinality minimality.

decls.name: exists_track_of_branch
decls.docstring:
PAPER (printed pp. 19–20, used silently throughout §§5–8): **a branch of a subdivision `H`
of `J` is one of the tracks that the subdivision attaches to the edges of `J`.**

The argument is the paper's: consecutive edges of the branch share an internal vertex of the
branch, which is not a branch-vertex, hence not a vertex of `J`, hence internal to whichever
track of the subdivision carries it — so the two tracks coincide.  All the edges of the branch
therefore lie on a single track, and maximality of the branch makes the two equal.

*"From the minimality of F, r'₁ has no neighbour in T"*. The disjunction records the symmetry
used by the paper when orienting this path.

links.rationale: Packages 5.8.2's case-2 output for the `bᵢ = cᵢ` branch of claim (2) (`N'ci = (Nci \ {ri}) ∪ {r'i}`), together with the quoted no-neighbour-in-`T` fact used to orient the replacement path.

decls.name: mem_expandTracks_of_mem
decls.docstring: Every branch-vertex of a `J`-track survives in the expansion of that track.

links.rationale: Lean-internal plumbing: every branch-vertex of a J-track is preserved by expandTracks; no paper counterpart.

decls.name: exists_return_track
decls.docstring:
**A branch of a subdivision of a 3-connected graph has a return track.**

The edge of `J` carrying the branch `t` is not a bridge: by 7.1 there is a second track of `J`
between its ends whose first edge is another edge at the first end, and expanding that track
along the subdivision gives a track `LT` of `H` from `b₁` to `b₂` with at least three vertices
and no edge in common with `t`.

links.rationale: Auxiliary existence lemma: since J is 3-connected the edge carrying branch t is not a bridge, so 7.1 supplies a second J-track between its ends whose expansion gives a return H-track sharing no edge with t; feeds parity_from_return_track. No standalone paper statement.

decls.name: parity_from_return_track
decls.docstring:
**The replacement path has the parity of the rung it replaces.**

The return track's rung `LQ` misses the old rung, and meets the clique at `bᵢ` in exactly one
vertex.  So `R′` followed by the reverse of `LQ` is a hole of `G`, which is even because `G` is
Berge, and `LQ` has the parity of the old rung because `H` is bipartite.

links.rationale: Proves that R' has the parity of the rung Rb1b2 it replaces, via the return-track hole argument; this is the fact needed (but not given by the case-1-of-5.8.2 hypothesis) to justify the paper's replacement move 'we obtain another appearance of J in G' in the proof of 7.5.

decls.name: ends_notMem_of_cross
decls.docstring:
**Neither end of one prism path lies on another prism path.**

If the only edges between `P` and `Rg` are `u₀v₀` and `u₁v₁`, and `Rg` is a path from `v₀` to
`v₁` with at least three vertices, then `v₀ ∉ P` and `v₁ ∉ P`: the vertex of `Rg` next to `v₀`
would give a second edge out of `v₀` into `Rg`.

links.rationale: Technical fact about path/rung boundary edges: if only the two named cross-edges join P and Rg, the ends of Rg are not on P. Lean-internal geometric plumbing, no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: path_avoid_of_head_avoid
decls.docstring:
A path all of whose vertices stay out of `S` once its first vertex does and the property
propagates along the path.

links.rationale: Lean-internal plumbing: if a path's head avoids a set and avoidance propagates edge-by-edge, the whole path avoids it.

decls.name: swap_prism_pair
decls.docstring:
**The two matched prisms of case 1.**

For distinct `x, z` in `Nc₁ \ {r₁}` this produces one opposite triangle `{r₂, β₁, β₂} ⊆ Nc₂`
and two paths `P₁, P₂` that serve **both** prisms: `Rc₁c₂, P₁, P₂` is a prism with triangle
`{r₁, x, z}`, and `R′, P₁, P₂` is a prism with triangle `{p₁, x, z}`.

links.rationale: Builds, from a single application of 7.1, the matched pair of prisms (before and after the R' replacement) sharing the same two paths P1, P2, which is exactly the pairing the paper invokes via 7.4 in the proof of 7.5.

decls.name: nset_inter_trackRung
decls.docstring:
**The clique at an end of a branch meets that branch's rung in exactly one vertex**, namely
the vertex representing the branch's end edge at that vertex.

links.rationale: Lean-internal geometric fact: the clique at a branch's end meets that branch's rung in exactly the one vertex representing the end edge. No direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: shared_end_prism_pair
decls.docstring:
**Remaining gap: the matched prisms of the shared-end case.**

PAPER (proof of 7.5, claim (2), printed p. 37): *"There also correspond three tracks in `H′`,
yielding a prism in `L(H′)` … Since `Rb₁b₂ ≠ Rc₁c₂`, it follows that `Rb₁b₂` is incident with at
most one of `c₁, c₂`, so these two prisms are related as in 7.4."*

The replaced branch `t` runs from the distinguished end `c₁` to some other branch vertex `b₂`,
its rung `Rt` has the end `r` at `c₁`, and the replacement path `R′` has the end `p` at `c₁`.
The triple `{r, x, z}` contains the distinguished rung end `ρ₁` at `c₁`, so 7.1 applies **once
in `J`** with the three prescribed initial edges at `c₁`: the edge represented by `r`, the edge
represented by the other of `x, z`, and the edge represented by `ρ₁`.  Expanding those three
`J`-tracks in the old subdivision gives the first prism, with its third path the distinguished
rung; expanding the same three `J`-tracks in the subdivision produced by the replacement gives
the second one.  Only the first path changes, because only the track that begins with the
branch `t` meets `t` at all, and the opposite triangle sits at `c₂`, which the replaced branch
does not touch.

This is the one geometric statement of the 5.8.2 rung replacement that is still open.

links.rationale: Constructs the matched pair of prisms (before/after the R' replacement) for the case where the replaced branch shares exactly one end with the distinguished branch Bc1c2, formalizing the 'these two prisms are related as in 7.4' step of 7.5's proof.

decls.name: shared_end_swap_normalized
decls.docstring: **The shared-end clique swap, with the replaced branch oriented away from `c₁`.**

links.rationale: Normalizes shared_end_prism_pair's clique-swap conclusion to the case where the replaced branch is oriented away from c1; Lean-internal bookkeeping around the same paper step, no separate quote.

decls.name: formPrism_swap
decls.docstring: Exchanging the second and third paths of a prism gives a prism again.

links.rationale: Pure combinatorics: exchanging the second and third paths of a prism (with matching relabelling) yields a prism again. Lean-internal, no paper counterpart.

decls.name: shared_end_prism_pair_core
decls.docstring:
**The matched prisms of the shared-end case, with the distinguished rung end in the third
slot of the triangle.**  This is the geometric heart; the general statement follows by
exchanging the two non-`r` triangle vertices.

links.rationale: Geometric heart of the shared-end case: a single application of 7.1 at c1 produces, via track expansion, the matched pair of prisms (before/after the R' replacement) needed for the 'related as in 7.4' step of 7.5's proof.

decls.name: isTrackFrom_tail
decls.docstring:
The tail of a track is a track: dropping the first vertex keeps the second as the new
first end and leaves the other end where it was.

links.rationale: Lean-internal list fact: dropping the first vertex of a track keeps it a track from the second vertex to the same other end. No paper counterpart.

decls.name: trackRung_append
decls.docstring:
**The rung of a concatenated track splits.**

If the track `L` is the track `t` followed by the rest of a track `M` that starts where `t`
ends, then the rung of `L` is the rung of `t` followed by the rung of `M`.

links.rationale: Lean-internal fact: the rung of a concatenated track is the concatenation of the rungs, used to split off the replaced branch's rung from the rest of the track. No standalone paper quote.

decls.name: trackRung_congr
decls.docstring: Rewriting a rung along an equality of the underlying tracks.

links.rationale: Trivial congruence lemma rewriting a rung along an equality of the underlying track list. Pure Lean plumbing.

decls.name: mem_nset_trackRung_iff
decls.docstring: **A rung meets the clique at one end of its track in exactly the first rung vertex.**

links.rationale: Lean-internal geometric fact: a rung meets the clique at one end of its track in exactly the first rung vertex. Supports the rung-splitting argument but is not itself a quoted paper step.

decls.name: mem_nset_trackRung_iff_last
decls.docstring: The mirror of `mem_nset_trackRung_iff` at the other end of the track.

links.rationale: The mirror of mem_nset_trackRung_iff at the other end of the track.

decls.name: notMem_nset_of_notMem_track
decls.docstring: If a vertex of `H` is off the track `q`, then the clique it names misses the rung of `q`.

links.rationale: Lean-internal fact: a vertex off a track names a clique disjoint from that track's rung. No paper counterpart.

decls.name: trackRung_disjoint
decls.docstring: Two tracks with no common edge have disjoint rungs.

links.rationale: Lean-internal fact: tracks sharing no edge have disjoint rungs. No paper counterpart.

decls.name: case_one_parity
decls.docstring:
**Remaining gap: the replacement path has the parity of the rung it replaces.**

PAPER (proof of 7.5, claim (2), printed p. 37): *"So if in `L(H)` we replace `Rb₁b₂` by `R′` we
obtain another appearance of `J` in `G`, say `L(H′)`."*  An appearance is the line graph of a
**bipartite** subdivision, so the new branch must have the parity of the old one.  In cases 2,
3 and 4 of 5.8.2 the case hypothesis supplies that parity outright; in case 1 it does not, and
the paper leaves it to be read off from `Berge G`.

The argument is one hole.  Because `J` is 3-connected, the edge of `J` carrying the branch is
not a bridge, so after deleting that branch there is still a track from `b₁` to `b₂`; its rung
`LQ` runs from a vertex of `Nb₁ \ {r₁}` to a vertex of `Nb₂ \ {r₂}`.  The boundary condition
`hboundary` says that `R′` meets `LQ` in no vertex and sends exactly one edge to each of its
ends, so `R′` followed by the reverse of `LQ` is a hole of `G`.  Being Berge, `G` has no odd
hole, so `pathLength R′` and `pathLength LQ` have the same parity.  Since `H` is bipartite and
`LQ` and the old rung come from two tracks with the same ends, `LQ` has the parity of the old
rung.

The hypothesis `hne` is needed and is not cosmetic: when the two ends of `R′` coincide (case 3
of 5.8.2) the replacement path is a single vertex anticomplete to the old rung, no hole arises,
and the parity really is not determined.

links.rationale: Discharges the case-1-of-5.8.2 gap that the replacement branch has the right parity to make H' bipartite (needed for L(H') to be a genuine appearance), a fact the case-1 hypothesis does not supply directly and which the paper leaves implicit, to be read off from Berge G.

decls.name: case_one_single_clique_swap
decls.docstring:
**Remaining gap: the matched prisms of the same-branch case 1.**

PAPER (proof of 7.5, claim (2), printed p. 37): *"There also correspond three tracks in `H′`,
yielding a prism in `L(H′)` … these two prisms are related as in 7.4."*

Here the replaced branch **is** the distinguished branch `Bc₁c₂`, and only the clique at `c₁`
changes: it loses the rung end `r₁` and gains the end `p₁` of the replacement path.

The construction is the one described in the plan for this lane.  For distinct
`x, z ∈ Nc₁ \ {r₁}`, apply 7.1 through the distinguished branch
(`Thm75PrismThroughBranch.thm75PrismThroughBranch`) to the **old** appearance and arrange its
output so that the third path is the distinguished rung itself and the first triangle is
`{r₁, x, z}`.  Replacing that one path by `R′` — legitimate because `R′` meets `K` only inside
the old rung and attaches to the rest of `K` only at `p₁` and `r₂` — gives a prism with the same
opposite triangle and the same other two paths.  Reversing the roles of the two prisms gives the
second `SwapPrisms` instance, because `Nc₁ \ {r₁}` and `((Nc₁ \ {r₁}) ∪ {p₁}) \ {p₁}` are the
same set and `R′` is even of length at least two.

links.rationale: Discharges the 'these two prisms are related as in 7.4' step for the same-branch case 1 of 5.8.2, where the replaced branch is the distinguished branch Bc1c2 itself.

decls.name: shared_end_single_clique_swap
decls.docstring:
**Remaining gap: the matched prisms when the replaced branch shares one end with the
distinguished branch.**

PAPER (proof of 7.5, claim (2), printed p. 37): *"Since `Rb₁b₂ ≠ Rc₁c₂`, it follows that
`Rb₁b₂` is incident with at most one of `c₁, c₂`, so these two prisms are related as in 7.4."*

The replaced branch `t` is not the distinguished branch `Bc₁c₂`, but one of its two ends is the
distinguished end `c₁`; `hshared` says which one, and names the rung end `r` that the clique at
`c₁` loses and the vertex `p` that it gains.  The clique at `c₂` and the distinguished rung are
untouched, because a branch different from `Bc₁c₂` cannot be incident with both `c₁` and `c₂`.

The construction applies 7.1 **once in `J`**, prescribing the three initial edges at `c₁`, and
expands the same three `J`-tracks in the old and in the new subdivision.  The replaced branch is
the initial branch of the track that starts with the edge represented by `r`; the other two
tracks avoid it, so their rung paths are literally unchanged under the edge-label dictionary,
and the opposite triangle at `c₂` is unchanged.  For the reverse direction, both subdivisions
still contain the odd distinguished branch of length at least three, so its two ends have
opposite colours and are nonadjacent, and every track between them is odd of length at least
three, giving even rung paths of length at least two.

links.rationale: Discharges the 'these two prisms are related as in 7.4' step for the case where the replaced branch shares exactly one end with the distinguished branch Bc1c2.

decls.name: case_one_outcome
decls.docstring:
**The outcome of the case-1 replacement on the distinguished branch.**

The hypotheses are the appearance, its distinguished odd branch `Bc₁c₂` with rung `R` and rung
ends `r₁, r₂`, the path `P` of the connected set (which avoids the appearance), and the case-1
attachment pattern.  The conclusion names the new appearance, its two endpoint cliques, the
7.4 relation between the old and the new clique at `c₁`, and where the new rung sits.

links.rationale: Carries out the case-1 replacement of the distinguished rung Rc1c2 by R' and records the resulting new appearance L(H'), matching the paper's construction of R' and the new appearance in the proof of 7.5.

decls.name: SwapPrisms
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"There also correspond three tracks in H', yielding a prism in L(H'). ... these
two prisms are related as in 7.4."* The changed triangle vertex is `t`, replaced by `t'`.

links.rationale: Definition (a Prop, not a proof) formalizing what it means for the old and new cliques to carry matched prisms, capturing the paper's 'these two prisms are related as in 7.4' relation.

decls.name: SingleCliqueSwap
decls.docstring: One changed endpoint clique, with prism witnesses in both directions.

links.rationale: Definition: one endpoint clique changes under the replacement, with matched prisms witnessing the swap in both directions. Supports SwapPrisms/OneCliqueReplacement; no separate paper quote.

decls.name: OneCliqueReplacement
decls.docstring:
The replacement changes at most one of the two distinguished cliques. The last
alternative reverses the names of the distinguished ends.

links.rationale: Definition: the R' replacement changes at most one of the two distinguished cliques N1, N2 (up to swapping their names). Lean-internal bookkeeping definition, no single quoted paper sentence of its own.

decls.name: subsingleton_after_swap
decls.docstring: Apply 7.4 to exclude two missing neighbours in the new clique.

links.rationale: Applies 7.4 to show the new clique after a swap misses a dominant vertex's neighbourhood in at most one vertex; a technical step feeding dominant_iff_of_one_clique_replacement, no independent quote.

decls.name: dominant_iff_of_one_clique_replacement
decls.docstring: PAPER: *"The same argument in the reverse direction"*.

links.rationale: Discharges the quoted sentence from the paper's 7.5.

decls.name: dominant_of_complete_remainders
decls.docstring: All vertices of a clique except its named rung end are common neighbours of `Y`.

links.rationale: Lean-internal fact: if every vertex of N1 (resp. N2) other than a named point is Y-complete, then every y in Y is dominant for (N1, N2). Feeds complete_remainder_of_missing_end; no standalone paper quote.

decls.name: complete_remainder_of_missing_end
decls.docstring:
PAPER (printed p. 38): *"Since r'₁, r'₂ are not in X, they are certainly not
Y'-complete ... every vertex of N'c₁ \\ {r'₁} and N'c₂ \\ {r'₂} are Y'-complete."*
This uses claim (1) for the new appearance.

links.rationale: Formalizes the step: since the rung end r is not Y'-complete and at most one vertex of the clique N fails to be Y'-complete, every vertex of N except r is Y'-complete, in the proof of 7.5's claim (2).

decls.name: clique_remainder_subset_of_no_T
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"r'₁ has no neighbour in T, and in particular every vertex in Nc₁ \\ {r₁} is
in X"*. A vertex of the old clique remainder outside `X` would be in `T`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the step that a rung end with no neighbour in the outside set T forces the rest of the old clique into X, in the proof of 7.5's claim (2).

decls.name: dominance_and_maximality_of_double_swap
decls.docstring:
The dominance and maximality part of the same-branch case, once both old clique
remainders are common neighbours of `Y`.

links.rationale: Proves both halves of the quoted sentence: once the old clique remainders are Y-complete, every y in Y is dominant for the new appearance's cliques, and Y remains a maximal such anticonnected set.

decls.name: SmallerClaim2Instance
decls.docstring:
All data produced by the printed rung-replacement paragraphs that is needed for the next
use of the induction hypothesis.  The appearance and the distinguished branch may change, and
the new connected set already has cardinality at most `n`.

links.rationale: Structure bundling all data produced by the printed rung-replacement paragraphs of 7.5's claim (2) that the induction hypothesis needs: the (possibly new) appearance, distinguished branch, and a connected set of cardinality at most n. No single quoted sentence; it packages the paragraphs' overall output.

decls.name: ExactCardFive82Context
decls.docstring:
The exact-cardinality input to the printed rung-replacement paragraphs.  Keeping this data
in one structure makes the remaining gap state only the mathematical output of those paragraphs,
instead of restating the final disjunction of claim (2).

links.rationale: Structure bundling the hypotheses of the exact-cardinality (F.ncard = n+1) branch of 7.5's claim (2) induction: the appearance, the distinguished odd branch, the maximal Y-dominant set, and the connected set F together with the case-2-of-5.8.2 outcome data. Lean-internal bookkeeping, not itself a quoted step.

decls.name: oldAppearance
decls.docstring: The original appearance, in the same data format as the replacement.

links.rationale: Packages the context's data as a BranchAppearance for reuse by the shared appearance lemmas. Lean-internal, no paper counterpart.

decls.name: not_mem_X
decls.docstring: PAPER: *"Consequently F ∩ X is empty."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the paper's 'Consequently F ∩ X = ∅' conclusion in the proof of 7.5's claim (2): no vertex of the minimal connected set F is Y-complete.

decls.name: not_complete
decls.docstring: No vertex of `F` is a common neighbour of `Y`.

links.rationale: Immediate consequence of not_mem_X: no vertex of F is a common neighbour of Y. Lean-internal, feeds not_dominant.

decls.name: clique_subset_K
decls.docstring: The old endpoint cliques lie in `K`.

links.rationale: Lean-internal fact: the endpoint cliques of the distinguished branch lie inside K. No independent paper quote.

decls.name: not_dominant
decls.docstring:
A dominant vertex of `F` would enlarge the maximal anticonnected set `Y`.
This rules out case 3 when the replaced branch is the distinguished branch.

links.rationale: A vertex of F cannot be dominant for the two distinguished cliques, else Y ∪ {x} would be a larger anticonnected set of dominant vertices, contradicting Y's maximality. Rules out case 3 of 5.8.2 when the replaced branch is the distinguished one; feeds not_case_three_of_same_branch, no separate paper quote.

decls.name: rung_ends_ne_of_same_branch
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"Case 4 is impossible since Bc₁c₂ has length ≥ 3."*
In that case the old rung ends would be a common vertex of its disjoint endpoint cliques.

links.rationale: Proves the two rung ends r1 ≠ r2 when the replaced branch is the distinguished branch Bc1c2, which is exactly why case 4 of 5.8.2 (r1 = r2) is impossible there, since Bc1c2 has length ≥ 3.

decls.name: not_case_three_of_same_branch
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"Case 3 is impossible, since then the vertex p₁ would be Bc₁c₂-dominant ...
and therefore would be in either X or Y, a contradiction."*

links.rationale: Rules out case 3 verbatim: when b₁ = c₁ and b₂ = c₂, the hypothesis that p₁ is complete to both cliques outside {r₁,r₂} makes p₁ Bc₁c₂-dominant (`dominant_of_complete_remainders`), putting r₁ or r₂ in both a clique and the disjoint old-appearance clique -- contradicting their disjointness -- so case 3 cannot occur in the same-branch setting.

decls.name: ReplacementGeometry
decls.docstring:
The geometric output of replacing a rung. The first location alternative retains the
distinguished rung. The second retains its complement in the old appearance. In both cases
the new appearance meets `F` on the replaced side.

The last field records either the pairs of prisms used by 7.4 or the two explicit endpoint
swaps of case 2. It does not assume dominance or a smaller connected set.

links.rationale: Structure recording the geometric output of the rung replacement: the new appearance, how its cliques relate to the old ones, where the new rung sits, and which of 7.4's prism pairs or case-2's swaps witness it. Packages the paragraphs' output; no single quoted sentence of its own.

decls.name: gap_same_branch_case_one
decls.docstring:
**Remaining gap: case 1 of 5.8.2 when `bᵢ = cᵢ`**, PAPER (printed p. 37):
*"In case 1, let `R'` be the (unique) path from `p₁` to `s₂` in `(V(P) ∪ V(Rb₁b₂)) \ {s₁}` …
So if in `L(H)` we replace `Rb₁b₂` by `R'` we obtain another appearance of `J` in `G`, say
`L(H')`"*, and (printed p. 37) *"case 1 is impossible, by applying 7.4 as before to show that
`Y` remains a maximal anticonnected set of `B'`-dominant vertices, and applying the inductive
hypothesis."*

Here the replacement path reuses the terminal segment of the old rung running from `s₂ = r₂`,
so only the clique at `c₁` changes: the outcome is the `OneCliqueReplacement` alternative that
keeps `Nc₂` and exchanges `r₁` for `p₁` in `Nc₁`, with the paired prisms of 7.4 as witnesses.
What is missing is the construction of `H'` together with its endpoint-clique dictionary and
those prisms.

links.rationale: Carries out the case-1 rung replacement (R' from p1 to s2, avoiding s1) and its resulting appearance for the same-branch scenario. NOTE: the paper's own text a few lines later says 'case 1 is impossible' when b_i = c_i (via a direct 7.4 + induction argument); this lemma instead treats case 1 uniformly via the same geometric construction used for the general (non-distinguished-branch) case, so the correspondence to the quoted construction sentence is solid but the surrounding case-elimination logic differs from the paper's own shortcut — flagged for a closer look.

decls.name: gap_same_branch_case_two
decls.docstring:
**Remaining gap: case 2 of 5.8.2 when `bᵢ = cᵢ`**, PAPER (printed pp. 37--38):
*"in the other cases let `R'` be `P`.  So if in `L(H)` we replace `Rb₁b₂` by `R'` we obtain
another appearance of `J` in `G`, say `L(H')` … `N'cᵢ = (Ncᵢ \ {rᵢ}) ∪ {r'ᵢ}` for `i = 1, 2`"*,
together with *"From the minimality of `F`, `r'₁` has no neighbour in `T`"*.

The output is the same-branch witness `SameBranchReplacementData`: the new appearance replaces
both endpoint cliques by exchanging the two old rung ends for the two ends of `P`, and its
distinguished rung is `P` itself.  `P` is even by the case hypothesis (`Rc₁c₂` is even because
`Bc₁c₂` is odd), so the new distinguished branch is again odd, and it has length at least three
because `p₁ ≠ p₂`.  What is missing is the construction of `H'` and its clique dictionary, and
the minimality argument for the attachment-free end.

links.rationale: Formalizes case 2 of 5.8.2 when the replaced branch is the distinguished one — the only case that actually applies once b_i = c_i — exchanging both old rung ends r1, r2 for the ends of P and giving the new distinguished rung P, which is even (since Bc1c2 is odd) and has length ≥ 3 since p1 ≠ p2.

decls.name: replacement_geometry_of_same_branch_case_two
decls.docstring:
The geometry of the same-branch case 2 follows from the replaced appearance: the two new
cliques meet `K` inside the two old ones because the ends of `R'` lie in `F`, the old
complement of the rung survives, and `F` meets the new rung because the new rung *is* `R'`.

links.rationale: Assembles the ReplacementGeometry record from gap_same_branch_case_two's SameBranchReplacementData witness: the new cliques meet K inside the old ones, and F meets the new rung because the new rung is R' itself. Lean-internal bookkeeping around the same paper step, no separate quote.

decls.name: gap_other_branch_geometry
decls.docstring:
**Remaining gap: the replaced branch is not the distinguished one**, PAPER (printed p. 37):
*"Now suppose that `b₁b₂` and `c₁c₂` are different edges of `J`.  Then `Bc₁c₂` is still a branch
of `H'`, and we claim that every `y ∈ Y` is `Bc₁c₂`-dominant with respect to `L(H')` … Since
`Rb₁b₂ ≠ Rc₁c₂`, it follows that `Rb₁b₂` is incident with at most one of `c₁, c₂`, so these two
prisms are related as in 7.4."*

Here the distinguished branch and both of its endpoint cliques survive the replacement, so the
`OneCliqueReplacement` alternative is the trivial one, and the new appearance keeps the old
distinguished rung while `F` meets the new rung `R'`.  What is missing is the construction of
`H'`, i.e. the subdivision replacement and its clique dictionary.

links.rationale: Constructs the new appearance for the case where the replaced branch b1b2 differs from the distinguished branch c1c2: the distinguished rung and both endpoint cliques survive unchanged, matching the paper's 'Bc1c2 is still a branch of H'' setup for the different-edges case of 7.5's claim (2).

decls.name: replacement_geometry_of_other_branch

decls.name: head_getElem
decls.docstring:
Along a track of a bipartite graph the colour alternates. -/
theorem track_colour {H : SimpleGraph W} (col : H.Coloring (Fin 2)) {q : List W}
    (hq : IsTrackList H q) :
    ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < q.length) (h0 : 0 < q.length),
      ((col (q[i]'hi) : ℕ) + i) % 2 = ((col (q[0]'h0) : ℕ)) % 2 := by
  intro i
  induction i with
  | zero => intro hi h0; simp
  | succ n ih =>
    intro hi h0
    have hn : n < q.length := by omega
    have hprev := ih hn h0
    have hadj : H.Adj (q[n]'hn) (q[n + 1]'hi) := hq.2.2 n (by omega)
    have hcol : col (q[n]'hn) ≠ col (q[n + 1]'hi) := col.valid hadj
    have hne : ((col (q[n]'hn) : ℕ)) ≠ ((col (q[n + 1]'hi) : ℕ)) := fun h => hcol (Fin.ext h)
    have b1 : ((col (q[n]'hn) : ℕ)) < 2 := (col (q[n]'hn)).isLt
    have b2 : ((col (q[n + 1]'hi) : ℕ)) < 2 := (col (q[n + 1]'hi)).isLt
    omega

theorem head_getElem {α : Type*} {l : List α} {a : α} (h : l.head? = some a)
    (h0 : 0 < l.length) : l[0]'h0 = a := by
  cases l with
  | nil => simp at h0
  | cons x t => simp only [List.head?_cons, Option.some.injEq] at h; simpa using h

theorem last_getElem {α : Type*} {l : List α} {b : α} (h : l.getLast? = some b)
    (h0 : 0 < l.length) : l[l.length - 1]'(by omega) = b := by
  have hne : l ≠ [] := by intro hc; subst hc; simp at h0
  have h1 : l.getLast? = some (l.getLast hne) := List.getLast?_eq_some_getLast hne
  rw [h] at h1
  have h2 : b = l.getLast hne := Option.some_injective _ h1
  rw [h2]
  exact (List.getLast_eq_getElem hne).symm

and one at `c₂`, never meet: they cannot both contain `c₁` (or `c₂`), since `c₁c₂` is not an edge,
and they cannot meet at a third vertex, since `c₁`, `c₂` have different biparity. -/
theorem nset_anticomplete {H : SimpleGraph W} (col : H.Coloring (Fin 2)) (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (K : Set V) (φ : H.lineGraph ≃g G.induce K) {c₁ c₂ : W}
    (hcol : col c₁ ≠ col c₂) (hnadj : ¬ H.Adj c₁ c₂) :
    Anticomplete G (NSet G H K φ c₁) (NSet G H K φ c₂) := by
  rintro x ⟨e, he, hec, rfl⟩ y ⟨f, hf, hfc, rfl⟩ hadj
  have hne : c₁ ≠ c₂ := fun h => hcol (by rw [h])
  have hlg : H.lineGraph.Adj ⟨e, he⟩ ⟨f, hf⟩ := φ.map_rel_iff.mp hadj
  rw [SimpleGraph.lineGraph_adj_iff_exists] at hlg
  obtain ⟨-, z, hze, hzf⟩ := hlg
  by_cases hz1 : z = c₁
  · subst hz1
    have hfe : f = s(z, c₂) := (Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff hne).mp ⟨hzf, hfc.2⟩
    rw [hfe] at hf
    exact hnadj hf
  · by_cases hz2 : z = c₂
    · subst hz2
      have hee : e = s(c₁, z) := (Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff hne).mp ⟨hec.2, hze⟩
      rw [hee] at he
      exact hnadj he
    · have he' : e = s(c₁, z) := (Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff (Ne.symm hz1)).mp ⟨hec.2, hze⟩
      have hf' : f = s(c₂, z) := (Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff (Ne.symm hz2)).mp ⟨hfc.2, hzf⟩
      refine no_common_neighbour col hcol z ?_ ?_
      · rw [he'] at he; exact he
      · rw [hf'] at hf; exact hf

/-! ### The edges of a track at its two ends

links.rationale: Identifies the first edge of a track as the pair of its first two list entries. Pure list plumbing, no paper counterpart.
The pair of a track's last two list entries is the track's last edge.
Any edge of a track containing its declared start vertex `a` must be the track's first edge.
Any edge of a track containing its declared end vertex `b` must be the track's last edge.
The edges of a track list are all edges of the host graph `H`.
Produces the first edge of a track `q` from `a` to `b`, and shows `a` is one of its endpoints.
Produces the last edge of a track `q` from `a` to `b`, and shows `b` is one of its endpoints.
Uniqueness form of `trackEdges_eq_first`: two edges of a track both containing `a` coincide.
Uniqueness form of `trackEdges_eq_last`: two edges of a track both containing `b` coincide.

decls.docstring:

`rᵢ ∈ Ncᵢ`."*  The rung meets `Nc₁` and `Nc₂` in exactly one vertex each.

links.rationale: Discharges the paper's 7.5 sentence naming the rung's two ends `r₁ ∈ Nc₁`, `r₂ ∈ Nc₂`: the rung meets `Nc₁` and `Nc₂` in exactly one vertex each.

decls.name: not_mem_nset_of_not_mem
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"Let the ends of `Rc₁c₂` (that is, the end-edges of `Bc₁c₂`) be `r₁, r₂`, where
`rᵢ ∈ Ncᵢ`."*  The rung meets `Nc₁` and `Nc₂` in exactly one vertex each. -/
theorem rung_ends (G : SimpleGraph V) {H : SimpleGraph W} (K : Set V)
    (φ : H.lineGraph ≃g G.induce K) {B : List W} {c₁ c₂ : W} (hfrom : IsTrackFrom H B c₁ c₂)
    (h1 : 1 < B.length) (Rset : Set V)
    (hRset : Rset = {x : V | ∃ (e : Sym2 W) (he : e ∈ H.edgeSet),
      e ∈ trackEdges B ∧ x = (↑(φ ⟨e, he⟩) : V)}) :
    ∃ r₁ r₂ : V, NSet G H K φ c₁ ∩ Rset = {r₁} ∧ NSet G H K φ c₂ ∩ Rset = {r₂} := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨e₁, he₁mem, he₁c⟩ := exists_first_edge hfrom h1
  obtain ⟨e₂, he₂mem, he₂c⟩ := exists_last_edge hfrom h1
  have he₁E : e₁ ∈ H.edgeSet := trackEdges_subset_edgeSet hfrom.1 he₁mem
  have he₂E : e₂ ∈ H.edgeSet := trackEdges_subset_edgeSet hfrom.1 he₂mem
  refine ⟨(↑(φ ⟨e₁, he₁E⟩) : V), (↑(φ ⟨e₂, he₂E⟩) : V), ?_, ?_⟩
  · apply Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.mpr
    constructor
    · exact ⟨mem_nset G H K φ c₁ he₁E he₁c, by rw [hRset]; exact ⟨e₁, he₁E, he₁mem, rfl⟩⟩
    · rintro x ⟨⟨f, hf, hfc, rfl⟩, hxR⟩
      rw [hRset] at hxR
      obtain ⟨g, hg, hgmem, hxg⟩ := hxR
      have hfg : f = g := phi_inj φ hf hg hxg
      subst hfg
      have : f = e₁ := trackEdges_first_unique hfrom h1 hgmem he₁mem hfc.2 he₁c
      subst this
      rfl
  · apply Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.mpr
    constructor
    · exact ⟨mem_nset G H K φ c₂ he₂E he₂c, by rw [hRset]; exact ⟨e₂, he₂E, he₂mem, rfl⟩⟩
    · rintro x ⟨⟨f, hf, hfc, rfl⟩, hxR⟩
      rw [hRset] at hxR
      obtain ⟨g, hg, hgmem, hxg⟩ := hxR
      have hfg : f = g := phi_inj φ hf hg hxg
      subst hfg
      have : f = e₂ := trackEdges_last_unique hfrom h1 hgmem he₂mem hfc.2 he₂c
      subst this
      rfl

decls.name: exists_far_edge
decls.docstring:
PAPER (implicit in *"`T = (V(L(H)) \ V(Rc₁c₂)) \ X₁`"* being one side of the separation):
`L(H)` has a vertex off the rung and off `Nc₁ ∪ Nc₂`.  Since `J` is 3-connected, `J - {c₁, c₂}`

links.rationale: Formalizes an implicit step of 7.5's separation argument (behind the paper's `T = (V(L(H)) \ V(Rc₁c₂)) \ X₁`): since `J` is 3-connected, `L(H)` has an edge disjoint from the rung `Rc₁c₂` and from `{c₁, c₂}`, found via a first edge of the branch attached to an edge of `J - {c₁, c₂}`. The paper never spells this out, only relies on it, so it is kept as an unlinked helper.

decls.name: mem_of_mem_trackEdges
decls.docstring:
PAPER (implicit in *"`T = (V(L(H)) \ V(Rc₁c₂)) \ X₁`"* being one side of the separation):
`L(H)` has a vertex off the rung and off `Nc₁ ∪ Nc₂`.  Since `J` is 3-connected, `J - {c₁, c₂}`
is connected and has an edge; the first edge of the corresponding branch of `H` is disjoint from
`{c₁, c₂}` and is not an edge of `Bc₁c₂`. -/
theorem exists_far_edge {U : Type*} [Fintype U] [Finite W] {J : SimpleGraph U}
    {H : SimpleGraph W} (hJ : IsKConnected J 3) (hsub : IsSubdivision J H) {B : List W}
    {c₁ c₂ : W} (hbranch : IsBranch H B) (hfrom : IsTrackFrom H B c₁ c₂)
    (hc₁ : c₁ ∈ branchVertices H) (hc₂ : c₂ ∈ branchVertices H) (hne : c₁ ≠ c₂) :
    ∃ g, g ∈ H.edgeSet ∧ g ∉ trackEdges B ∧ c₁ ∉ g ∧ c₂ ∉ g := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨ι, T, hinj, htrack, hlenT, hrev, hdisj, hnew, hcover, hedges⟩ := hsub
  have hdeg : ∀ u : U, 3 ≤ (J.neighborSet u).ncard := fun u =>
    Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCounting.three_le_degree_of_three_connected J hJ u
  have hrange : Set.range ι ⊆ branchVertices H :=
    Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCounting.range_subset_branchVertices hinj htrack hlenT
      hdisj hnew hdeg
  have hbr : branchVertices H ⊆ Set.range ι :=
    Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCounting.branchVertices_subset_range htrack hrev hdisj
      hcover hedges
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hbr hc₁
  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hbr hc₂
  have hab : a ≠ b := by rintro rfl; exact hne (ha.symm.trans hb)
  have hcard : 3 < Fintype.card U := hJ.1
  have hsc : ({a, b} : Set U).ncard ≤ 2 := by
    have h1 : ({a, b} : Set U).ncard ≤ ({b} : Set U).ncard + 1 := Set.ncard_insert_le _ _
    simpa using h1
  have hcompl : 2 ≤ ((({a, b} : Set U))ᶜ).ncard := by
    have h1 := Set.ncard_add_ncard_compl ({a, b} : Set U)
    rw [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card] at h1
    omega
  have hconn := hJ.2 ({a, b} : Set U) (by omega)
  obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ : ((({a, b} : Set U))ᶜ).Nonempty := by
    rw [← Set.ncard_pos (Set.toFinite _)]; omega
  have hdiff : (((({a, b} : Set U))ᶜ) \ {d}).ncard = ((({a, b} : Set U))ᶜ).ncard - 1 :=
    Set.ncard_diff_singleton_of_mem hd
  obtain ⟨d', hd'⟩ : (((({a, b} : Set U))ᶜ) \ {d}).Nonempty := by
    rw [← Set.ncard_pos (Set.toFinite _)]; omega
  have hdd' : d ≠ d' := fun h => hd'.2 (by rw [← h]; rfl)
  have hsne : (⟨d, hd⟩ : ↥((({a, b} : Set U))ᶜ)) ≠ ⟨d', hd'.1⟩ := fun h =>
    hdd' (congrArg Subtype.val h)
  obtain ⟨cc, hcadj⟩ := Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCounting.exists_adj_of_reachable
    (hconn.preconnected ⟨d, hd⟩ ⟨d', hd'.1⟩) hsne
  have huv : J.Adj d (cc : U) := hcadj
  have hdna : d ≠ a := fun h => hd (by rw [h]; exact Or.inl rfl)
  have hdnb : d ≠ b := fun h => hd (by rw [h]; exact Or.inr rfl)
  have hcna : (cc : U) ≠ a := fun h => cc.2 (by rw [h]; exact Or.inl rfl)
  have hcnb : (cc : U) ≠ b := fun h => cc.2 (by rw [h]; exact Or.inr rfl)
  -- the first edge of the track of `H` attached to the edge `d (cc)` of `J`
  have hqfrom : IsTrackFrom H (T d (cc : U)) (ι d) (ι (cc : U)) := htrack _ _ huv
  have hq2 : 2 ≤ (T d (cc : U)).length := by
    have := hlenT _ _ huv; simp only [trackLength] at this; omega
  have hadj01 : H.Adj ((T d (cc : U))[0]'(by omega)) ((T d (cc : U))[1]'(by omega)) :=
    hqfrom.1.2.2 0 (by omega)
  have h0 : (T d (cc : U))[0]'(by omega) = ι d := head_getElem hqfrom.2.1 (by omega)
  set x : W := (T d (cc : U))[1]'(by omega) with hxdef
  have hg : s(ι d, x) ∈ H.edgeSet := by rw [← h0]; exact hadj01
  -- `x` is not an image of `ι` unless it is `ι (cc)`
  have hxcase : x ∉ Set.range ι ∨ x = ι (cc : U) := by
    by_cases hint : x ∈ trackInterior (T d (cc : U))
    · exact Or.inl (hnew d (cc : U) huv x hint)
    · rcases Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCompose.mem_ends_of_mem hqfrom.2.1 hqfrom.2.2
        (List.getElem_mem (by omega)) hint with h | h
      · exfalso
        have hnd : (T d (cc : U)).Nodup := hqfrom.1.2.1
        have h10 : x = (T d (cc : U))[0]'(by omega) := by rw [h0]; exact h
        have h10' : (T d (cc : U))[1]'(by omega) = (T d (cc : U))[0]'(by omega) := h10
        exact absurd (hnd.getElem_inj_iff.mp h10') (by omega)
      · exact Or.inr h
  have hxa : x ≠ ι a := by
    rcases hxcase with h | h
    · exact fun hc => h ⟨a, hc.symm⟩
    · rw [h]; exact fun hc => hcna (hinj hc)
  have hxb : x ≠ ι b := by
    rcases hxcase with h | h
    · exact fun hc => h ⟨b, hc.symm⟩
    · rw [h]; exact fun hc => hcnb (hinj hc)
  refine ⟨s(ι d, x), hg, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- not an edge of `B`
    rintro ⟨i, hi, heq⟩
    have hmem : ι d ∈ s((B)[i]'(by omega), (B)[i + 1]'hi) := by rw [← heq]; simp
    have hdB : ι d ∈ B := by
      rcases Sym2.mem_iff.mp hmem with h | h <;> rw [h] <;> exact List.getElem_mem _
    have hdint : ι d ∉ trackInterior B := fun hc => hbranch.2.1 _ hc (hrange ⟨d, rfl⟩)
    rcases Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCompose.mem_ends_of_mem hfrom.2.1 hfrom.2.2 hdB
      hdint with h | h
    · exact hdna (hinj (h.trans ha.symm))
    · exact hdnb (hinj (h.trans hb.symm))
  · rw [← ha]
    intro hc
    rcases Sym2.mem_iff.mp hc with h | h
    · exact hdna (hinj h.symm)
    · exact hxa h.symm
  · rw [← hb]
    intro hc
    rcases Sym2.mem_iff.mp hc with h | h
    · exact hdnb (hinj h.symm)
    · exact hxb h.symm

links.rationale: If an edge lies in a track's edge set, both of its endpoints occur among the track's listed vertices. Pure list/graph plumbing, no paper counterpart.
A vertex of a subdivision track that is not in the image of the branch-vertex map `ι` must be interior to that track.
If two `J`-adjacent pairs give the same unordered pair, their tracks have the same edge set (using track-reversal when the pair is flipped).

decls.name: trackEdges_subset_of_prefix
decls.docstring:
PAPER (printed p. 19–20, used silently): the branches of a subdivision `H` of `J` are exactly
the tracks the subdivision attaches to the edges of `J`. -/
theorem branch_eq_track {U : Type*} [Finite W] {J : SimpleGraph U} {H : SimpleGraph W}
    {ι : U → W} {T : U → U → List W}
    (htrack : ∀ u v : U, J.Adj u v → IsTrackFrom H (T u v) (ι u) (ι v))
    (hrev : ∀ u v : U, J.Adj u v → T v u = (T u v).reverse)
    (hdisj : ∀ u v u' v' : U, J.Adj u v → J.Adj u' v' → s(u, v) ≠ s(u', v') →
      ∀ w ∈ trackInterior (T u v), w ∉ T u' v')
    (hnew : ∀ u v : U, J.Adj u v → ∀ w ∈ trackInterior (T u v), w ∉ Set.range ι)
    (hedges : H.edgeSet = ⋃ (u : U) (v : U) (_ : J.Adj u v), trackEdges (T u v))
    (hrange : Set.range ι ⊆ branchVertices H) (hbrsub : branchVertices H ⊆ Set.range ι)
    {B : List W} {c₁ c₂ : W} (hbranch : IsBranch H B) (hfrom : IsTrackFrom H B c₁ c₂)
    (hc₁ : c₁ ∈ branchVertices H) (hc₂ : c₂ ∈ branchVertices H) (hne : c₁ ≠ c₂)
    (hlen : 2 ≤ trackLength B) :
    ∃ u v : U, J.Adj u v ∧ ι u = c₁ ∧ ι v = c₂ ∧ trackEdges (T u v) = trackEdges B := by
  classical
  have hL : 3 ≤ B.length := by simp only [trackLength] at hlen; omega
  -- every edge of `B` lies on some track of the subdivision
  have hlab : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 < B.length),
      ∃ u v : U, J.Adj u v ∧ s(B[i]'(by omega), B[i + 1]'hi) ∈ trackEdges (T u v) := by
    intro i hi
    have hmem : s(B[i]'(by omega), B[i + 1]'hi) ∈ H.edgeSet := hfrom.1.2.2 i hi
    rw [hedges] at hmem
    simpa using hmem
  obtain ⟨u₀, v₀, huv₀, he₀⟩ := hlab 0 (by omega)
  -- all edges of `B` lie on the same track
  have hall : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 < B.length),
      s(B[i]'(by omega), B[i + 1]'hi) ∈ trackEdges (T u₀ v₀) := by
    intro i
    induction i with
    | zero => intro hi; exact he₀
    | succ n ih =>
      intro hi
      have hn : n + 1 < B.length := by omega
      have hprev := ih hn
      obtain ⟨u, v, huv, he⟩ := hlab (n + 1) hi
      -- the shared vertex `B[n+1]` is internal to `B`, hence not a branch-vertex
      have hwint : B[n + 1]'hn ∈ trackInterior B :=
        Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCounting.mem_trackInterior_getElem B n (by omega)
      have hwnb : B[n + 1]'hn ∉ branchVertices H := hbranch.2.1 _ hwint
      have hwnr : B[n + 1]'hn ∉ Set.range ι := fun hc => hwnb (hrange hc)
      have hw₀ : B[n + 1]'hn ∈ T u₀ v₀ := mem_of_mem_trackEdges hprev (by simp)
      have hw₁ : B[n + 1]'hn ∈ T u v := mem_of_mem_trackEdges he (by simp)
      have hi₀ : B[n + 1]'hn ∈ trackInterior (T u₀ v₀) :=
        mem_trackInterior_of_not_range htrack huv₀ hw₀ hwnr
      have hsame : s(u₀, v₀) = s(u, v) := by
        by_contra hcon
        exact hdisj u₀ v₀ u v huv₀ huv hcon _ hi₀ hw₁
      rw [trackEdges_eq_of_sym2_eq hrev huv₀ hsame] at he
      exact he
  -- hence `trackEdges B ⊆ trackEdges (T u₀ v₀)`, and every vertex of `B` lies on that track
  have hsubE : trackEdges B ⊆ trackEdges (T u₀ v₀) := by
    rintro e ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩
    exact hall i hi
  have hsubV : ∀ w ∈ B, w ∈ T u₀ v₀ := by
    intro w hw
    obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := List.getElem_of_mem hw
    by_cases hlast : i + 1 < B.length
    · exact mem_of_mem_trackEdges (hall i hlast) (by simp)
    · have hi' : i = B.length - 1 := by omega
      subst hi'
      refine mem_of_mem_trackEdges (hall (B.length - 2) (by omega)) ?_
      have hidx : B.length - 2 + 1 = B.length - 1 := by omega
      rw [Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCounting.getElem_eq_of_index_eq B hidx
        (by omega) (by omega)]
      simp
  -- maximality of the branch
  have hTint : ∀ w ∈ trackInterior (T u₀ v₀), w ∉ branchVertices H := fun w hw hcon =>
    hnew u₀ v₀ huv₀ w hw (hbrsub hcon)
  have hmax : trackEdges (T u₀ v₀) = trackEdges B :=
    hbranch.2.2 (T u₀ v₀) (htrack u₀ v₀ huv₀).1 hTint hsubE hsubV
  -- identify the two ends
  have hends : ∀ c : W, c ∈ B → c ∈ branchVertices H → c = ι u₀ ∨ c = ι v₀ := by
    intro c hcB hcb
    have hcT : c ∈ T u₀ v₀ := hsubV c hcB
    have hcint : c ∉ trackInterior (T u₀ v₀) := fun hcon =>
      hnew u₀ v₀ huv₀ c hcon (hbrsub hcb)
    exact Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCompose.mem_ends_of_mem (htrack u₀ v₀ huv₀).2.1
      (htrack u₀ v₀ huv₀).2.2 hcT hcint
  have hc₁B : c₁ ∈ B := List.mem_of_mem_head? hfrom.2.1
  have hc₂B : c₂ ∈ B := List.mem_of_mem_getLast? hfrom.2.2
  rcases hends c₁ hc₁B hc₁ with h1 | h1 <;> rcases hends c₂ hc₂B hc₂ with h2 | h2
  · exact absurd (h1.trans h2.symm) hne
  · exact ⟨u₀, v₀, huv₀, h1.symm, h2.symm, hmax⟩
  · refine ⟨v₀, u₀, huv₀.symm, h1.symm, h2.symm, ?_⟩
    rw [hrev u₀ v₀ huv₀, Workspace.ProofLemmas.SubdivisionCounting.trackEdges_reverse]
    exact hmax
  · exact absurd (h1.trans h2.symm) hne
