  by_cases hor : Orient (U := U) u v
  · rw [interiorRung_pos hor]
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ : ∃ y, (R u v).head? = some y := by
      rcases hl : R u v with _ | ⟨a, t⟩
      · exact absurd hl (rung_ne_nil hR huv)
      · exact ⟨a, rfl⟩
    refine mem_tail_of_ne hx hy ?_
    rintro rfl

    {u v : U} (huv : J.Adj u v) : (gluedTrack J R u₀ u v).Nodup := by
  have hmapinr : ∀ x ∈ interiorRung R u v, ∃ y : {z : V // z ∈ rungUnion J R ∧

    intro x hx

    · rw [List.mem_singleton] at h
      exact huv.ne (Sum.inl_injective h)
  · rw [List.nodup_append]
    refine ⟨hmapnodup, by simp, ?_⟩
    intro a ha b hb
    rw [List.mem_singleton] at hb
    subst hb
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxe⟩ := List.mem_map.mp ha

    rw [← hxe]
    simp

    ∃ x ∈ interiorRung R u v, emb J R u₀ x = w := by

  exact List.mem_map.mp hw

    (hw : w ∈ gluedTrack J R u₀ u v) :
    w = Sum.inl u ∨ w = Sum.inl v ∨ ∃ x ∈ interiorRung R u v, emb J R u₀ x = w := by
  have hw' : w ∈ Sum.inl u :: ((interiorRung R u v).map (emb J R u₀) ++ [Sum.inl v]) := hw
  rcases List.mem_cons.mp hw' with h | h
  · exact Or.inl h
  · rcases List.mem_append.mp h with h' | h'
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inr (List.mem_map.mp h'))

  intro hmem
  rcases gluedTrack_mem_elim hmem with h | h | ⟨y, hy, hye⟩
  · rw [← hxe, emb_mem_interior hSN hR hRsymm huv hx] at h
    exact absurd h (by simp)
  · rw [← hxe, emb_mem_interior hSN hR hRsymm huv hx] at h
    exact absurd h (by simp)
  · rw [← hxe, emb_mem_interior hSN hR hRsymm huv hx,
      emb_mem_interior hSN hR hRsymm hu'v' hy] at hye
    have hxy : y = x := by
      have h' := Sum.inr_injective hye

    subst hxy
    have h1 : y ∈ S u v := StripSystemBasics.rung_subset_strip (hR u v huv) y

    have h2 : y ∈ S u' v' := StripSystemBasics.rung_subset_strip (hR u' v' hu'v') y

decls.name: exists_glued_subdivision
decls.docstring:
**The glued graph is a subdivision of `J`.**

Given a `J`-strip system `(S,N)` in a Berge graph `G` with `J` 3-connected, and an edge-indexed
choice of rungs `R`, the tracks

```
T u v = [inl u, inr x₁, …, inr x_k, inl v]      (R u v = [x₀, …, x_k])
```

glue into a graph `Hs` on `GluedVertex J R` which is a subdivision of `J` with `ι = Sum.inl`.
All eight conjuncts of `Tracks.IsSubdivision J Hs` are listed explicitly, so that the witnesses
`Hs`, `T` — and the edge dictionary `ρ` sending the `i`-th edge of `T u v` to the `i`-th vertex
of `R u v` — are available to the companion modules.

Disjointness of the tracks is the strip-system axiom *"the sets `S_uv` (`uv ∈ E(J)`) are
pairwise disjoint"* (`StripSystemBasics.strip_disjoint`) together with `V(R u v) ⊆ S_uv`; that
each track is a track of `Hs` is immediate from the construction, since `Hs` is *defined* by its
edge set being the union of the `trackEdges (T u v)`.

links.rationale: Builds, by hand, the object the quoted sentence asserts with no printed argument: an explicit subdivision H of J realizing the appearance on the chosen rungs' union.

Lean-internal plumbing: transports a bipartite-subdivision line-graph isomorphism from the ambient index types `U`, `Wt` to canonical `Fin n`-indexed graphs via `IsoTransport`; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: thm85Claim1
decls.docstring:
**Claim (1) of the proof of 8.5** (printed p. 42).

`F` is the connected set of the statement of 8.5 (no member of it major), and `R` is an
arbitrary choice of rungs, forming `L(H)` on the vertex set `K`.

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (1) of the proof of 8.5 (printed p. 42): for every choice of rungs forming `L(H)`, no `y ∈ F` saturates `L(H)` (via 8.4, since no member of `F` is major and there is no nondegenerate `J`-enlargement or overshadowed `K₄` appearance), and if `J = K₄` then `L(H)` is not degenerate (via 8.3).

decls.name: thm85Claim2
decls.docstring:
**Claim (2) of the proof of 8.5** (printed p. 42):
*"There is no `v ∈ V(J)` such that `X ⊆ ⋃(S_uv : uv ∈ E(J))`."*

`X` is the set of attachments of `F` in `V(S,N)`, and the union is over the edges of `J`
incident with `v`.  `hFmin` is the minimality of `F` (printed p. 42, *"We may assume that `F`
is minimal (connected) with this property"*), and `hclaim1` is claim (1).

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (2) of the proof of 8.5 (printed p. 42): the attachment set `X` of the minimal non-local connected set `F` is never contained in the union of the strips at a single vertex `v` of `J`.

decls.name: allChoices

**The conclusion of the first half of claim (2), for an arbitrary choice of rungs.**

whose pair is not local, there is a neighbour `u₀` of `v` such that on every other rung at `v`
the attachments of `F` are exactly the vertices of `N_v`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the per-choice fact from the printed proof of 8.5, claim (2) (printed p. 42): for an arbitrary given choice of rungs, there is a neighbour `u₀` of `v` such that on every other rung `R_vw` (`w ≠ u₀`) the attachments of `F` are exactly the vertices of `N_v` -- this is the sentence the printed proof states for one choice, immediately BEFORE it generalises 'since it holds for all choices of the rungs R_vw' to conclude `X \ S_uv = N_v \ S_uv`, which this lemma does not itself derive.

decls.name: first_case_attachment_identity
decls.docstring:
PAPER (proof of 8.5, claim (2), printed p. 42):

*"The branch containing `x'` does not meet `x`, so `D` is the branch between `u` and `v`, and
`d=v`. Hence `x'` is incident with `v` in `H`, and `delta_H(v) ⊆ X ∪ E(D)`. Consequently,
for all neighbours `w ≠ u` of `v` in `J`, `X` contains the vertex of `R_vw` that belongs to
`N_v`, and contains no other vertex of `R_vw`. This restores the symmetry between `u'` and the
other neighbours of `v` different from `u`; and since it holds for all choices of the rungs
`R_vw`, we deduce that `X \ S_uv = N_v \ S_uv`."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the full branch-identification-to-set-equality step of claim (2)'s proof (printed p. 42): once the branch from 5.8 is pinned to `D = uv` with end `d = v`, every rung `R_vw` (`w ≠ u`) meets `X` exactly in its `N_v`-end, and generalising over every choice of rungs (the paper's 'since it holds for all choices of the rungs R_vw') gives the set equality `X \ S_uv = N_v \ S_uv` that this lemma actually concludes -- the quote now runs through to that conclusion instead of stopping just before it.

decls.name: attachment_identity_contradicts_maximality
decls.docstring:
PAPER (proof of 8.5, claim (2), printed p. 42):

*"The minimality of `F` implies that there is a path `P` with `V(P)=F`, with ends `p1,p2`
such that `p1` is complete to `N_v \ N_vu`, and no other vertex of `P` has any neighbours in
`N_v \ N_vu`, and `p2` is adjacent to `x`, and no other vertex of `P` has any neighbours in
`S_uv \ N_v`. But then we can add `p1` to `N_v` and `F` to `S_uv`, contradicting the
maximality of `(S,N)`."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the quoted closing step of claim (2)'s proof (printed p. 42): the minimality-derived path `P` with `V(P) = F` and its two distinguished ends lets us enlarge `N_v` by `p₁` and the strip `S_uv` by `F`, contradicting the maximality of `(S,N)`.

decls.name: per_choice_attachments_at_v
decls.docstring:
**"For all neighbours `w ≠ u` of `v` in `J`, `X` contains the vertex of `R_vw` that belongs
to `N_v`, and contains no other vertex of `R_vw`."**  (Proof of 8.5, claim (2), printed p. 42.)

The neighbour `u` of the paper is produced here as `u₀`, the vertex of `J` at the far end of
the branch that 5.8 returns.

links.rationale: Formalizes what a single choice of rungs yields in claim (2)'s proof (printed p. 42): the vertex the paper calls `u` is recovered here as the second end `u₀` of the branch supplied by 5.8.

decls.name: thm85Claim3
decls.docstring:
**Claim (3) of the proof of 8.5** (printed p. 42): *"There are two disjoint edges in `K`"*,
where `K = {uv ∈ E(J) : X ∩ S_uv ≠ ∅}` and `X` is the set of attachments of `F` in `V(S,N)`.

`hclaim1` is claim (1) and `hclaim2` is claim (2).

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (3) of the proof of 8.5 (printed p. 42): `K = {uv ∈ E(J) : X ∩ S_uv ≠ ∅}` contains two disjoint edges, using claims (1) and (2) together with statement 5.8.

decls.name: common_end_of_local_choice
decls.docstring:
If the attachments on a rung family are local in the resulting line graph, all strips
which meet the original attachment set have a common end in `J`.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper for claim (3) of 8.5: if the attachments of the claim-(3) rung family are local in the resulting line graph, all strips meeting the original attachment set share a common end in `J`; no single quotable sentence of its own.

decls.name: common_end_of_branch_outcome
decls.docstring:
PAPER (proof of 8.5, claim (3), printed p. 42):

*"If there are no two disjoint edges in `K`, then by (1) and 5.8, it follows that either
`X ∩ V(L(H))` is local (with respect to `L(H)`) or 5.8.2.a holds, and in either case there
is a branch `D` of `H` with an end `d` such that every edge of `X ∩ E(H)` either is in
`E(D)` or is incident with `d`. In particular, every branch containing an edge of `X` is
incident with `d`, and so `d` meets all edges of `J` in `K`."*

This lemma is the non-local half of that sentence.  The local half is proved in
`Thm85Claim3Analysis.common_end_of_local_choice`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the non-local half of claim (3)'s branch analysis (printed p. 42): if `K` has no two disjoint edges, the branch `D` supplied by 5.8 meets all edges of `J` that lie in `K`, contradicting claim (2). The local half is `Thm85Claim3Analysis.common_end_of_local_choice`.

decls.name: rung_mem_N_unique
decls.docstring:
A rung meets `N_c` in at most one vertex, for each of the two ends `c` of its edge.  This
is the uniqueness clause of `IsUVRung` (printed p. 39, *"`s` is the unique vertex of `R` in
`N_u`"*).

links.rationale: Restates the uniqueness clause of the `uv`-rung definition (a rung meets `N_c` in at most one vertex at each end `c`), from the strip-system definition preceding 8.1, used throughout claims (2)-(3) of 8.5's proof.

decls.name: active_of_rung_end_ne
decls.docstring:
**A strip at `a` whose rung end is not the exceptional vertex `r` is active.**

If `p ∈ F` is complete to all of the line-graph clique at `ι a` except possibly `r`, then for
every neighbour `w` of `a` in `J` whose rung end is not `r`, the strip `S_{aw}` meets the
attachment set of `F`.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: a strip at `a` whose rung end is not the exceptional vertex `r` is active, i.e. meets the attachment set of `F`, whenever `F` is complete to the line-graph clique at `ι a` outside `r`; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: branch_ends_ne
decls.docstring:
The two ends of a branch of `H` are different.  (A branch has at least two vertices, and a
track has no repeated vertex.)

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: the two ends of a branch of `H` are different, since a branch has at least two vertices and a track has no repeated vertex; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: mem_Nc_decode
decls.docstring:
**A vertex of the line-graph clique at `ι a` is the end of a rung at `a`.**  Every member
of `N(ι a)` is the image of an edge of `H` incident with `ι a`, hence of an edge `E a w` for a
neighbour `w` of `a` in `J`, hence the end in `N_a` of the chosen `aw`-rung.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: every vertex of the line-graph clique at `ι a` is the image of an edge of `H` incident with `ι a`, hence the end in `N_a` of some chosen `aw`-rung; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: branch_ends_dictionary
decls.docstring:
**Reading the branch outcome of 5.8 back in the strip system.**

The branch `q` returned by 5.8 joins two branch vertices of `H`, so its ends are `ι a₁` and
`ι a₂` for two vertices `a₁, a₂` of `J`; the vertices of `G` it carries are exactly those of a
rung, so `a₁a₂` is an edge of `J` and `Rline` is an `a₁a₂`-rung; and `r₁`, `r₂` are its ends in
`N_{a₁}`, `N_{a₂}`.

links.rationale: Lean-internal dictionary fact, not a step of 8.5's own proof: reads the branch outcome of statement 5.8 back through the generic L(H)/rung correspondence set up before 8.4 ('for each edge uv of J, choose a uv-rung R_{uv} ... forms L(H)', printed p. 40 / pdf p. 42) -- the branch q returned by 5.8 has ends ι a₁, ι a₂ for adjacent a₁, a₂ ∈ V(J), Rline is the a₁a₂-rung, and r₁, r₂ are its ends in N_{a₁}, N_{a₂}. No sentence of 8.5's own printed proof states this decoding; the previously recorded p.45 quote ('The branch containing x' does not meet x, so D is the branch between u and v') belongs to claim (2)'s own case analysis and does not match what this lemma proves, so no paper_span is claimed.

decls.name: first_case_or_both_ends
decls.docstring:
**The last three subcases of 5.8.2 all make both ends of the path complete to their
cliques.**  Either the first subcase 5.8.2.a holds verbatim, or `p₁` is complete to
`N(b₁) \ {r₁}` and `p₂` is complete to `N(b₂) \ {r₂}`.  (In 5.8.2.c the two ends coincide and
the completeness is stated for the union; `r₁ ∈ N(b₂)` would put `r₁` in
`N(b₂) ∩ Rline = {r₂}`, which is how the two exceptional vertices are separated.)

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: the last three subcases of 5.8.2 all make both ends of the path complete to their respective cliques, distinguishing the two exceptional vertices `r₁, r₂`; no single quotable sentence of its own.

decls.name: path_eq_F_of_two_attachments
decls.docstring:
**The path returned by 5.8 is the whole of the minimal set `F`.**

If one end of the path has a neighbour in the strip `S_{a₁w}` and the other end has a
neighbour in the strip `S_{a₁a₂}` which is not in `N_{a₁}`, then those two attachments of the
path are not local: they lie in different strips, and the only vertex of `J` whose
neighbourhood could contain both is `a₂`, which the first attachment avoids.  The minimality of
`F` therefore forces the vertex set of the path to be all of `F`.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: if the path returned by 5.8 has two non-local attachments (one in a strip `S_{a₁w}`, one in `S_{a₁a₂} \ N_{a₁}`), minimality of `F` forces the path's vertex set to be all of `F`; no single quotable sentence of its own.

decls.name: exists_disjoint_edges_at_ends_avoiding
decls.docstring:
At the two ends of an edge in a 3-connected graph, one can select disjoint incident
edges while avoiding one prescribed edge.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: at the two ends of an edge in a 3-connected graph one can select disjoint incident edges while avoiding one prescribed edge; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: traversal_has_disjoint_meeting_rungs_avoiding
decls.docstring:
A traversal supplies two disjoint selected rungs meeting the attachment set, and the two
edges can be chosen to avoid any one prescribed edge.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: a traversal supplies two disjoint selected rungs meeting the attachment set, choosable to avoid any one prescribed edge, feeding `broad_of_single_edge_change`'s induction; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: broad_of_single_edge_change
decls.docstring: Replacing the rung on at most one unoriented edge preserves broadness.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper for claim (5) of 8.5: replacing the rung on at most one unoriented edge preserves broadness of the choice; no single quotable sentence of its own.

decls.name: every_choice_broad
decls.docstring:
PAPER (proof of 8.5, claim (5), printed pp. 43–44):

*"Consequently, if we take another choice of rungs, differing from this one on only one edge,
then it too is broad. It follows that every choice is broad."*

links.rationale: Formalizes the quoted conclusion of claim (5) of 8.5 (printed pp. 43-44): a finite induction, changing rungs one edge at a time, transfers broadness from the choice supplied by claims (3)+(4) to every choice of rungs.

decls.name: thm85Endgame
decls.docstring:
**Claims (4), (5), (6) and the closing paragraph of the proof of 8.5** (printed pp. 43–44).

Everything the printed proof has established at the point where a *broad* choice of rungs is
introduced is supplied as a hypothesis: `hclaim1` is (1), `hclaim2` is (2), `hclaim3` is (3),
and `hPF` says that the minimal `F` is the vertex set of the path `f₁ … f_n`.  The conclusion is
the contradiction the printed proof reaches.

links.rationale: Assembles claims (4), (5), (6) and the closing paragraph of the proof of 8.5 (printed pp. 43-44) into one theorem whose conclusion is `False`, matching the printed proof's own final contradiction -- the odd hole `f₁-r_hj-R_hj-r_jh-r_ji-f₁` that ends 'This proves 8.5.' -- rather than the definition of a broad choice of rungs quoted from the opening of this same block, which this decl does not itself state.

decls.name: exists_adj_in_subdivision
decls.docstring: Every vertex of the subdivision `H` has a neighbour.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: every vertex of the subdivision `H` has a neighbour; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: ends_ne_of_branch
decls.docstring: The two ends of a branch are different.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: the two ends of a branch are different; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: branch_edge_data
decls.docstring:
**The branch of 5.8, read in the strip system.**

`Nc b₁` is the set of `N_i`-ends of the chosen rungs at `i`, `Nc b₂` the set of `N_j`-ends of
the chosen rungs at `j`, the path carried by the branch is the chosen rung `R_ij`, and `ij` is
an edge of `J`.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: reads the branch supplied by statement 5.8 in strip-system language for the endgame of 8.5, identifying `N_{b₁}`/`N_{b₂}` with the rung ends at `i`/`j` and the carried path with the rung `R_ij`; no single quotable sentence of its own.

decls.name: pair_not_local
decls.docstring: Two vertices lying in the strips of two disjoint edges of `J` form a non-local pair.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: two vertices lying in the strips of two disjoint edges of `J` form a non-local pair; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: exists_adj_ne₂
decls.docstring: In a 3-connected graph every vertex has a neighbour outside any prescribed pair.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: in a 3-connected graph every vertex has a neighbour outside any prescribed pair; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: claim4
decls.docstring:
**Claim (4) of the proof of 8.5** (printed p. 43), existence and uniqueness of the
traversal of a broad choice of rungs.

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (4) of the proof of 8.5 (printed p. 43): every broad choice of rungs has a unique pair `(i,j)` of adjacent vertices of `J` (the traversal) satisfying the three printed bullets, obtained by applying 5.8 and excluding subcase 5.8.2.a.

decls.name: exists_adj_ne
decls.docstring: In a 3-connected graph every vertex has a neighbour different from any prescribed vertex.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: in a 3-connected graph every vertex has a neighbour different from any prescribed vertex; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: nodup_four
decls.docstring:
`[a,b,p,q]` has no repeated entry as soon as the four pairwise distinctions that are not
already forced by `a ≠ b` and `p ≠ q` hold.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: `[a,b,p,q]` has no repeated entry once the pairwise distinctions not already forced by `a ≠ b` and `p ≠ q` are supplied; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: attachment_of_traversal
decls.docstring:
**The printed bullets of (4), read at a single rung.**

If the traversal of the choice `R` is `pq` and the edge `ab` is different from `pq`, then any
vertex of the rung `R_ab` that has a neighbour in `F` is the end of that rung in `N_p` (and its
only neighbour in `F` is `f₁`) or the end in `N_q` (and its only neighbour in `F` is `f_n`).

links.rationale: Reads claim (4)'s printed bullets at a single rung: if the traversal of the choice `R` is `pq` and edge `ab ≠ pq`, any vertex of `R_ab` with a neighbour in `F` is the `N_p`-end (with sole neighbour `f₁`) or the `N_q`-end (with sole neighbour `f_n`).

decls.name: rung_N_unique
decls.docstring: A rung meets `N_u` in exactly one vertex.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: a rung meets `N_u` in exactly one vertex; no direct paper counterpart (compare `Thm85Claim3Common.rung_mem_N_unique`, which carries the paper's own citation).

decls.name: exists_choice_through
decls.docstring:
**"Make a choice of rungs such that `x ∈ V(R_ab)`"**: a family of rungs through one
prescribed vertex.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: constructs a family of rungs through one prescribed vertex; the doc-comment's quoted phrase is only a paraphrase of the paper's recurring 'make a choice of rungs' idiom and did not verify against a specific paper sentence, so left unlinked.

decls.name: exists_choice_through_two
decls.docstring: The same with two prescribed vertices on two different edges.

links.rationale: Lean-internal helper: the same construction with two prescribed vertices on two different edges; no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: orientation
decls.docstring:
**The orientation of the traversal.**

The printed proof says *"`x₁` is adjacent to exactly one of `f₁, f_n`, say `f₁`"*, thereby
fixing which end of the path `f₁ … f_n` is the `N_i`-end.  Under the hypothesis of (6) — all
choices have the same traversal *edge* — a choice whose traversal is the reversed pair `(j,i)`
forces `f₁ = f_n`, in which case the two orientations say the same thing.

links.rationale: Fixes the orientation of the traversal per the quoted sentence of claim (6)'s proof (printed p. 44): under the hypothesis that all choices share the same traversal edge, a choice whose traversal is the reversed pair forces `f₁ = f_n`, so the two orientations agree.

decls.name: attachment_dichotomy
decls.docstring:
**"`X ∩ (V(S,N) \ S_ij) = A₁ ∪ A₂`, and there are no other edges between `F` and
`A₁ ∪ A₂`"** (printed p. 44).

Every attachment of `F` outside the strip `S_ij` is an end in `N_i` of a rung whose only
neighbour in `F` is `f₁`, or an end in `N_j` of a rung whose only neighbour in `F` is `f_n`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the quoted attachment-completeness step of claim (6)'s proof (printed p. 44): every attachment of `F` outside the strip `S_ij` is an end, in `N_i` or `N_j`, of a rung whose only neighbour in `F` is `f₁` or `f_n` respectively, and there are no other `F`-edges.

decls.name: rung_end_adj_left
decls.docstring:
**"`f₁` is complete to `A₁`"** (printed p. 44): every vertex of `N_i ∩ S_iw`, for a
neighbour `w ≠ j` of `i`, is adjacent to `f₁`.

links.rationale: Formalizes '`f₁` is complete to `A₁`' (proof of 8.5, claim (6), printed p. 44): every vertex of `N_i ∩ S_iw`, for a neighbour `w ≠ j` of `i`, is adjacent to `f₁`.

decls.name: rung_end_adj_right
decls.docstring: **"`f_n` is complete to `A₂`"** (printed p. 44).

links.rationale: Formalizes '`f_n` is complete to `A₂`' (proof of 8.5, claim (6), printed p. 44), the counterpart of `rung_end_adj_left` at the other end of the traversal.

decls.name: claim6
decls.docstring:
**Claim (6) of the proof of 8.5** (printed p. 44):
*"There are two choices of rungs with different traversals."*

links.rationale: Formalizes claim (6) of the proof of 8.5 (printed p. 44): there are two choices of rungs with different traversals, the statement whose refutation drives the closing contradiction of 8.5.

decls.name: claim4_unique_traversal
decls.docstring:
**Gap for claim (4) of 8.5** (printed p. 43).

PAPER: *"For every broad choice of rungs `R_uv` (`uv ∈ E(J)`), there is a unique pair `(i,j)`
of adjacent vertices of `J` such that: for every `w` different from `j` and adjacent to `i`,
`r_iw f₁` is the unique edge between `V(R_iw)` and `F`; for every `w` different from `i` and
adjacent to `j`, `r_jw f_n` is the unique edge between `V(R_jw)` and `F`; and for every edge
`uv` disjoint from `ij`, there are no edges between `V(R_uv)` and `F`.  For by (1) we can apply
5.8, and since the choice of rungs is broad, the minimality of `F` implies that one of 5.8.2.b,
5.8.2.c, 5.8.2.d holds. ... This proves (4)."*

links.rationale: Proves claim (4) of 8.5: every broad choice of rungs has a unique traversal edge pair `(i,j)`.

decls.name: claim5_every_choice_broad
decls.docstring:
**Gap for claim (5) of 8.5** (printed pp. 43–44).

PAPER: *"Every choice of rungs is broad.  For from (3), there is a broad choice, and from (4)
in any broad choice ... there are four different edges ... such that the first two are
disjoint, the last two are disjoint, and `X` meets all four selected rungs.  Consequently, if
we take another choice of rungs, differing from this one on only one edge, then it too is
broad.  It follows that every choice is broad.  This proves (5)."*

links.rationale: Proves claim (5) of 8.5: every choice of rungs of the strip system is broad.

decls.name: claim6_different_traversals
decls.docstring:
**Gap for claim (6) of 8.5** (printed p. 44).

PAPER: *"There are two choices of rungs with different traversals.  Take a choice of rungs,
and let `ij` be its traversal; and suppose that all other choices of rungs have the same
traversal. ... From the minimality of `F`, there are no other edges between `F` and
`A₁ ∪ A₂`; but then we can add `f₁` to `N_i`, `f_n` to `N_j`, and `F` to `S_ij`, contrary
to the maximality of the strip system.  This proves (6)."*

links.rationale: Proves claim (6) of 8.5: some two choices of rungs must have different traversal edges.

decls.name: closing_optimal_choices_give_odd_hole
decls.docstring:
**Gap for the closing paragraph of 8.5** (printed p. 44).

PAPER: *"For any choice of rungs, there is an optimal choice with the same traversal ... so
(6) implies that there are two optimal choices of rungs with different traversals. ... Hence
`J = K₄` and `jk` is disjoint from `hi`. ... Similarly all `hk`- and `ik`-rungs have length
0, and therefore all `hj`-rungs have even length, since `G` is Berge. ... But then the path
`f₁-r_hj-R_hj-r_jh-r_ji-f₁` is an odd hole, a contradiction.  This proves 8.5."*

links.rationale: Finishes the proof of 8.5: two optimal choices of rungs with different traversals force `J = K₄`, and the closing paragraph's rung-length analysis then produces an odd hole, contradicting `G` Berge.

decls.name: attachment_at_traversal_end
decls.docstring:
**"`K` consists precisely of the edges of `J` with exactly one end in common with `hi`,
together possibly with `hi` itself"**, the containment `⊇` (printed p. 44).

The first bullet of (4) says that the `N_h`-end of the selected `hw`-rung is adjacent to `f₁`,
so it is an attachment of `F` lying in the strip `S_hw`.

links.rationale: Proves the `⊇` containment of the closing paragraph's description of `K`: the first two bullets of claim (4) put the `N_h`-end of every selected `hw`-rung (`w ≠ i`) into the attachment set of `F` in the strip `S_hw`.

decls.name: optimal_traversal_meets
decls.docstring:
**"In particular `hi` meets all edges in `K`"** (printed p. 44).

The third bullet of (4) makes the selected rung of an edge disjoint from `hi` anticomplete to
`F`; optimality says that this rung meets `X` as soon as the strip does.

links.rationale: For an optimal choice with traversal `hi`, shows every edge whose strip meets the attachment set `X` shares an end with `hi`, using the third bullet of claim (4) plus optimality.

decls.name: k4_neighbourhoods
decls.docstring:
**"Hence `J = K₄` and `jk` is disjoint from `hi`"** (printed p. 44), in the form of the
adjacencies: the two traversal edges are disjoint, and each of the four vertices is adjacent to
the other three and to nothing else.

links.rationale: Combines `attachment_at_traversal_end` and `optimal_traversal_meets` for two optimal choices with different traversals `hi`, `jk` to derive `J = K₄` with each of `h,i,j,k` adjacent to exactly the other three.

decls.name: optimal_with_same_traversal
decls.docstring:
**Gap: "For any choice of rungs, there is an optimal choice with the same traversal"**
(printed p. 44).

PAPER: *"Let us say a choice `R_uv` (`uv ∈ E(J)`) is optimal if `R_uv` has a vertex in `X` for
all edges `uv` in `K`.  For any choice of rungs, there is an optimal choice with the same
traversal (just replace rungs that miss `X` by rungs that meet `X` wherever possible)."*

links.rationale: Constructs an optimal choice of rungs with the same traversal as a given choice, by replacing the rung on the traversal edge itself.

decls.name: k4_endgame
decls.docstring:
**Gap: the last two paragraphs of the proof of 8.5** (printed pp. 44–45).

PAPER: *"Hence `V(J) = {h,i,j,k}`.  Now since the strip system is not degenerate, there is one
of the four edges `hj, hk, ij, ik` whose strip contains a rung of nonzero length; some `hj`-rung
`R` has length `> 0` say.  From (4) it follows that exactly one vertex of `R` is in `X`, one of
its ends; say the end in `N_h`.  Let `R_uv` (`uv ∈ E(J)`) be any choice of rungs such that
`R_hj = R`.  Since the end of `R` in `N_j` does not belong to `X`, it follows from (4) that for
each of `R_hk, R_ij, R_ik`, its unique vertex in `X` is its end in `N_h ∪ N_i`.  Since the choice
of these rungs was arbitrary, it follows that `X ∩ S_hk = N_hk`, `X ∩ S_ij = N_ij`, and
`X ∩ S_ik = N_ik`.  If also `X ∩ S_hj = N_hj` then `hi` is the traversal for every choice of
rungs, contrary to (6), so `X ∩ S_hj ≠ N_hj`.  It follows that every `ij`-rung has length 0; for
if one, `R'` say, has length `> 0`, then its unique vertex in `X` is its end in `N_i`, and by
exchanging `h` and `i` it follows that `X ∩ S_hj = N_hj`, a contradiction.  Similarly all `hk`-
and `ik`-rungs have length 0, and therefore all `hj`-rungs have even length, since `G` is Berge.
From (1), we may assume that `f₁` is adjacent to `r_hj` and complete to `S_hk`, and `f_n` is
complete to `S_ij ∪ S_ik`, and there are no other edges between `F` and
`S_hk ∪ S_ij ∪ S_ik ∪ {r_hj}`.  Let `R'` be an `hj`-rung such that its vertex in `N_h`
(`r'_hj`, say) is not its unique vertex in `X`.  Consequently, its other end (`r'_jh`) is its
unique vertex in `X`.  By the same argument with `hi` and `jk` exchanged, it follows that one of
`f₁, f_n` is complete to `S_ij ∪ {r'_jh}` and the other to `S_hk ∪ S_ik`; and hence `n = 1`.
But then the path `f₁-r_hj-R_hj-r_jh-r_ji-f₁` is an odd hole, a contradiction.  This proves
8.5."*

The `K₄` structure reached by `k4_neighbourhoods` is supplied as the four neighbourhood
descriptions; the printed sentence *"Hence `V(J) = {h,i,j,k}`"* follows from them and the
3-connectivity of `J`.

links.rationale: Given the `K₄` shape from `k4_neighbourhoods`, derives the odd hole `f₁-r_hj-R_hj-r_jh-r_ji-f₁` that finishes the proof of 8.5.

decls.name: closing
decls.docstring: **The closing paragraph of the proof of 8.5** (printed pp. 44–45).

links.rationale: Assembles `k4_neighbourhoods` and `k4_endgame` into the full closing paragraph of 8.5's proof; the paper text it discharges is already carried, sentence by sentence, by those two lemmas.

decls.name: mem_of_walk
decls.docstring: A set closed under taking neighbours contains everything reachable from it.

links.rationale: Generic graph-theory helper: a set closed under taking neighbours contains everything reachable from it. No paper counterpart.

decls.name: not_two_neighbours
decls.docstring: A vertex of a 3-connected graph has more than two neighbours.

decls.name: cover_of_hub_neighbourhoods
decls.docstring:
**"Hence `V(J) = {h,i,j,k}`"**: if the two ends of an edge of a 3-connected graph have all
their neighbours inside a fixed four-element set, then that set is all of `V(J)`.  Deleting the
other two vertices leaves a connected graph in which `i` and `j` see only each other.

links.rationale: Pure graph fact used to get the paper's "Hence `V(J) = {h,i,j,k}`": if the two ends of an edge of a 3-connected graph have all their neighbours inside a fixed four-element set, that set is all of `V(J)` (deleting the other two vertices leaves a connected graph in which `i` and `j` see only each other). The quoted sentence is too short and symbol-heavy for the paper-text verifier to confirm on its own.

decls.name: edge_meeting_four
decls.docstring: In `K₄` on `{h,i,j,k}`, an edge meeting each of `hj`, `hk`, `ij`, `ik` is `hi` or `jk`.

links.rationale: Pure combinatorial fact about `K₄`: on `{h,i,j,k}`, an edge meeting each of `hj`, `hk`, `ij`, `ik` must be `hi` or `jk`. No paper counterpart of its own.

decls.name: zero_rung_of_common_end
decls.docstring: A rung with a vertex in `N_u ∩ N_v` has length `0`.

links.rationale: Rung-book-keeping helper: a rung with a vertex in `N_u ∩ N_v` has length `0`. Used repeatedly in the degeneracy argument but not itself a printed sentence.

decls.name: disjoint_traversals_absurd
decls.docstring:
**"Since `i'j'` meets all edges of `J` that share exactly one end with `ij`, and `J` is
3-connected, it follows that `J = K₄` … and so `L(H)` is degenerate, contrary to (1)"**
(printed pp. 43–44).

The pair `(i,j)` is only assumed to satisfy the first two bullets of claim (4) — that is enough
to make every rung at `i` or at `j` other than `R_ij` have a neighbour in `F` — while `(a,b)` is
a full traversal.  The third bullet of `(a,b)` then confines the neighbours of `i` and of `j` to
`{j,a,b}` and `{i,a,b}`, and the uniqueness clauses identify the two ends of each of the four
rungs `R_ia, R_ib, R_ja, R_jb`, so all four have length `0`.

links.rationale: Generalized form of the paper's degenerate-`K₄` argument: if a second edge `ab` is a full traversal disjoint from a pair `ij` that already satisfies the first two bullets of claim (4), then `J = K₄` and the four cross rungs `R_ia, R_ib, R_ja, R_jb` all have length `0`, making the appearance degenerate and contradicting claim (1). Used both to prove the uniqueness half of claim (4) and inside the closing paragraph of 8.5.

decls.name: RungChoice
decls.docstring:
A choice of one rung for every unoriented edge.  The second conjunct says that changing
the orientation reverses the list.

links.rationale: A choice of one rung per unoriented edge of `J`, symmetric under reversing the orientation.

decls.name: BroadChoice
decls.docstring: The paper's broad choice: two vertex-disjoint edges have selected rungs meeting `X`.

links.rationale: Names the paper's proof-local notion of a broad choice of rungs: two vertex-disjoint edges have selected rungs meeting the attachment set `X`.

decls.name: UniqueEdgeBetween
decls.docstring: `xy` is the unique edge of `G` between `A` and `B`.

links.rationale: States that `xy` is the unique `G`-edge between the sets `A` and `B`. Lean-internal plumbing with no direct paper counterpart of its own.

decls.name: IsTraversal
decls.docstring:
The three bullets in claim (4), with the orientation fixed by the path ends `f₁` and
`fn`.  Membership in `N i` identifies the endpoint called `r_iw` in the paper.

links.rationale: Packages the three bullets of claim (4) into a single predicate, with the orientation fixed by the path ends `f₁` and `f_n`.

decls.name: HasUniqueTraversal
decls.docstring: A selected family has one and only one oriented traversal.

links.rationale: Names claim (4)'s conclusion: a selected family of rungs has one and only one (ordered) traversal edge.

decls.name: HasDifferentTraversals
decls.docstring: Claim (6): two choices have different traversal edges.

links.rationale: Names claim (6)'s notion: two choices of rungs have different traversal edges.

decls.name: OptimalChoice
decls.docstring:
The paper's optimal choice.  The edges in `K` are expressed without introducing a second
set: they are exactly the edges whose strips meet `X`.

links.rationale: Names the paper's optimal choice of rungs: every edge whose strip meets the attachment set `X` has its selected rung meet `X` too.

decls.name: exists_broad_choice
decls.docstring:
Claim (3) supplies a broad choice by selecting, on every active strip, a rung through an
attachment in that strip.

links.rationale: Builds a broad choice of rungs from claim (3)'s two disjoint attachment-meeting edges, by selecting a rung through an attachment on each active strip.

decls.name: exists_rung_choice_replacing
decls.docstring:
**"Take another choice of rungs, differing from this one on only one edge"** (printed
p. 44).  Any prescribed rung on one edge extends to a choice of rungs that is unchanged
elsewhere.

links.rationale: Realizes the printed operation of taking another choice of rungs that differs from a given one on only one edge: any prescribed rung on one edge extends to a full choice unchanged elsewhere.

decls.name: attachment_edges_meet_traversal
decls.docstring:
**"`K` consists precisely of the edges of `J` with exactly one end in common with `hi`,
together possibly with `hi` itself"** (printed p. 44), in the form used by the closing
paragraph: for any choice of rungs with traversal `ij`, no strip of an edge disjoint from `ij`
meets the attachment set `X`.

If it did, one would change the choice on that one edge so that its rung passes through the
attachment.  The changed choice still satisfies the first two bullets of claim (4) at `(i,j)`,
so its own traversal is either `ij` itself — impossible, since the third bullet would make the
changed rung anticomplete to `F` — or an edge meeting `ij` in one vertex, which strands one of
`i, j` with only two neighbours, or an edge disjoint from `ij`, which is the degenerate `K₄` of
`Thm85EndgameK4Shape.disjoint_traversals_absurd`.

links.rationale: Same conclusion as `Thm85EndgameClosing.optimal_traversal_meets` / `Thm85EndgamePathTwoVerticesGapMeets.meets_traversal` -- every edge `uv` whose strip meets the attachment set `X` shares an end with the traversal: 'In particular hi meets all edges in K' (closing paragraph of 8.5, printed p. 44/pdf p. 46) -- proved here from claims (4)-(5) for an arbitrary (not necessarily optimal) rung choice with a given traversal.

decls.name: getElem_zero
decls.docstring: The first vertex of a path list, as an indexed entry.

links.rationale: Restates a path list's first vertex as an indexed array entry. Lean-internal plumbing.

decls.docstring: The last vertex of a path list, as an indexed entry.

decls.name: head_neighbour_unique
decls.docstring: The first vertex of a path has at most one neighbour on the path.

links.rationale: The first vertex of an induced path has at most one neighbour on the path. Pure Lean-internal path fact.

decls.name: last_neighbour_unique
decls.docstring: The last vertex of a path has at most one neighbour on the path.

links.rationale: The last vertex of an induced path has at most one neighbour on the path. Pure Lean-internal path fact.

decls.name: interior_two_neighbours
decls.docstring: A vertex strictly inside a path has two distinct neighbours on the path.

links.rationale: A vertex strictly inside an induced path has two distinct neighbours on the path. Pure Lean-internal path fact.

decls.name: ends_eq_of_vertex_set_eq
decls.docstring:
**The ends of a path are determined by its vertex set.**

If two paths of `G` have the same vertex set, then their end pairs coincide.

links.rationale: Two induced paths of `G` with the same vertex set have the same end pair (up to reversal). Supplies the fact, left implicit in the paper, that the path from 5.8 and the path `f₁ … f_n` share ends because they share a vertex set.

decls.name: eq_of_ends_eq
decls.docstring: A path whose two ends coincide is a single vertex.

links.rationale: A path whose two ends coincide has only that one vertex. Pure Lean-internal path fact.

decls.name: path_ends_distinct
decls.docstring:
**"Hence `n ≥ 2`, for if `n = 1` then we can add `f₁` to `N_i`, `N_j` and `S_ij`, contrary
to the maximality of the strip system"** (printed p. 44).

`F` is the vertex set of the path `f₁ … f_n` of the proof of 8.5, so `n = 1` is exactly
`f₁ = f_n`.  In that case `F = {f₁}`, the attachments of `F` are the neighbours of `f₁` in
`V(S,N)`, and the printed sentence adds `f₁` to `N_i`, `N_j` and `S_ij` for the traversal edge
`ij`, producing a strictly larger `J`-strip system and contradicting `hmax`.

links.rationale: Proves `f₁ ≠ f_n`, i.e. the path `F` of 8.5's proof has at least two vertices: if `f₁ = f_n`, either every choice of rungs shares the traversal `ij` (so `F` can be added to `S_ij`, `N_i`, `N_j`, contradicting maximality of the strip system) or two choices have different traversals, and the closing paragraph's odd-hole argument applies.

decls.name: broad_of_single_edge_change
decls.docstring: Replacing the rung on at most one unoriented edge preserves broadness.

links.rationale: Replacing the selected rung on at most one unoriented edge preserves broadness of a choice. Combinatorial step used inside `every_choice_broad`; no paper sentence of its own.

decls.name: every_choice_broad
decls.docstring:
**Claim (5) of 8.5**: *"every choice of rungs is broad"* (printed pp. 43–44), with claim (4)
supplied only as the existence of a traversal.

links.rationale: Re-proves claim (5) (every choice of rungs is broad) with claim (4) supplied only as existence of a traversal, since the `n = 1` step of 8.5 needs claim (5) before `f₁ ≠ f_n` is known and the ordered uniqueness of claim (4) is false when `f₁ = f_n`.

decls.name: pair_not_local
decls.docstring: Two vertices lying in the strips of two disjoint edges of `J` form a non-local pair.

links.rationale: Two vertices lying in the strips of two vertex-disjoint edges of `J` form a non-local pair. Combinatorial step feeding claim (4)'s use of 5.8; no paper sentence of its own.

decls.name: exists_adj_ne₂
decls.docstring: In a 3-connected graph every vertex has a neighbour outside any prescribed pair.

links.rationale: Lean-internal graph-theory helper: in a 3-connected graph every vertex has a neighbour outside any prescribed pair. No direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: claim4_exists
decls.docstring:
**Claim (4) of the proof of 8.5** (printed p. 43), existence and uniqueness of the
traversal of a broad choice of rungs.

links.rationale: Existence-only half of claim (4): every broad choice of rungs has *some* traversal pair `(i,j)`. Repeats the proof of `Thm85EndgameClaim4.claim4` but drops the `f₁ ≠ f_n` hypothesis needed only for the separate uniqueness half (`Thm85EndgameTraversalUnique.traversal_unique`).

decls.name: n1_different_traversals_absurd
decls.docstring:
**Gap: the closing paragraph of the proof of 8.5, for `n = 1`** (printed pp. 44–45).

Two choices of rungs with different traversals force `J = K₄`, and then the printed argument
ends with the odd hole `f₁-r_hj-R_hj-r_jh-r_ji-f₁`.  See the module docstring for the full
paper text and for why the already-formalized `Thm85EndgameClosing.closing` cannot be used when
`f₁ = f_n`.

links.rationale: Runs the closing paragraph of 8.5's proof for the special case `f₁ = f_n` (`n = 1`), where the ordered uniqueness of claim (4) is unavailable: two choices of rungs with different traversals force `J = K₄`, and the printed odd-hole argument `f₁-r_hj-R_hj-r_jh-r_ji-f₁` finishes it.

decls.name: traversal_swap
decls.docstring: With `f₁ = f_n` a traversal may be read in either direction.

links.rationale: With `f₁ = f_n`, a traversal `IsTraversal … R p q` may equally be read as `IsTraversal … R q p`. Lean-internal symmetry fact, no paper counterpart.

decls.name: cross_rung_end
decls.docstring:
**"From (4) it follows that exactly one vertex of `R` is in `X`, one of its ends; say the
end in `N_h`"** (printed p. 45), for an arbitrary `hj`-rung.

links.rationale: For `J = K₄` on `{h,i,j,k}` with `F = {f₁}` and traversal `hi`, shows every `hj`-rung has its `N_h`-end as the unique vertex adjacent to `f₁`. Changing the choice on `hj` and re-applying claim (4) forces the new traversal to be `hi` or `jk`; the `jk` case is excluded by the printed odd hole `f₁-r_hj-R_hj-r_jh-r_ji-f₁`.

decls.name: odd_of_pos
decls.docstring:
**"But then the path `f₁-r_hj-R_hj-r_jh-r_ji-f₁` is an odd hole, a contradiction"**
(printed p. 45).

`L` is the `hj`-rung `R_hj`; `r` is its end `r_hj` in `N_h`, the unique vertex of `L` adjacent
to `f₁`; and `b` is `r_ji`, a vertex of `N_j ∩ S_ij` adjacent to `f₁`.  If `L` has nonzero
length the cycle has length `pathLength L + 3 ≥ 4`, so it is a hole, and `G` being Berge makes
`pathLength L` odd.

links.rationale: Builds the cycle `f₁-r_hj-R_hj-r_jh-r_ji-f₁` (an `hj`-rung of nonzero length, its two ends, and `f₁`), shows it is an induced hole, and concludes from `G` Berge that the rung's length must be odd.

decls.name: attachment_at_traversal_end
decls.docstring:
**"`K` consists precisely of the edges of `J` with exactly one end in common with `hi`,
together possibly with `hi` itself"** (printed p. 44), the containment `⊇`: the first bullet of
claim (4) puts the `N_h`-end of the selected `hw`-rung next to `f₁`.

links.rationale: The `⊇` containment of the closing paragraph's `K`, restated with claim (4) supplied only as existence of a traversal: the first bullet of claim (4) puts the `N_h`-end of the selected `hw`-rung next to `f₁`, an attachment of `F` in `S_hw`. Duplicate of `Thm85EndgameClosing.attachment_at_traversal_end` for the weaker `n = 1` setting.

decls.name: meets_traversal
decls.docstring:
`Thm85EndgameOptimalChoice.attachment_edges_meet_traversal` with claim (4) supplied only as
the existence of a traversal.  The proof is the printed one, unchanged.

links.rationale: Duplicate of `Thm85EndgameOptimalChoice.attachment_edges_meet_traversal` with claim (4) supplied only as existence of a traversal; same conclusion (every edge whose strip meets `X` shares an end with the traversal `hi`), used for the `n = 1` case.

decls.name: k4_neighbourhoods
decls.docstring:
**"Hence `J = K₄` and `jk` is disjoint from `hi`"** (printed p. 44), with claim (4) in the
existence form and with plain choices of rungs.  This is
`Thm85EndgameClosing.k4_neighbourhoods` with `optimal_traversal_meets` replaced by
`meets_traversal`, which has the same conclusion but does not need optimality.

links.rationale: Duplicate of `Thm85EndgameClosing.k4_neighbourhoods` with claim (4) in the existence form and plain (non-optimal) choices of rungs, for the `n = 1` case of the closing paragraph where the ordered uniqueness of claim (4) is unavailable.

decls.name: rung_N_unique
decls.docstring: A rung meets `N_u` in exactly one vertex.

links.rationale: A `uv`-rung meets `N_u` in exactly one vertex. Rung-book-keeping fact, no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: traversal_of_unified
decls.docstring: **The three bullets of (4).**

links.rationale: Assembles the three bullets of claim (4) of 8.5 from the raw data supplied by 5.8's branch/rung dictionary, once the branch has been identified with an edge `ij` of `J`. Its docstring describes rather than quotes the paper, so no `paper_span` is added.

decls.name: traversal_unique
decls.docstring:
**Gap: the uniqueness half of claim (4) of 8.5** (printed pp. 43–44).

PAPER: *"Hence there is an edge `ij` as in (4).  Suppose there is another, say `i'j'`.  Since
`i'j'` meets all edges of `J` that share exactly one end with `ij`, and `J` is 3-connected, it
follows that `J = K₄` and the two edges `ij`, `i'j'` are disjoint.  Moreover, the unique vertex
of `R_{ii'}` in `X` is both `r_{ii'}` and `r_{i'i}`, so `R_{ii'}` has length 0.  Similarly
`R_{ij'}`, `R_{ji'}`, `R_{jj'}` all have length 0, and so `L(H)` is degenerate, contrary to (1).
This proves (4)."*

The hypotheses are those of claim (4): `hclaim1` is claim (1), whose second bullet supplies the
nondegeneracy of `L(H)` when `J = K₄`, and `f₁ ≠ f_n` is not needed — the two traversals are for
the *same* choice of rungs `R`.

links.rationale: Proves the uniqueness half of claim (4): a broad choice of rungs cannot have two different traversal pairs, since a second traversal disjoint from the first would force `J = K₄` with four zero-length rungs, degenerating the appearance. (The quote straddles pp. 45-46; the substance this lemma proves -- J = K4 and the four zero-length rungs forcing L(H) degenerate -- is on p.46, so the page is recorded there rather than at the opening 'Hence there is an edge ij as in (4)' on p.45.)

decls.name: thm85EnlargeStripBySet
decls.docstring:
**"We can add `F` to `S_uv` (and one vertex of `F` to each of `N_u`, `N_v`), contradicting
the maximality of `(S,N)`."**  (Proof of 8.5, printed pp. 42–43; used at the end of claim (2)
and twice inside claim (6).)

`Au` and `Av` are the sets of vertices of `F` promoted into `N_u` and into `N_v`; at the three
call sites each is empty or a singleton, but nothing below needs that.  `hcover` is the one
axiom that has to be supplied by the caller (see the module docstring).

links.rationale: Generic combinator used at three points of the proof of 8.5 (end of claim (2), and twice in claim (6)): absorbing a connected set `F` into the strip of one edge (and at most one vertex of `F` into each end's neighbourhood) yields a strictly larger `J`-strip system, contradicting maximality. Its docstring's bold quote paraphrases and merges three distinct printed sentences rather than quoting one verbatim, so no single `paper_span` is added.

decls.name: isSubdivision_of_iso
decls.docstring:
**Being a subdivision transports along an isomorphism of the subdivided graph.**

If `H` is a subdivision of `J` and `J ≃g J'`, then `H` is a subdivision of `J'`: re-index the
embedding `ι : V(J) → V(H)` and the family of tracks `T` along `e.symm`.

links.rationale: Being a subdivision transports along an isomorphism of the subdivided graph: if `H` is a subdivision of `J` and `J ≃g J'`, then `H` is a subdivision of `J'`, by re-indexing the embedding and tracks. Purely bureaucratic bridging lemma, no paper counterpart.

decls.name: thm85Five8Transported
decls.docstring:
**5.8 for `J` on an arbitrary finite vertex type.**

The statement is that of `Workspace.Statements.S05.SPGT.thm_5_8` verbatim — only the vertex
type of `J` has been relaxed from `Fin m` to an arbitrary `U` with `[Fintype U]`.

links.rationale: Restates 5.8 (already proved for `J : SimpleGraph (Fin m)`) for `J` on an arbitrary finite vertex type `U`, by transporting along an isomorphism `J ≃g J'` with `J'` on `Fin (Fintype.card U)`. Needed because 8.5's proof applies 5.8 to the ambient strip system's graph `J`, which lives on an arbitrary type; the statement itself is not a new paper sentence.

decls.name: rungUnion_subset_stripSystemVertices
decls.docstring: The union of a chosen family of rungs is contained in the strip-system vertex set.

links.rationale: The union of a chosen family of rungs is contained in the strip-system vertex set. Set-containment bookkeeping, no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: exists_nonlocal_preimage_pair
decls.docstring:
Pulling two prescribed rung vertices back through the appearance isomorphism preserves
non-locality.

This is the formal version of the sentence in claim (2), *"Then `{x,x'}` is not local with
respect to `L(H)`"*.  The branch dictionary handles the branch alternative in
`LocalForLineGraph`; the rung-end dictionary handles the incident-edge alternative.

links.rationale: Formal version of the sentence in claim (2) (proof of 8.5, printed p. 42): "Then {x,x'} is not local with respect to L(H)" -- pulling two prescribed rung vertices back through the appearance isomorphism preserves non-locality. The branch dictionary handles the branch alternative in LocalForLineGraph; the rung-end dictionary handles the incident-edge alternative. (The quote is trimmed to this clause; the lemma does not itself go on to apply 5.8.)

decls.name: attachmentEdges_not_local_of_pair
decls.docstring: A non-local pair contained in the attachment-edge set makes that whole set non-local.

links.rationale: A non-local pair contained in the attachment-edge set makes that whole set non-local. Generic set-theoretic step feeding claim (4)'s application of 5.8; no paper sentence of its own.

decls.name: thm85MinimalNonlocal
decls.docstring:
**"We may assume that `F` is minimal (connected) with this property."**  (Proof of 8.5,
printed p. 42.)

links.rationale: Extracts a minimal connected subset `F₀` of a connected `F` whose attachment set is still non-local, by choosing one of least cardinality among such subsets (nonempty since the empty set's attachment set is local).

decls.name: thm85PathStructure
decls.docstring: **"`F` is the vertex set of a path, say `f₁, …, f_n`"** (proof of 8.5, printed p. 42).

links.rationale: Shows the minimal non-local `F` of the proof of 8.5 is the vertex set of an induced path: claim (3)'s two disjoint attachment-meeting edges give a two-element non-local subset of the attachment set, so minimality of `F` forces it to be the minimal connected set attached to both, which is a path. (The module's stale "work item, not yet proved" docstring note predates the completed proof — the theorem has no `sorry`.)

decls.name: exists_mem_ne_pair
decls.docstring: A set of size ≥ 3 has a member outside any prescribed pair.

decls.name: exists_disjoint_edges_at_ends
decls.docstring:
**From the two ends of an edge of a 3-connected graph one can pick two disjoint edges.**

This is the combinatorial core of the exclusion of outcomes 5.8.2.b, 5.8.2.c, 5.8.2.d in the
printed proof of claim (3): in each of them the ends `p₁, p₂` of the path are complete to
`N_{b₁} \ {r₁}` and `N_{b₂} \ {r₂}`, so the strips of the edges `b₁w` and `b₂w'` both meet the
attachment set.

links.rationale: From the two ends of an edge of a 3-connected graph, picks two disjoint edges. Combinatorial core of excluding outcomes 5.8.2.b/c/d in the proof of claim (3); no direct paper sentence of its own.

decls.name: exists_symmetric_rung_family_of_choice
decls.docstring:
**A per-ordered-pair choice of rungs can be made edge-indexed.**

Given any family `C` with `C a b` a `ab`-rung for every ordered adjacent pair, there is a family
`R` which is a choice of rungs in the paper's sense — indexed by the *edges* of `J`, so that
reversing the orientation reverses the list — and each `R a b` is one of `C a b`, `(C b a)ᴿ`.
This is what turns "for each edge `uv` of `J` choose a `uv`-rung with such-and-such a property"
into the hypotheses of `Thm84EveryChoiceFormsLineGraph.everyChoiceFormsLineGraph`.

This is the **generic** version of the already-proved
`Thm82RungFamily.exists_symmetric_rung_family`, which only pins the choice down on one
prescribed edge.

links.rationale: Turns a per-ordered-pair choice of rungs into one indexed by unoriented edges (reversing the orientation reverses the list). Generic Lean-internal packaging step, no direct paper counterpart.

decls.name: exists_rung_family_meeting
decls.docstring:
**"Make a choice of rungs `R_uv` (`uv ∈ E(J)`) such that `X ∩ V(R_uv) ≠ ∅` for each
`uv ∈ K`"** (proof of 8.5, claims (2) and (3), printed p. 42).

This is **strictly stronger** than the still-`sorry` `TwoPrescribedSymmetricRungFamily`: it
prescribes a meeting point on *every* edge whose strip meets `D`, not merely on two prescribed
edges.

links.rationale: Constructs a full choice of rungs that meets a prescribed set `D` on every edge whose strip meets `D` (used for claims (2) and (3) with `D` the attachment set `X`). Stronger than only prescribing the choice on two edges.

decls.name: exists_nonlocal_pair
decls.docstring:
**The step "`X` is not local, so there are `x ∈ X ∩ S_uv \ N_v` and `x' ∈ X ∩ S_{u'v}` with
`u' ≠ u`, and `{x, x'}` is not local"** (proof of 8.5, claim (2), printed p. 42).

links.rationale: Formalizes the printed step (proof of 8.5, claim (2), printed p. 42): "X is not local, so there are x ∈ X ∩ S_uv \ N_v and x' ∈ X ∩ S_u'v with u' ≠ u, and {x, x'} is not local."

decls.name: subset_iUnion_of_common_end
decls.docstring:
**"`d` meets all edges of `J` in `K`, contrary to (2)"** (proof of 8.5, claim (3), printed
p. 42): if every edge of `J` whose strip meets `X` has `w₀` as an end, then `X` is contained in

**The hole `x₁-a₁-P₁-b₁-y₂-x₁`.**

end `v` has the private neighbour `t` off the path, with `s` adjacent to `t`, closes into the
hole `t-s-u-p-v-t` of length `pathLength p + 3`.  In a Berge graph that length is even, so
`pathLength p` is odd.

decls.name: no_long_path_and_antipath

**The second paragraph of the printed proof of 9.1.**

`P` is a path `a-P-b` of odd length `≥ 3`; `Q` is an antipath `x-Q-y` of length `≥ 3`, disjoint
from `P`; `Y` is the interior of `Q`.  The ends `a, b` of `P` are `Y`-complete, as is a further
vertex `c` with no neighbour in `P*` (in 9.1 these are `a₁, b₁` and `c = a₂`), and no interior
vertex of `P` has a neighbour in `{x, y}`, while `a` is adjacent to `x` only and `b` to `y`
only among `{x, y}`.  This configuration is contradictory in a Berge graph.

decls.name: localForLineGraph_iff_intrinsic
decls.docstring:
All edges of one subdividing track lie in one flat component of the line graph. -/
theorem trackEdges_flat_reachable (hbip : H.IsBipartite) {u v : Fin 4}
    (huv : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).Adj u v) {e f : H.edgeSet}
    (he : (e : Sym2 W) ∈ trackEdges (T u v))
    (hf : (f : Sym2 W) ∈ trackEdges (T u v)) :
    Relation.ReflTransGen (FlatAdj H.lineGraph) e f := by
  let q := T u v
  have hq : IsTrackFrom H q (ι u) (ι v) := htrack u v huv
  have hq2 : 2 ≤ q.length := by
    have := hlen u v huv
    change 1 ≤ q.length - 1 at this
    omega
  let edgeAt : ∀ k : ℕ, k + 1 < q.length → H.edgeSet := fun k hk =>
    ⟨s(q[k]'(by omega), q[k + 1]'hk), hq.1.2.2 k hk⟩
  have hstep : ∀ k (hk : k + 2 < q.length),
      FlatAdj H.lineGraph (edgeAt k (by omega)) (edgeAt (k + 1) (by omega)) := by
    intro k hk
    have hnd := hq.1.2.1
    have hne : edgeAt k (by omega) ≠ edgeAt (k + 1) (by omega) := by
      intro h
      have hv := congrArg Subtype.val h
      change s(q[k]'(by omega), q[k + 1]'(by omega)) =
        s(q[k + 1]'(by omega), q[k + 2]'(by omega)) at hv
      rcases Sym2.eq_iff.mp hv with hp | hp
      · have := hnd.getElem_inj_iff.mp hp.1
        omega
      · have := hnd.getElem_inj_iff.mp hp.1
        omega
    have hmid : q[k + 1]'(by omega) ∈ trackInterior q :=
      SubdivisionCounting.mem_trackInterior_getElem q k hk
    have hnotbranch : q[k + 1]'(by omega) ∉ branchVertices H := by
      intro hb
      have hrange : q[k + 1]'(by omega) ∈ Set.range ι := by
        rw [← branchVertices_eq_range hι htrack hlen hrev hdisj hnew hcover hedges]
        exact hb
      exact hnew u v huv _ hmid hrange
    exact flatAdj_of_common_nonbranch hbip hne (by simp [edgeAt]) (by simp [edgeAt]) hnotbranch
  have hreach0 : ∀ k (hk : k + 1 < q.length),
      Relation.ReflTransGen (FlatAdj H.lineGraph) (edgeAt 0 (by omega)) (edgeAt k hk) := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero =>
        intro hk
        have heq : edgeAt 0 (by omega) = edgeAt 0 hk := Subtype.ext rfl
        rw [heq]
    | succ k ih =>
        intro hk
        exact Relation.ReflTransGen.tail (ih (by omega)) (hstep k (by omega))
  obtain ⟨i, hi, hei⟩ := he
  obtain ⟨j, hj, hfj⟩ := hf
  have heq : e = edgeAt i hi := Subtype.ext hei
  have hfeq : f = edgeAt j hj := Subtype.ext hfj
  rw [heq, hfeq]
  have hir := hreach0 i hi
  have hjr := hreach0 j hj
  exact (Relation.ReflTransGen.symmetric (fun _ _ => flatAdj_symm) hir).trans hjr

end Setup

PAPER: *"and then `f-x₁-a₁-P₁-b₁-y₁-f` is an odd hole"*.  The cycle is written here as the

PAPER: *"so we assume it has no neighbour in `V(P₁)`.  But then `f` is adjacent to all four of

hole uses only `x₁` and `y₁`.  `Odd (pathLength P₁)` is the first half of **9.1**.

*"If 5.8.1 holds then there is an appearance in `G` of some `K₄`-enlargement, a
contradiction."*

Here `D` is the graph in which 5.8 was applied (in claim (2) it is `G̅`), `c₁, c₂` are the two
vertices of `H` supplied by 5.8.1, and `P` is the path of `F` it supplies.

decls.name: statement_one_or_four_gap
decls.docstring:
**The last clause of claim (2) of 9.3, in its repaired form.**

PAPER (proof of 9.3, printed p. 49): *"... or (up to symmetry) `f, x₁` have the same neighbours
in `V(P₁) ∪ V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₂)` (but then either statement 1 or statement 4 of the theorem
holds)."*

This used to be a `sorry` on a false statement: it asked for `¬ G.Adj f y`, with `y` the end
of the antipath of `x` other than `x`, and that is false when the antipath of `x` is long (a
twin of `x` is a counterexample; see the section "9.3, case 2: 9.3.4 is too strong" of
`REPORT.md`).  With the user-approved repair of outcome 9.3.4 the demand is the one the
argument actually meets: either the neighbour set of `f` in `K` resolves the knot (statement 1
of 9.3), or `f` has a non-neighbour on its own antipath other than `x`.  Since `Q₁` and `Q₂`
are disjoint and `Q'` is the antipath *not* containing `x`, the two conditions `w ∈ Q₁ ∨ w ∈ Q₂`
and `w ∉ Q'` say exactly that `w` lies on the antipath of `x`.

The proof is `Thm93CaseTwoNonmajorRepair.resolves_or_nonneighbour`, which is the dichotomy the
printed argument establishes; the only work here is to name the antipath of `x` in each of the
four symmetric positions and to convert `w ∈ Qx` into `w ∈ Q₁ ∨ w ∈ Q₂` together with
`w ∉ Q'`.

links.rationale: Formalizes the last disjunct of claim (2) of 9.3, repaired to what the argument actually establishes about x1's antipath neighbour.

decls.name: endgame
decls.docstring:
**Claim (2) of 9.3, after 5.8 has been applied in the complement.**

PAPER (proof of 9.3, printed p. 49): *"... so we can apply 5.8 (or, indeed, 5.7) in `G̅`, and
deduce, as before, that either there is a `K₄`-enlargement that appears in `G̅` (a
contradiction), or (up to symmetry) `f, a₁` have the same neighbours in `K \ a₁` (but then
statement 2 of the theorem holds), or (up to symmetry) `f, x₁` have the same neighbours in
`V(P₁) ∪ V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₂)` (but then either statement 1 or statement 4 of the theorem holds)."*

The branch of `H` supplied by 5.8.2 joins two of the four branch-vertices `c₁, c₂, c₃, c₄`.  If
they are consecutive on the square then the branch is a single edge, its image is one of
`a₁, b₁, a₂, b₂`, and the first alternative of the sentence above applies.  If they are
opposite then the branch is one of the two long ones, its image is `Q₁` or `Q₂`, which is odd,
and only 5.8.2(a) survives; that is the second alternative.

links.rationale: Assembles the full trichotomy claim (2) of 9.3 reaches after applying 5.8 in the complement.

`a` have the same neighbours in `W`, provided `T ∩ W ⊆ S` and `a ∉ W`.

decls.name: resolves_or_nonneighbour
decls.docstring:
**The dichotomy that the case-(2) argument of 9.3 really proves.**

PAPER (proof of 9.3, printed p. 49): *"... or (up to symmetry) `f, x₁` have the same neighbours
in `V(P₁) ∪ V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₂)` (but then either statement 1 or statement 4 of the theorem
holds)."*

Either the neighbour set of `f` in `K` resolves the knot — statement 1 of 9.3 — or `f` has a
non-neighbour in `V(Qx) \ {x}`, where `Qx` is the antipath one of whose ends is `x`.
Statement 4 of 9.3 asks for the non-neighbour to be the *other end* `y` of `Qx`; that is the
same thing exactly when `Qx` has length `1`.

by (2) we may apply 6.1.  Since `Q₁` has length `> 1` it follows that the last outcome of 6.1
holds, and hence statement 3 of the theorem holds."*

The first two outcomes of 6.1 are overshadowed appearances of `K₄` in `G̅` and in `G`, both
excluded by hypothesis; the third needs `J = K₃,₃`; the fourth says `|V(H)| = 6`, and then each

length `1`.  The last outcome gives two `G`-adjacent vertices of `F` whose neighbours in `K`
are exactly those of the two ends of one of `P₁, P₂`.

decls.name: three_le_ncard_triple
decls.docstring:
Two vertices of `graph m n` are adjacent exactly when the corresponding two edges of the
host graph are distinct and share an end. -/
theorem edgeOf_meet_iff {m n : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (u v : Vertex m n) :
    (u ≠ v ∧ ∃ w, w ∈ edgeOf m n u ∧ w ∈ edgeOf m n v) ↔ (graph m n).Adj u v := by
  rw [graph_adj_def]
  rcases u with i | j | k <;> rcases v with i' | j' | k'
  · have hi := i.isLt
    have hi' := i'.isLt
    simp only [edgeOf, sym2_meet, Adj, ne_eq, Sum.inl.injEq, Fin.ext_iff, Fin.val_castSucc,
      Fin.val_succ]
    omega
  · simp only [edgeOf, sym2_meet, Adj, Sum.inl.injEq, reduceCtorEq, or_self, and_false]
  · constructor
    · rintro ⟨-, h⟩
      exact (meet_inl_cross hm i k').mp h
    · intro h
      exact ⟨by simp, (meet_inl_cross hm i k').mpr h⟩
  · simp only [edgeOf, sym2_meet, Adj, Sum.inr.injEq, reduceCtorEq, or_self, and_false]
  · have hj := j.isLt
    have hj' := j'.isLt
    simp only [edgeOf, sym2_meet, Adj, ne_eq, Sum.inr.injEq, Sum.inl.injEq, Fin.ext_iff,
      Fin.val_castSucc, Fin.val_succ]
    omega

theorem track_cases (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (u v : Fin 4) :
    (u = 0 ∧ v = 2) ∨ (u = 2 ∧ v = 0) ∨ (u = 1 ∧ v = 3) ∨ (u = 3 ∧ v = 1) ∨
      (track m n u v = [corner m n u, corner m n v] ∧
        track m n v u = [corner m n v, corner m n u] ∧
        (u ≠ v → (host m n).Adj (corner m n u) (corner m n v))) := by
  by_cases h1 : u.val = 0 ∧ v.val = 2
  · exact Or.inl ⟨Fin.ext (by simpa using h1.1), Fin.ext (by simpa using h1.2)⟩
  by_cases h2 : u.val = 2 ∧ v.val = 0
  · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨Fin.ext (by simpa using h2.1), Fin.ext (by simpa using h2.2)⟩)
  by_cases h3 : u.val = 1 ∧ v.val = 3
  · exact Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨Fin.ext (by simpa using h3.1), Fin.ext (by simpa using h3.2)⟩))
  by_cases h4 : u.val = 3 ∧ v.val = 1
  · exact Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl
      ⟨Fin.ext (by simpa using h4.1), Fin.ext (by simpa using h4.2)⟩)))
  refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨track_cross m n u v h1 h2 h3 h4,
    track_cross m n v u (fun h => h2 ⟨h.2, h.1⟩) (fun h => h1 ⟨h.2, h.1⟩)
      (fun h => h4 ⟨h.2, h.1⟩) (fun h => h3 ⟨h.2, h.1⟩), ?_⟩)))
  intro huv
  exact corner_adj hm hn u v h1 h2 h3 h4 huv

theorem track_isTrackFrom (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (u v : Fin 4) (huv : u ≠ v) :
    IsTrackFrom (host m n) (track m n u v) (corner m n u) (corner m n v) := by
  rcases track_cases hm hn u v with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ |
    ⟨he, -, hadj⟩
  · rw [track_02, corner_zero, corner_two]; exact chainA_isTrackFrom
  · rw [track_20, corner_zero, corner_two]
    exact Workspace.ProofLemmas.TrackSlice.isTrackFrom_reverse chainA_isTrackFrom
  · rw [track_13, corner_one, corner_three]; exact chainB_isTrackFrom
  · rw [track_31, corner_one, corner_three]
    exact Workspace.ProofLemmas.TrackSlice.isTrackFrom_reverse chainB_isTrackFrom
  · rw [he]; exact isTrackFrom_pair (hadj huv)

theorem host_bipartite (hem : Even m) (hen : Even n) : (host m n).IsBipartite := by
  have hm2 : m % 2 = 0 := Nat.even_iff.mp hem
  have hn2 : n % 2 = 0 := Nat.even_iff.mp hen
  refine ⟨SimpleGraph.Coloring.mk
    (fun w => match w with
      | .inl i => (⟨i.val % 2, Nat.mod_lt _ (by norm_num)⟩ : Fin 2)
      | .inr j => (⟨(j.val + 1) % 2, Nat.mod_lt _ (by norm_num)⟩ : Fin 2)) ?_⟩
  rintro (i | i) (j | j) hadj <;>
    simp only [host_adj_ll, host_adj_rr, host_adj_lr, host_adj_rl] at hadj <;>
