decls.name: thm_3_3
decls.docstring:
**3.3** (printed p. 13)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, let `C` be a hole in `G` of length ≥ 6, with vertices
`p₁,…,p_m` in order, and let `Q` be an antipath with vertices `p₁,q₁,…,q_n,p₂`, with
length ≥ 4 and even.  Let `z ∈ V(G)`, complete to `V(Q)` and with no neighbours among
`p₃,…,p_m`.  There is at most one vertex in `{p₃,…,p_m}` complete to either
`{q₁,…,q_{n-1}}` or `{q₂,…,q_n}`, and any such vertex is one of `p₃, p_m`."*

The hole is the list `C` of its vertices in cyclic order; naming its first three vertices
`p₁, p₂, p₃` is just the decomposition `C = p₁ :: p₂ :: p₃ :: rest` (always available since
`C` has length ≥ 6), `p_m` is the last vertex of `C`, and `{p₃,…,p_m}` is `C.drop 2`.
The antipath `Q` has interior list `q = [q₁,…,q_n]`, so `{q₁,…,q_{n-1}} = q.dropLast` and
`{q₂,…,q_n} = q.tail`, and `V(Q) = {v | v ∈ Q}`.  The conclusion is the conjunction of
"at most one such vertex" and "any such vertex is `p₃` or `p_m`".

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 3.3 (printed on PDF page 15).

decls.name: glue_hole
decls.docstring:
If `P` and `R` are vertex-disjoint paths and the only edges of `G` between `V(P)`
and `V(R)` are the two joining the last vertex of `P` to the first of `R` and the first
of `P` to the last of `R`, then `P ++ R` is a hole.

decls.name: no_odd_path_star
decls.docstring:
**The "easy check".**  `Nw` is the neighbourhood of `w`.  An odd path whose two ends
are nonadjacent neighbours of `w` and whose interior avoids the neighbourhood of `w`
closes up through `w` into an odd hole.

decls.name: eq_of_reachable_isolated
decls.docstring:
**The "easy check".**  `Nw` is the neighbourhood of `w`.  An odd path whose two ends
are nonadjacent neighbours of `w` and whose interior avoids the neighbourhood of `w`
closes up through `w` into an odd hole. -/
private theorem no_odd_path_star {H : SimpleGraph V}
    (hHberge : ∀ c : List V, IsHoleList H c → Even (holeLength c))
    (w : V) (Nw : Set V) (hNw : ∀ x : V, x ∈ Nw ↔ H.Adj w x)
    (u v : V) (p : List V) (hu : u ∈ Nw) (hv : v ∈ Nw) (hnadj : ¬ H.Adj u v)
    (hp : IsPathFrom H p u v)
    (hint : ∀ x ∈ Workspace.Types.Core.SPGT.interior p, x ∉ Nw) :
    ¬ Odd (pathLength p) := by
  intro hodd
  rw [Nat.odd_iff] at hodd
  have hne1 : pathLength p ≠ 1 := fun h =>
    hnadj (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.isPathFrom_ends_adj_of_length_one hp h)
  have hplen : 4 ≤ p.length := by
    have h := Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.length_eq_pathLength_add_one hp.1
    omega
  -- a vertex of the path lying in `Nw` must be one of the two ends
  have hend : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < p.length), (p[i]'hi) ∈ Nw → (i = 0 ∨ i = p.length - 1) := by
    intro i hi hmem
    by_contra hcon
    push Not at hcon
    exact hint _
      (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.getElem_mem_interior hp.1 hi (by omega) (by omega)) hmem
  have hwu : w ≠ u := by rintro rfl; exact ((hNw w).mp hu).ne rfl
  have hwv : w ≠ v := by rintro rfl; exact ((hNw w).mp hv).ne rfl
  -- `w` is not a vertex of the path
  have hwp : w ∉ p := by
    intro hmem
    have hwint : w ∈ Workspace.Types.Core.SPGT.interior p :=
      (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.mem_interior_iff_of_pathFrom hp).mpr ⟨hmem, hwu, hwv⟩
    obtain ⟨k, hk, hk1, hk2, hkw⟩ :=
      Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.exists_getElem_of_mem_interior hp.1 hwint
    have hm1 : (p[k - 1]'(by omega)) ∈ Nw := by
      refine (hNw _).mpr ?_
      rw [← hkw]
      exact (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.path_adj_iff hp.1 hk
        (show k - 1 < p.length by omega)).mpr (Or.inr (by omega))
    have hm2 : (p[k + 1]'(by omega)) ∈ Nw := by
      refine (hNw _).mpr ?_
      rw [← hkw]
      exact (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.path_adj_iff hp.1 hk
        (show k + 1 < p.length by omega)).mpr (Or.inl rfl)
    have h1 := hend (k - 1) (by omega) hm1
    have h2 := hend (k + 1) (by omega) hm2
    rcases h1 with h1 | h1 <;> rcases h2 with h2 | h2 <;> omega
  -- `w` is adjacent to exactly the two ends
  have hadjw : ∀ x ∈ p, (H.Adj x w ↔ (x = v ∨ x = u)) := by
    intro x hx
    constructor
    · intro hxw
      obtain ⟨i, hi, hix⟩ := List.mem_iff_getElem.mp hx
      have hiN : (p[i]'hi) ∈ Nw := by rw [hix]; exact (hNw x).mpr hxw.symm
      have hpos : 0 < p.length := by omega
      rcases hend i hi hiN with h | h
      · subst h
        right
        rw [← hix]
        exact Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.getElem_zero_of_head? hp.2.1 hpos
      · subst h
        left
        rw [← hix]
        exact Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.getElem_last_of_getLast? hp.2.2 hpos
    · rintro (rfl | rfl)
      · exact ((hNw x).mp hv).symm
      · exact ((hNw x).mp hu).symm
  have hsing : IsPathFrom H [w] w w :=
    ⟨Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.isPathList_singleton H w, by simp, by simp⟩
  have hhole : IsHoleList H (p ++ [w]) := by
    refine glue_hole hp hsing ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro x hx hx'
      rw [List.mem_singleton] at hx'
      subst hx'
      exact hwp hx
    · intro x hx y hy
      rw [List.mem_singleton] at hy
      subst hy
      rw [hadjw x hx]
      constructor
      · rintro (h | h)
        · exact Or.inl ⟨h, rfl⟩
        · exact Or.inr ⟨h, rfl⟩
      · rintro (⟨h, -⟩ | ⟨h, -⟩)
        · exact Or.inl h
        · exact Or.inr h
    · simp only [List.length_singleton]; omega
  have hev : Even ((p ++ [w]).length) := hHberge _ hhole
  simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] at hev
  rw [Nat.even_iff] at hev
  rw [Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.pathLength_eq] at hodd
  omega

/-! #### Connectivity bookkeeping

decls.name: not_connectedSet_of_isolated
decls.docstring:
A set containing two distinct vertices one of which has no neighbour inside it is
not connected.

decls.name: connectedSet_pair
decls.docstring: Two adjacent vertices form a connected set.

decls.name: anticonnected_of_attached
decls.docstring:
If `N` is a nonempty anticonnected subset of `B` and every vertex of `B \ N` has a
non-neighbour in `N`, then `B` is anticonnected.  (This is the maximality of the
anticomponent `B₁` that the paper appeals to.)

decls.name: balanced_of_edge
decls.docstring:
`(V(G) \ {x,y}, {x,y})` is balanced whenever `x` and `y` are adjacent.  (Used only
for the degenerate case `N = ∅`.)

decls.name: balanced_star
decls.docstring:
The heart of 4.1: for `N` the neighbourhood of `a₁` and any `B'` with `N ⊆ B'`,
`a₁ ∉ B'` and `B' \ N` a single vertex complete to `N`, the pair `(V(G) \ B', B')` is
balanced.

decls.name: finish_star
decls.docstring:
The heart of 4.1: for `N` the neighbourhood of `a₁` and any `B'` with `N ⊆ B'`,
`a₁ ∉ B'` and `B' \ N` a single vertex complete to `N`, the pair `(V(G) \ B', B')` is
balanced. -/
private theorem balanced_star {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : Berge G) (a₁ : V) (N B' : Set V)
    (hN : ∀ x : V, x ∈ N ↔ G.Adj a₁ x) (hNB' : N ⊆ B') (ha₁ : a₁ ∉ B')
    (hB : ∀ w ∈ B', w ∉ N → (VertexComplete G w N ∧ ∀ z ∈ B', z ≠ w → z ∈ N)) :
    Workspace.Types.Core.SPGT.Balanced G (B'ᶜ) B' := by
  constructor
  · -- no odd path between nonadjacent vertices of `B'` with interior outside `B'`
    intro u v p hu hv hnadj hp hint hodd
    have hodd' : Odd (pathLength p) := hodd
    rw [Nat.odd_iff] at hodd
    have huv : u ≠ v :=
      Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.isPathFrom_ends_ne hp (by omega)
    have huN : u ∈ N := by
      by_contra hcon
      obtain ⟨hcomp, hall⟩ := hB u hu hcon
      exact hnadj (hcomp v (hall v hv (Ne.symm huv)))
    have hvN : v ∈ N := by
      by_contra hcon
      obtain ⟨hcomp, hall⟩ := hB v hv hcon
      exact hnadj (hcomp u (hall u hu huv)).symm
    exact no_odd_path_star hG.1 a₁ N hN u v p huN hvN hnadj hp
      (fun x hx hxN => hint x hx (hNB' hxN)) hodd'
  · -- no odd antipath between adjacent vertices outside `B'` with interior in `B'`
    intro u v p hu hv hadj hp hint hodd
    have hodd' : Odd (pathLength p) := hodd
    rw [Nat.odd_iff] at hodd
    have hp' : IsPathFrom Gᶜ p u v := Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.isAntipathFrom_iff.mp hp
    have hnadjc : ¬ Gᶜ.Adj u v := fun h => ((SimpleGraph.compl_adj G u v).mp h).2 hadj
    have hune : u ≠ a₁ := by
      intro h; subst h; exact hv (hNB' ((hN v).mpr hadj))
    have hvne : v ≠ a₁ := by
      intro h; subst h; exact hu (hNB' ((hN u).mpr hadj.symm))
    have huNc : Gᶜ.Adj a₁ u :=
      (SimpleGraph.compl_adj G a₁ u).mpr ⟨Ne.symm hune, fun h => hu (hNB' ((hN u).mpr h))⟩
    have hvNc : Gᶜ.Adj a₁ v :=
      (SimpleGraph.compl_adj G a₁ v).mpr ⟨Ne.symm hvne, fun h => hv (hNB' ((hN v).mpr h))⟩
    by_cases hcase : ∀ x ∈ Workspace.Types.Core.SPGT.interior p, x ∈ N
    · refine no_odd_path_star (H := Gᶜ) hG.2 a₁ {z : V | Gᶜ.Adj a₁ z}
        (fun _ => Iff.rfl) u v p huNc hvNc hnadjc hp' ?_ hodd'
      intro x hx hxc
      exact ((SimpleGraph.compl_adj G a₁ x).mp hxc).2 ((hN x).mp (hcase x hx))
    · push Not at hcase
      obtain ⟨w, hwint, hwN⟩ := hcase
      obtain ⟨hcomp, hall⟩ := hB w (hint w hwint) hwN
      have hne1 : pathLength p ≠ 1 := fun h =>
        hnadjc (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.isPathFrom_ends_adj_of_length_one hp' h)
      have hplen : 4 ≤ p.length := by
        have h := Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.length_eq_pathLength_add_one hp'.1
        omega
      obtain ⟨k, hk, hk1, hk2, hkw⟩ :=
        Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.exists_getElem_of_mem_interior hp'.1 hwint
      have hnotint : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < p.length), Gᶜ.Adj w (p[i]'hi) →
          (i = 0 ∨ i = p.length - 1) := by
        intro i hi hadji
        by_contra hcon
        push Not at hcon
        have hmem : (p[i]'hi) ∈ Workspace.Types.Core.SPGT.interior p :=
          Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.getElem_mem_interior hp'.1 hi (by omega) (by omega)
        have hzN : (p[i]'hi) ∈ N := hall _ (hint _ hmem) hadji.ne'
        exact ((SimpleGraph.compl_adj G w _).mp hadji).2 (hcomp _ hzN)
      have hadj1 : Gᶜ.Adj w (p[k - 1]'(by omega)) := by
        rw [← hkw]
        exact (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.path_adj_iff hp'.1 hk
          (show k - 1 < p.length by omega)).mpr (Or.inr (by omega))
      have hadj2 : Gᶜ.Adj w (p[k + 1]'(by omega)) := by
        rw [← hkw]
        exact (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.path_adj_iff hp'.1 hk
          (show k + 1 < p.length by omega)).mpr (Or.inl rfl)
      have h1 := hnotint (k - 1) (by omega) hadj1
      have h2 := hnotint (k + 1) (by omega) hadj2
      rcases h1 with h1 | h1 <;> rcases h2 with h2 | h2 <;> omega

/-! #### Assembling the skew partition

decls.name: key
decls.docstring:
The heart of 4.1: for `N` the neighbourhood of `a₁` and any `B'` with `N ⊆ B'`,
`a₁ ∉ B'` and `B' \ N` a single vertex complete to `N`, the pair `(V(G) \ B', B')` is
balanced. -/
private theorem balanced_star {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : Berge G) (a₁ : V) (N B' : Set V)
    (hN : ∀ x : V, x ∈ N ↔ G.Adj a₁ x) (hNB' : N ⊆ B') (ha₁ : a₁ ∉ B')
    (hB : ∀ w ∈ B', w ∉ N → (VertexComplete G w N ∧ ∀ z ∈ B', z ≠ w → z ∈ N)) :
    Workspace.Types.Core.SPGT.Balanced G (B'ᶜ) B' := by
  constructor
  · -- no odd path between nonadjacent vertices of `B'` with interior outside `B'`
    intro u v p hu hv hnadj hp hint hodd
    have hodd' : Odd (pathLength p) := hodd
    rw [Nat.odd_iff] at hodd
    have huv : u ≠ v :=
      Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.isPathFrom_ends_ne hp (by omega)
    have huN : u ∈ N := by
      by_contra hcon
      obtain ⟨hcomp, hall⟩ := hB u hu hcon
      exact hnadj (hcomp v (hall v hv (Ne.symm huv)))
    have hvN : v ∈ N := by
      by_contra hcon
      obtain ⟨hcomp, hall⟩ := hB v hv hcon
      exact hnadj (hcomp u (hall u hu huv)).symm
    exact no_odd_path_star hG.1 a₁ N hN u v p huN hvN hnadj hp
      (fun x hx hxN => hint x hx (hNB' hxN)) hodd'
  · -- no odd antipath between adjacent vertices outside `B'` with interior in `B'`
    intro u v p hu hv hadj hp hint hodd
    have hodd' : Odd (pathLength p) := hodd
    rw [Nat.odd_iff] at hodd
    have hp' : IsPathFrom Gᶜ p u v := Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.isAntipathFrom_iff.mp hp
    have hnadjc : ¬ Gᶜ.Adj u v := fun h => ((SimpleGraph.compl_adj G u v).mp h).2 hadj
    have hune : u ≠ a₁ := by
      intro h; subst h; exact hv (hNB' ((hN v).mpr hadj))
    have hvne : v ≠ a₁ := by
      intro h; subst h; exact hu (hNB' ((hN u).mpr hadj.symm))
    have huNc : Gᶜ.Adj a₁ u :=
      (SimpleGraph.compl_adj G a₁ u).mpr ⟨Ne.symm hune, fun h => hu (hNB' ((hN u).mpr h))⟩
    have hvNc : Gᶜ.Adj a₁ v :=
      (SimpleGraph.compl_adj G a₁ v).mpr ⟨Ne.symm hvne, fun h => hv (hNB' ((hN v).mpr h))⟩
    by_cases hcase : ∀ x ∈ Workspace.Types.Core.SPGT.interior p, x ∈ N
    · refine no_odd_path_star (H := Gᶜ) hG.2 a₁ {z : V | Gᶜ.Adj a₁ z}
        (fun _ => Iff.rfl) u v p huNc hvNc hnadjc hp' ?_ hodd'
      intro x hx hxc
      exact ((SimpleGraph.compl_adj G a₁ x).mp hxc).2 ((hN x).mp (hcase x hx))
    · push Not at hcase
      obtain ⟨w, hwint, hwN⟩ := hcase
      obtain ⟨hcomp, hall⟩ := hB w (hint w hwint) hwN
      have hne1 : pathLength p ≠ 1 := fun h =>
        hnadjc (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.isPathFrom_ends_adj_of_length_one hp' h)
      have hplen : 4 ≤ p.length := by
        have h := Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.length_eq_pathLength_add_one hp'.1
        omega
      obtain ⟨k, hk, hk1, hk2, hkw⟩ :=
        Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.exists_getElem_of_mem_interior hp'.1 hwint
      have hnotint : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < p.length), Gᶜ.Adj w (p[i]'hi) →
          (i = 0 ∨ i = p.length - 1) := by
        intro i hi hadji
        by_contra hcon
        push Not at hcon
        have hmem : (p[i]'hi) ∈ Workspace.Types.Core.SPGT.interior p :=
          Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.getElem_mem_interior hp'.1 hi (by omega) (by omega)
        have hzN : (p[i]'hi) ∈ N := hall _ (hint _ hmem) hadji.ne'
        exact ((SimpleGraph.compl_adj G w _).mp hadji).2 (hcomp _ hzN)
      have hadj1 : Gᶜ.Adj w (p[k - 1]'(by omega)) := by
        rw [← hkw]
        exact (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.path_adj_iff hp'.1 hk
          (show k - 1 < p.length by omega)).mpr (Or.inr (by omega))
      have hadj2 : Gᶜ.Adj w (p[k + 1]'(by omega)) := by
        rw [← hkw]
        exact (Workspace.ProofLemmas.PathBasics.path_adj_iff hp'.1 hk
          (show k + 1 < p.length by omega)).mpr (Or.inl rfl)
      have h1 := hnotint (k - 1) (by omega) hadj1
      have h2 := hnotint (k + 1) (by omega) hadj2
      rcases h1 with h1 | h1 <;> rcases h2 with h2 | h2 <;> omega

/-! #### Assembling the skew partition -/

private theorem finish_star {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : Berge G) (A B : Set V)
    (hdisj : Disjoint A B) (a₁ a' : V) (ha₁ : a₁ ∈ A) (ha' : a' ∈ A) (hne : a' ≠ a₁)
    (N B' : Set V) (hN : ∀ x : V, x ∈ N ↔ G.Adj a₁ x) (hNB' : N ⊆ B') (hB'B : B' ⊆ B)
    (hB : ∀ w ∈ B', w ∉ N → (VertexComplete G w N ∧ ∀ z ∈ B', z ≠ w → z ∈ N))
    (hnac : ¬ AnticonnectedSet G B') :
    AdmitsBalancedSkewPartition G := by
  have ha₁B' : a₁ ∉ B' := fun h => (Set.disjoint_left.mp hdisj ha₁) (hB'B h)
  have ha'B' : a' ∉ B' := fun h => (Set.disjoint_left.mp hdisj ha') (hB'B h)
  refine ⟨B'ᶜ, B', ⟨⟨?_, ?_, ?_, hnac⟩, balanced_star hG a₁ N B' hN hNB' ha₁B' hB⟩⟩
  · exact Set.compl_union_self B'
  · exact disjoint_compl_left
  · refine not_connectedSet_of_isolated (X := B'ᶜ) ha₁B' ha'B' (Ne.symm hne) ?_
    intro z hz hadjz
    exact hz (hNB' ((hN z).mpr hadjz))

private theorem finish_edge {G : SimpleGraph V} (A B : Set V) (hdisj : Disjoint A B)
    (a₁ a' : V) (ha₁ : a₁ ∈ A) (ha' : a' ∈ A) (hne : a' ≠ a₁)
    (hiso : ∀ z : V, ¬ G.Adj a₁ z) (x y : V) (hx : x ∈ B) (hy : y ∈ B) (hxy : G.Adj x y) :
    AdmitsBalancedSkewPartition G := by
  have hmem : ∀ c : V, c ∈ A → c ∉ ({x, y} : Set V) := by
    intro c hc hcm
    rcases (show c = x ∨ c = y from hcm) with rfl | rfl
    · exact (Set.disjoint_left.mp hdisj hc) hx
    · exact (Set.disjoint_left.mp hdisj hc) hy
  refine ⟨({x, y} : Set V)ᶜ, ({x, y} : Set V), ⟨⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩, balanced_of_edge hxy⟩⟩
  · exact Set.compl_union_self _
  · exact disjoint_compl_left
  · exact not_connectedSet_of_isolated (X := ({x, y} : Set V)ᶜ) (hmem a₁ ha₁) (hmem a' ha')
      (Ne.symm hne) (fun z _ => hiso z)
  · refine not_connectedSet_of_isolated (G := Gᶜ) (X := ({x, y} : Set V))
      (show x ∈ ({x, y} : Set V) by simp) (show y ∈ ({x, y} : Set V) by simp) hxy.ne ?_
    intro z hz hadjz
    rcases (show z = x ∨ z = y from hz) with rfl | rfl
    · exact hadjz.ne rfl
    · exact ((SimpleGraph.compl_adj G x z).mp hadjz).2 hxy

links.rationale: The body of the printed proof of 4.2 in the case it reduces to (some vertex in B has no neighbour in some component of A): it carries out the paper's minimal-configuration choice and the ensuing case analysis that establishes (A,B) is balanced.

decls.name: thm_4_1
decls.docstring:
**4.1** (printed p. 14)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, and suppose that `G` admits a skew partition `(A,B)` such that
either some component of `A` or some anticomponent of `B` has only one vertex.  Then `G`
admits a balanced skew partition."*

Transcription notes.

* *"`G` admits a skew partition `(A,B)` such that …"* is rendered by naming the witnessing
  partition: `(A,B)` is a skew partition of `G` satisfying the stated side condition.
* *"has only one vertex"* is `∃ a, A' = {a}`, i.e. the set is a singleton.
* The two alternatives appear in the order printed.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 4.1 (printed on PDF page 16).

decls.name: balanced_mono
decls.docstring: Balancedness is inherited by subsets on both sides.

links.rationale: Balancedness of a pair (A,B) is inherited by subsets on both sides — used in the proof of 4.2 to restrict a balanced pair down to the vertices that matter.
Shrinking the right-hand set preserves anticompleteness — a monotonicity lemma used to assemble the anticomplete splits in the proof of 4.2.
Shrinking the left-hand set preserves anticompleteness — a monotonicity lemma used to assemble the anticomplete splits in the proof of 4.2.

decls.name: nonempty_of_not_connected
decls.docstring:
A nonempty set that is not connected is nonempty — the complement-free half of
`LooseSkewPartition.nonempty_of_not_anticonnected`.

links.rationale: A set that fails to be connected is nonempty — the complement-free counterpart of LooseSkewPartition.nonempty_of_not_anticonnected, used to extract nonemptiness of the disconnected side A of the skew partition in the proof of 4.2.

decls.name: anticomplete_diff
decls.docstring: A component `C` of `A` is anticomplete to the rest of `A`.

links.rationale: A component C of A is anticomplete to the rest of A \ C — bookkeeping used to split A around the chosen component A1 in the proof of 4.2.

decls.name: isComponent_self
decls.docstring: Any connected set is a component of itself.

links.rationale: A connected set is trivially a component of itself — a base case used to seed the component-splitting arguments in the proof of 4.2.

decls.name: isComponent_of_split
decls.docstring: A component of `S` is a component of any `A = S ∪ T` with `S` anticomplete to `T`.

links.rationale: A component of S remains a component of A = S ∪ T whenever S is anticomplete to T — used to recompute components after moving a vertex between the two sides of the skew partition in the proof of 4.2.

decls.name: not_connectedSet_of_split

decls.name: exists_ne_of_two

decls.name: ncard_le_card

decls.name: key
decls.docstring:
**The body of the printed proof of 4.2**, in the case the paper reduces to: *"some vertex
in `B` has no neighbour in some component of `A`"*.

*"With `G` fixed, let us choose the skew partition `(A,B)` and a component `A₁` of `A` and an
anticomponent `B₁` of `B` with `|B| − 2|B₁|` minimum, such that some vertex in `B₁` (say `b₁`)
has no neighbour in `A₁`."*  Since `B₁ ⊆ B`, the integer `|B| − 2|B₁|` equals
`|B \ B₁| − |B₁|`; the natural number `|B \ B₁| + (|V(G)| − |B₁|)` differs from it by the
constant `|V(G)|`, so minimising the one minimises the other.

links.rationale: The body of the printed proof of 4.2 in the case it reduces to (some vertex in B has no neighbour in some component of A): it carries out the paper's minimal-configuration choice and the ensuing case analysis that establishes (A,B) is balanced.

decls.name: thm_4_2
decls.docstring:
**4.2** (printed p. 15)

PAPER: *"If `G` is Berge, and admits a loose skew partition, then it admits a balanced skew
partition."*

*Loose* is the printed-p.-15 notion: *"a skew partition `(A,B)` of `G` is loose if either some
vertex in `B` has no neighbour in some component of `A`, or some vertex in `A` is complete to
some anticomponent of `B`"*; `AdmitsLooseSkewPartition G` says some skew partition of `G` is
loose.

decls.docstring:
**The union of two paths with the same ends, whose interiors are disjoint and
anticomplete, is a hole** — the paper's `P₁ ∪ P₂`.  Its length is the sum of the lengths of

decls.docstring:

`A₁`."*  If the two paths have the same ends and the sum of their lengths is odd, then in a

decls.name: case_one
decls.docstring:
**The first alternative of 4.3.**

PAPER: *"There is an even path `P₁` and an odd path `P₂` joining `u,v`, both with interior in
`A`.  Let `A₁` be the component of `A` including the interior of `P₁`.  Since `P₁ ∪ P₂` is not
a hole, it follows that `P₂` also has interior in `A₁`.  Let `A₂` be another component of `A`.
If `u,v` are joined by a path with interior in `A₂`, then its union with one of `P₁`, `P₂`
would be an odd hole, a contradiction; so there is no such path.  Hence one of `u,v` has no
neighbours in `A₂`, and hence `(A,B)` is loose."*

links.rationale: Discharges the quoted sentence from the paper's 4.3.

decls.name: thm_4_3
decls.docstring:
**4.3** (printed p. 15)

PAPER: *"Let `(A,B)` be a skew partition of a Berge graph `G`.  If either:*

*• there exist `u,v ∈ B` joined by an odd path with interior in `A`, and joined by an even
path with interior in `A`, or*

*• there exist `u,v ∈ A` joined by an odd antipath with interior in `B`, and joined by an even
antipath with interior in `B`,*

*then `(A,B)` is loose and therefore `G` admits a balanced skew partition."*

Transcription notes.

* In each alternative the *same* pair `u,v` carries both the odd and the even path (resp.
  antipath), so the two paths `p` (odd) and `p'` (even) are bound together with `u,v`.
* The paper does **not** require `u,v` to be nonadjacent (in the first alternative) or
  adjacent (in the second), nor `u ≠ v`, so no such conjunct is added.
* The conclusion is the conjunction of both asserted facts: `(A,B)` is loose, *and* `G`
  admits a balanced skew partition.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 4.3 (printed on PDF page 17).

decls.name: antipathPair_of_pathPair_compl
decls.docstring:
A path pair of `(Ḡ; B, A)` is an antipath pair of `(G; A, B)`.  (The two ends of the odd
path are distinct, so `¬ Ḡ`-adjacent is the same as `G`-adjacent for them.)

links.rationale: Duality lemma used in the proof of 4.4: a path pair of the complement graph (Ḡ; B, A) transfers to an antipath pair of (G; A, B), since the odd path's distinct ends make non-adjacency in Ḡ the same as adjacency in G for them.

decls.name: thm_4_4
decls.docstring:
**4.4** (printed p. 16)

PAPER: *"Let `(A,B)` be a skew partition of a Berge graph `G`, and let `A₁,…,A_m` be the
components of `A`, and `B₁,…,B_n` the anticomponents of `B`.  Then either:*

*• `(A,B)` is loose or balanced, or*

*• `(A_i,B_j)` is a path pair for all `i,j` with `1 ≤ i ≤ m` and `1 ≤ j ≤ n`, or*

*• `(A_i,B_j)` is an antipath pair for all `i,j` with `1 ≤ i ≤ m` and `1 ≤ j ≤ n`."*

Transcription notes.

* `A₁,…,A_m` is just an enumeration of *all* components of `A`, and `B₁,…,B_n` of all
  anticomponents of `B`; since the last two alternatives range over all `i` and all `j`, they
  are rendered by universal quantification over all components `A'` of `A` and all
  anticomponents `B'` of `B`.
* *"`(A,B)` is loose or balanced"*: `(A,B)` is a skew partition by hypothesis, so *balanced*
  here is the balanced-skew-partition notion (equivalently, under that hypothesis, the pair
  `(A,B)` being balanced in the sense of `SPGT.Balanced`).
* *Path pair* and *antipath pair* are the printed-p.-16 notions
  (`SkewTools.IsPathPair`, `SkewTools.IsAntipathPair`), which carry along the standing context
  "`(A,B)` is a skew partition, `A'` a component of `A`, `B'` an anticomponent of `B`".

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 4.4 (printed on PDF page 18).

decls.name: thm_4_5
decls.docstring:
**4.5** (printed p. 17)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge.  Suppose that there is a partition of `V(G)` into four nonempty
sets `X,Y,L,R`, such that there are no edges between `L` and `R`, and `X` is complete to `Y`.
If either:*

*• some vertex in `X ∪ Y` has no neighbours in `L` or no neighbours in `R`, or*

*• some vertex in `L ∪ R` is complete to `X` or complete to `Y`, or*

*• `(L,Y)` is balanced*

*then `G` admits a balanced skew partition."*

Transcription notes.

* *"a partition of `V(G)` into four nonempty sets"* is: the four sets cover `V(G)`, are
  pairwise disjoint, and each is nonempty.
* *"there are no edges between `L` and `R`"* is `Anticomplete G L R`, and *"`X` is complete to
  `Y`"* is `Complete G X Y`.
* *"has no neighbours in `L`"* is `VertexAnticomplete G v L`; *"is complete to `X`"* is
  `VertexComplete G v X`.
* *"`(L,Y)` is balanced"* is the pair-balancedness of `Core`, with the sets in the printed
  order: no odd path between nonadjacent vertices of `Y` with interior in `L`, and no odd
  antipath between adjacent vertices of `L` with interior in `Y`.
* The three alternatives appear in the order printed.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 4.5 (printed on PDF page 19).

decls.name: thm_4_6
decls.docstring:
**4.6** (printed p. 17)

PAPER: *"Let `(A,B)` be a skew partition of a Berge graph `G`, and let `W` be a kernel for it.
Let `A₁` be a component of `A`, and suppose that*

*• every pair of nonadjacent vertices of `W` with neighbours in `A₁` are joined by an even
path with interior in `A`*

*• every pair of adjacent vertices of `A₁` with nonneighbours in `W` are joined by an even
antipath with interior in `B`.*

*Then `G` admits a balanced skew partition."*

Transcription notes.

* This is the **published** form.  The arXiv v1 draft asked for the even path to have
  interior in `A₁` and the even antipath to have interior in `W`; the published paper asks
  only for interior in `A`, resp. in `B`.  As `A₁ ⊆ A` and `W ⊆ B`, the published hypotheses
  are weaker and the published theorem is therefore strictly stronger; it is the published
  form that is transcribed.  (Consistently, the arXiv proof is one line and the published
  proof runs to a page.)
* *Kernel* is the printed-p.-17 notion (`SkewTools.IsKernel`): an anticonnected subset `W` of
  `B` such that some component of `A` contains no `W`-complete vertex.  It carries the
  standing context "`(A,B)` is a skew partition of `G`", which is also stated separately here
  as the paper does.
* *"a pair of nonadjacent vertices of `W` **with neighbours in `A₁`**"* means that each of the
  two vertices has a neighbour in `A₁`; *"a pair of adjacent vertices of `A₁` **with
  nonneighbours in `W`**"* means that each of the two has a nonneighbour in `W`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 4.6 (printed on PDF page 19).

decls.name: thm_5_1
decls.docstring:
**5.1** (printed p. 18)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, and assume some nondegenerate `L(H)` is an induced subgraph of
`G`, where `H` is a bipartite subdivision of `K₄`.  Then either `G` is a line graph, or `G`
admits a proper 2-join, or `G` admits a balanced skew partition.  In particular, 1.8.1
holds."*

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 5.1 (printed on PDF page 20).
The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 5.2 (printed on PDF page 20).

decls.name: thm_5_3
decls.docstring:
**5.3** (printed p. 20)

PAPER: *"Let `H` be bipartite and cyclically 3-connected.  Then either `H = K₃,₃`, or `H` is
a subdivision of `K₄`, or `H` has a subgraph `H'` such that `H'` is a subdivision of `K₄` and
`L(H')` is nondegenerate."*

Transcription notes.

* *"a subgraph `H'` of `H`"* is a `SimpleGraph.Subgraph` of `H` — a set of vertices together
  with a set of edges among them, not necessarily induced and not necessarily proper — and
  the graph it *is* is `S.coe`.
* *"`L(H')` is nondegenerate"* is the printed-p.-18 notion for a subdivision of `K₄`, i.e.
  `NondegenerateAppearance K₄ S.coe`, which unfolds to `¬ DegenerateK4Appearance S.coe`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 5.3 (printed on PDF page 22).

decls.name: thm_5_4
decls.docstring:
**5.4** (printed p. 21)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge.  Let `J` be a 3-connected graph, such that there is no
`J`-enlargement with a nondegenerate appearance in `G`.  Let `L(H₀)` be an appearance of `J`
in `G`, such that if `L(H₀)` is degenerate, then `H₀ = J = K₃,₃` and no `J`-enlargement
appears in `Ḡ`.  Then either `G = L(H₀)`, or `H₀ ≠ K₃,₃` and `G` admits a proper 2-join, or
`G` admits a balanced skew partition."*

Transcription notes.

* The side condition *"`H₀ ≠ K₃,₃` and"* on the second alternative is **new in the published
  version** (the arXiv v1 draft had only *"`G` admits a 2-join"*) and is mathematically
  essential — it is exactly what makes the published 5.2 have no 2-join outcome.  It is
  transcribed as a conjunct of that alternative.
* *"`G = L(H₀)`"* is `Nonempty (G ≃g L(H₀))`: under the equality convention of printed p. 20
  the appearance `L(H₀)` *is* the induced subgraph `G|K₀`, so `G = L(H₀)` says that this
  induced subgraph is all of `G`.
* *"`H₀ = J = K₃,₃`"* is the conjunction `H₀ ≅ K₃,₃` and `J ≅ K₃,₃`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 5.4 (printed on PDF page 23).

decls.name: thm_5_5
decls.docstring:
**5.5** (printed p. 21)

PAPER: *"Let `H` be cyclically 3-connected, and let `C, D` be subgraphs with `C ∪ D = H`,
`|V(C ∩ D)| ≤ 2`, and `V(C), V(D) ≠ V(H)`.  Then one of `C, D` is contained in a branch of
`H`."*

(The paper adds immediately after: *"The proof is clear."*)

Transcription notes.

* `C, D` are `SimpleGraph.Subgraph`s of `H`; `C ∪ D` is `C ⊔ D` and *"`= H`"* is `= ⊤`;
  `C ∩ D` is `C ⊓ D`, whose vertex set is `C.verts ∩ D.verts`; and `V(H) = Set.univ`.
* *"`C` is contained in a branch of `H`"*: a branch is a track, given by the list `q` of its
  vertices, so containment is `C.verts ⊆ V(q)` together with `C.edgeSet ⊆ trackEdges q`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 5.5 (printed on PDF page 23).

decls.name: thm_5_6
decls.docstring:
**5.6** (printed p. 21)

PAPER: *"Let `c₁, c₂` be nonadjacent vertices of a graph `H`, such that `H \ {c₁, c₂}` is
connected.  For `i = 1, 2`, let the edges incident with `cᵢ` be partitioned into two sets
`Aᵢ, Bᵢ`, where `A₁, A₂` are both nonempty and at least one of `B₁, B₂` is nonempty.  Assume
that for every edge `uv ∈ A₁ ∪ A₂`, `H \ {u, v}` is connected, and that no vertex of `V(H)`
is incident with all edges in `A₁ ∪ A₂`.  Then one of the following holds:*

*1. there is a track in `H` with first edge in `A₁`, second edge in `B₁` (and hence second
vertex `c₁`), last vertex `c₂` and last edge in `A₂`, or*

*2. there is a track in `H` with first edge in `A₂`, second edge in `B₂` (and hence second
vertex `c₂`), last vertex `c₁` and last edge in `A₁`."*

Transcription notes.

* *"the edges incident with `cᵢ` are partitioned into two sets `Aᵢ, Bᵢ`"*: `Aᵢ ∪ Bᵢ = δ_H(cᵢ)`
  and `Aᵢ, Bᵢ` are disjoint.  Empty parts are allowed — the paper separately demands that
  `A₁, A₂` be nonempty and that at least one of `B₁, B₂` be nonempty.
* *"`H \ S` is connected"* is `ConnectedSet H Sᶜ`, following the paper's own convention that
  a set `X` is connected when `H|X` is connected (so `∅` counts as connected).
* A track is the list `q` of its vertices in order; the guard `3 ≤ q.length` (equivalently
  `2 ≤ trackLength q`) is exactly what it means for the track to *have* a second edge, and is
  needed for `s(q[1], q[2])` to be well-formed.  The first edge is `s(q[0], q[1])`, the second
  is `s(q[1], q[2])`, the last vertex is `q.getLast?` and the last edge is
  `s(q[q.length-2], q[q.length-1])`.
* The parenthetical *"(and hence second vertex `c₁`)"* is flagged by the paper as a
  consequence of the first two conditions, not as an extra requirement, so it is not a
  conjunct.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 5.6 (printed on PDF page 23).

decls.name: thm_5_7
decls.docstring:
**5.7** (printed p. 22)

PAPER: *"Let `H` be bipartite and cyclically 3-connected.  Let `X ⊆ E(H)`, such that there is
no track in `H` of even length `≥ 4`, with its end-edges in `X` and with no other edge in `X`.
Then either:*

*1. `X` saturates `L(H)`, or*

*2. there is a branch-vertex `b` of `H` with `X ⊆ δ(b)`, or*

*3. there is a branch `B` of `H` with `X ⊆ E(B)`, or*

*4. there is a branch `B` of `H` with ends `b₁, b₂` say, such that `X \ E(B) = δ(b₁) \ E(B)`,
or*

*5. there is a branch `B` of `H` of odd length with ends `b₁, b₂` say, such that*
*`X \ E(B) = (δ(b₁) ∪ δ(b₂)) \ E(B)`,*
*or*

*6. there are two vertices `c₁, c₂` of `H`, of different biparity and not in the same branch
of `H`, such that `X = δ(c₁) ∪ δ(c₂)`.*

*In particular, either statements 1 or 6 hold, or there are at most two branch-vertices of `H`
incident with more than one edge in `X`; and exactly two only if statement 5 holds."*

Transcription notes.

* This is the **published** one-hypothesis / six-alternative form (the arXiv v1 draft split it
  into two statements with different hypotheses and alternatives).
* The hypothesis: a track of even length `≥ 4` is a list `q` with `5 ≤ q.length` (equivalently
  `4 ≤ trackLength q`) and `Even (trackLength q)`; its end-edges are `s(q[0], q[1])` and
  `s(q[q.length-2], q[q.length-1])`; *"no other edge in `X`"* says every edge of the track
  other than those two is outside `X`.
* The final *"In particular …"* sentence is part of the statement (it is what the rest of the
  paper cites as 5.7.1–5.7.6), so the conclusion is the conjunction of the six-fold
  disjunction with that sentence.  *"branch-vertices of `H` incident with more than one edge
  in `X`"* is `{b ∈ branchVertices H | (δ_H(b) ∩ X).Nontrivial}`, and *"at most two"* /
  *"exactly two"* are stated with `Set.ncard`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 5.7 (printed on PDF page 24).

decls.name: thm_5_8
decls.docstring:
**5.8** (printed p. 25)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, let `J` be a 3-connected graph, and let `L(H)` be an appearance of
`J` in `G`.  For each vertex `v` of `J`, let `N_v` be the set of edges of `H` incident with
`v`; and for each edge `uv` of `J`, let `R_uv` be the path of `L(H)` with vertex set the set
of edges of the branch of `H` between `u` and `v`.  Let `F ⊆ V(G) \ V(L(H))` be connected,
such that the set of attachments of `F` in `L(H)` is not local.  Assume that no member of `F`
is major.  Then there is a path `P` of `G` with `V(P) ⊆ F` and with ends `p₁` and `p₂`, such
that either:*

*1. there are vertices `c₁, c₂` of `H`, not in the same branch of `H`, such that for
`i = 1, 2` `pᵢ` is complete in `G` to `N_{cᵢ}`, and there are no other edges between `V(P)`
and `V(L(H))`, or*

*2. there is an edge `b₁b₂` of `J` such that one of the following holds (for `i = 1, 2`, `rᵢ`
denotes the unique vertex in `N_{bᵢ} ∩ V(R_{b₁b₂})`):*

*(a) `p₁` is adjacent in `G` to all vertices in `N_{b₁} \ {r₁}`, and `p₂` has a neighbour in
`R_{b₁b₂} \ r₁`, and every edge from `V(P)` to `V(L(H)) \ {r₁}` is either from `p₁` to
`N_{b₁} \ {r₁}`, or from `p₂` to `V(R_{b₁b₂}) \ {r₁}`, or*

*(b) for `i = 1, 2`, `pᵢ` is adjacent in `G` to all vertices in `N_{bᵢ} \ {rᵢ}`, and there are
no other edges between `V(P)` and `V(L(H))` except possibly `p₁r₁, p₂r₂`, and `P` has the same
parity as `R_{b₁b₂}`, or*

*(c) `p₁ = p₂`, and `p₁` is adjacent to all vertices in `(N_{b₁} ∪ N_{b₂}) \ {r₁, r₂}`, and
all neighbours of `p₁` in `V(L(H))` belong to `N_{b₁} ∪ N_{b₂} ∪ V(R_{b₁b₂})`, and `R_{b₁b₂}`
is even, or*

*(d) `r₁ = r₂`, and for `i = 1, 2`, `pᵢ` is adjacent in `G` to all vertices in
`N_{bᵢ} \ {rᵢ}`, and there are no other edges between `V(P)` and `V(L(H)) \ {r₁}`, and `P` is
even."*

Transcription notes.

* The appearance is given by the bipartite subdivision `H` of `J`, the vertex set `K` of the
  induced subgraph of `G`, and the isomorphism `φ : L(H) ≃g G|K` (together `hsub` and `φ` are
  `IsAppearance G J H K`).  So `V(L(H)) = K`, and the vertex of `G` corresponding to an edge
  `e` of `H` is `↑(φ ⟨e, he⟩)`.
* `N_v` is introduced inside the statement and is bound here as the parameter `N`, pinned down
  by `hN`: it is `δ_H(v)` read as a subset of `V(L(H))` and then transported into `V(G)` by
  `φ` (the paper: *"the set `N_v` is just the set `δ_H(v)`, but now we are going to think of
  it as a subset of the vertex set of `L(H)`"*).  Statement 1 applies `N` to arbitrary
  vertices `c₁, c₂` of `H`, so `N` is defined for every vertex of `H`.
* `R_{b₁b₂}` is likewise introduced inside the statement; it is bound inside alternative 2,
  where it is used, as a path `R` of `G` whose vertex set is the `φ`-image of the edge set of
  the branch `q` of `H` between `b₁` and `b₂`.  *"The unique vertex in `N_{bᵢ} ∩ V(R_{b₁b₂})`"*
  pins down `rᵢ` by `N bᵢ ∩ V(R) = {rᵢ}`.
* *"an edge `b₁b₂` of `J`"* is rendered, as everywhere in this file, as *"a branch of `H` with
  ends `b₁, b₂`"*, with `b₁, b₂` branch-vertices of `H` (`= V(J)`, printed p. 20).
* In 2(a) the paper writes the bare `R_{b₁b₂} \ r₁` once and `V(R_{b₁b₂}) \ {r₁}` a few words
  later; both are transcribed with the intended reading `V(R_{b₁b₂}) \ {r₁}`.
* *"`P` has the same parity as `R_{b₁b₂}`"* is `Even (pathLength P) ↔ Even (pathLength R)`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 5.8 (printed on PDF page 27).

decls.name: thm_6_1
decls.docstring:
**6.1** (printed p. 28)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, let `L(H)` be an appearance in `G` of a 3-connected graph `J`, and
let `Y` be an anticonnected set of major vertices.  Assume that the set of all `Y`-complete
vertices in `L(H)` does not saturate `L(H)`.  Then either*

*• `J = K₃,₃` or `K₄`, and there is an overshadowed appearance of `J` in `G`, or*

*• `J = K₃,₃` or `K₄`, `L(H)` is degenerate, and there is an overshadowed appearance of `J` in
`Ḡ`, or*

*• `J = K₃,₃`, `L(H)` is degenerate, and there is a `J`-enlargement that appears in `Ḡ`, or*

*• `J = K₄` and `|V(H)| = 6`, or*

*• `J = K₄` and `L(H)` is degenerate, and there exist nonadjacent `y, y' ∈ Y` with the
following property.  Let the 4-cycle in `H` formed by the branch-vertices of `H` have edges
`a`-`b`-`c`-`d` in order.  Let `p` be the third edge of `H` such that `a, b, p` have a common
end, and similarly let `b, c, q` have a common end, and `c, d, r` and `d, a, s`.  Then (up to
symmetry) the neighbours of `y` in `L(H)` are `a, b, d, q, r` and possibly `c`, and the
neighbours of `y'` in `L(H)` are `b, c, d, p, s` and possibly `a`."*

Transcription notes.

* The appearance is given by the bipartite subdivision `H` of `J` (`hsub`), the vertex set `K`
  of the induced subgraph of `G`, and the isomorphism `φ : L(H) ≃g G|K`; together `hsub` and
  `φ` are `IsAppearance G J H K`.
* *"a set of major vertices"* is `∀ y ∈ Y, MajorForLineGraph G H K φ y`; that definition
  already contains `y ∉ K`, i.e. the paper's implicit `Y ⊆ V(G) \ V(L(H))`.
* The four vertices of the 4-cycle of bullet 5 are `v₁,v₂,v₃,v₄`; *"the 4-cycle in `H` formed
  by the branch-vertices of `H`"* is that they are distinct, are exactly the branch-vertices
  of `H`, and are cyclically adjacent.  Its edges *in order* are then
  `a = v₁v₂`, `b = v₂v₃`, `c = v₃v₄`, `d = v₄v₁`.
* *"the third edge of `H` such that `a, b, p` have a common end"*: `a` and `b` meet at `v₂`,
  and `p` is an edge incident with `v₂` other than `a` and `b`.  (`v₂` is a branch-vertex of a
  subdivision of `K₄`, hence has degree exactly `3`, which is what makes such a `p` unique;
  uniqueness is a consequence and is not asserted.)  Likewise `q` at `v₃`, `r` at `v₄` and `s`
  at `v₁`.
* *"the neighbours of `y` in `L(H)` are `a, b, d, q, r` and possibly `c`"* is the pair of
  inclusions `{a,b,d,q,r} ⊆ N(y) ∩ V(L(H)) ⊆ {a,b,c,d,q,r}`, with the neighbour set read back
  as a set of edges of `H`; likewise for `y'` with `{b,c,d,p,s}` and `{a,b,c,d,p,s}`.
* *"(up to symmetry)"* is absorbed by the existential quantifiers: the labelling `v₁,…,v₄` of
  the 4-cycle (hence of `a,b,c,d`) and the choice of which of the two vertices of `Y` is `y`
  are both existentially bound.
* The five alternatives appear in the order printed, with exactly the printed hypotheses on
  `J` and on degeneracy — in particular bullet 1 puts no degeneracy condition on `L(H)`,
  bullet 2 allows `J = K₃,₃` **or** `K₄`, and bullet 3 allows only `J = K₃,₃`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 6.1 (printed on PDF page 31).

decls.name: thm_7_1
decls.docstring:
**7.1** (printed p. 34)

PAPER: *"Let `c₁, c₂` be adjacent vertices of a 3-connected graph `J`, and let `e, f` be
edges of `J` incident with `c₁` and different from `c₁c₂`.  There are three tracks of `J`
from `c₁` to `c₂`, pairwise vertex-disjoint except for their ends, and with first edges
`c₁c₂, e, f` respectively."*

Notes on the transcription.

* `J` is a host graph, so the objects here are **tracks** (subgraphs, not induced), given
  by the list of their vertices in order (`Tracks.IsTrackFrom`), and 3-connectedness is
  `Tracks.IsKConnected J 3`.
* Edges of `J` are elements of `J.edgeSet ⊆ Sym2 U`; *"incident with `c₁`"* is `c₁ ∈ e`, and
  *"different from `c₁c₂`"* is `e ≠ s(c₁, c₂)`.
* *"with first edge `e`"*: the track starts at `c₁`, so its first edge is `c₁w` where `w` is
  its second vertex; this is written `Q = c₁ :: w :: rest` with `s(c₁, w) = e`.
* *"pairwise vertex-disjoint except for their ends"*: a vertex on two of the three tracks is
  `c₁` or `c₂`.
* The hypothesis `e ≠ f` is **not printed**, but it is the intended reading: the paper's
  one-line proof deletes from `J` every edge incident with `c₁` except `e` and `f` and
  asserts that the result is still 2-connected, which needs `c₁` to keep degree two; and
  with `e = f` the conclusion is outright false, since the two tracks with first edge `e`
  would share their second vertex, which is neither `c₁` nor `c₂`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 7.1 (printed on PDF page 36).

decls.name: thm_7_2
decls.docstring:
**7.2** (printed p. 35)

PAPER: *"Let `R₁, R₂, R₃` form a prism in a Berge graph `G`; then `R₁, R₂, R₃` all have the
same parity."*

(The paper's entire proof reads: *"The proof is clear."*)

*"Form a prism"* is `Prisms.FormPrism G a b R₁ R₂ R₃`, with triangles `{a 0, a 1, a 2}` and
`{b 0, b 1, b 2}`; *"the same parity"* refers to the parities of the three lengths.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 7.2 (printed on PDF page 37).

decls.name: thm_7_3
decls.docstring:
**7.3** (printed p. 35)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, let `Y ⊆ V(G)` be anticonnected, and for `i = 1, 2, 3` let
`aᵢ-Pᵢ-bᵢ` be a path in `G \ Y`, forming a prism with triangles `{a₁, a₂, a₃}`,
`{b₁, b₂, b₃}`.  Assume `P₁, P₂, P₃` all have length `> 1`, and that every vertex in `Y` is
adjacent to at least two of `a₁, a₂, a₃` and to at least two of `b₁, b₂, b₃`.  Then at least
two of `a₁, a₂, a₃` and at least two of `b₁, b₂, b₃` are `Y`-complete."*

Notes on the transcription.

* *"`aᵢ-Pᵢ-bᵢ` is a path in `G \ Y`"*: `Pᵢ` is a path of `G` with ends `aᵢ, bᵢ` (which is
  part of `FormPrism`) none of whose vertices lies in `Y`.
* *"every vertex in `Y` is adjacent to at least two of `a₁, a₂, a₃` and to at least two of
  `b₁, b₂, b₃`"* is verbatim the §10 notion *major with respect to the prism*
  (`MajorForPrism`, i.e. the neighbour set *saturates* the prism), so it is written that way.
* Likewise the conclusion *"at least two of `a₁, a₂, a₃` and at least two of `b₁, b₂, b₃`
  are `Y`-complete"* says that the set of `Y`-complete vertices *saturates* the prism.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 7.3 (printed on PDF page 37).

decls.name: thm_7_4
decls.docstring:
**7.4** (printed p. 35)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, and for `1 ≤ i ≤ 3` let `Pᵢ` be a path of even length `≥ 2`, from
`aᵢ` to `bᵢ`, such that these three paths form a prism with triangles `A = {a₁, a₂, a₃}` and
`B = {b₁, b₂, b₃}`.  Let `P₁'` be a path from `a₁'` to `b₁`, such that `P₁', P₂, P₃` also
form a prism.  Let `y ∈ V(G)` have at least two neighbours in `A` and in `B`.  Then it also
has at least two neighbours in `{a₁', a₂, a₃}`."*

Notes on the transcription.

* *"`P₁', P₂, P₃` also form a prism"*: since `P₁'` has ends `a₁'` and `b₁` and `P₂, P₃` keep
  their ends, the triangles of that prism are `{a₁', a₂, a₃}` and `{b₁, b₂, b₃}`; the first
  is the family `![a₁', a 1, a 2] : Fin 3 → V`.
* *"`y` has at least two neighbours in `A` and in `B`"* is verbatim the §10 notion *major
  with respect to the prism* (`MajorForPrism`), so it is written that way; the conclusion
  concerns only the new triangle, and says that at least two of `a₁', a₂, a₃` are neighbours
  of `y`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 7.4 (printed on PDF page 37).

decls.name: thm_7_5
decls.docstring:
**7.5** (printed p. 35)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, and let `L(H)` be an overshadowed appearance of `J` in `G`, where
`J` is 3-connected.  Then either:*

*• there is a `J`-enlargement with a nondegenerate appearance in `G`, or*

*• `G` admits a balanced skew partition."*

Notes on the transcription.

* An *appearance* `L(H)` of `J` in `G` is the pair `(H, K)` — a bipartite subdivision `H` of
  `J` and the induced subgraph `G|K` that `L(H)` is isomorphic to — together with the
  identification `φ : H.lineGraph ≃g G.induce K` (`Appearances.IsAppearance`); *overshadowed*
  is `Overshadowed.IsOvershadowedAppearance`, which needs the same `φ` because `δ_H(b)` is a
  set of vertices of `L(H)`.
* *"there is a `J`-enlargement with a nondegenerate appearance in `G`"*: some graph `J'` is a
  `J`-enlargement (`Appearances.IsJEnlargement`) and has an appearance in `G` that is
  nondegenerate.  Quantifying the enlargement and the subdivision witnessing its appearance
  over `SimpleGraph (Fin ·)` is this project's rendering of "there is a finite graph such
  that …".
* (The remark preceding 7.5 — *"We shall only need the following when `J = K₄` or `K₃,₃`, but
  we might as well prove it in general."* — is not part of the statement.)

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 7.5 (printed on PDF page 37).

decls.name: thm_8_1
decls.docstring:
**8.1** (printed p. 40)

PAPER: *"Let `(S,N)` be a `J`-strip system in a Berge graph `G`, where `J` is 3-connected.
Then for every `uv ∈ E(J)`, all `uv`-rungs have lengths of the same parity."*

Notes on the transcription.

* A `uv`-rung is `StripSystems.IsUVRung G J S N u v R`, a path of `G` given by the list `R`
  of its vertices in order, and its length is `Core.pathLength R`.
* *"All `uv`-rungs have lengths of the same parity"* is: any two `uv`-rungs have lengths of
  the same parity.  (The `IsUVRung` predicate already carries `J.Adj u v`, so the hypothesis
  `huv` merely records the paper's `uv ∈ E(J)`.)

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 8.1 (printed on PDF page 41).

decls.name: thm_8_2
decls.docstring:
**8.2** (printed p. 40)

PAPER: *"Let `(S,N)` be a `J`-strip system in a Berge graph `G`, where `J` is 3-connected.  If
there is an edge `uv` of `J` such that some `uv`-rung has length 0 and another `uv`-rung has
length `≥ 1`, then there is an overshadowed appearance of `J` in `G`."*

Notes on the transcription.

* *"Some `uv`-rung has length 0 and another `uv`-rung has length `≥ 1`"*: two `uv`-rungs `R`,
  `R'` with `pathLength R = 0` and `1 ≤ pathLength R'` (they are automatically different).
* *"There is an overshadowed appearance of `J` in `G`"*: there are a bipartite subdivision
  `H` of `J`, a vertex set `K'` of `G` and an identification `φ : H.lineGraph ≃g G.induce K'`
  making `L(H)` an appearance of `J` in `G` (`Appearances.IsAppearance`), which is
  overshadowed (`Overshadowed.IsOvershadowedAppearance`).

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 8.2 (printed on PDF page 42).

decls.name: thm_8_3
decls.docstring:
**8.3** (printed p. 40)

PAPER: *"Let `(S,N)` be a nondegenerate `J`-strip system in a Berge graph `G`, where `J` is
3-connected.  If there is no overshadowed appearance of `J` in `G`, then for every choice of
rungs, the line graph they form is a nondegenerate appearance of `J` in `G`."*

Notes on the transcription.

* *"Nondegenerate `J`-strip system"* is `StripSystems.NondegenerateStripSystem` (printed
  p. 40: *"A `J`-strip system is nondegenerate if there is some choice of rungs such that the
  line graph `L(H)` they form is a nondegenerate appearance of `J`"*).
* *"For every choice of rungs, the line graph they form is a nondegenerate appearance of `J`
  in `G`"*: `StripSystems.FormsLineGraph G J S N R H` says that the family `R` is a choice of
  rungs whose union induces an appearance of `J` in `G` via the subdivision `H`; so the
  conclusion is that every such `H` is nondegenerate.  That the formed line graph *exists*
  for every choice of rungs is the paper's remark immediately after the proof of 8.1
  (*"It follows from 8.1 and the final axiom above that the subgraph of `G` induced on the
  union of the vertex sets of these rungs is a line graph of a bipartite subdivision `H` of
  `J`"*), not part of 8.3, and so is not asserted here.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 8.3 (printed on PDF page 42).

decls.name: unsaturatedChoice
decls.docstring:
**"If every choice of rungs is saturated, then `X` saturates the strip system as required, so
we may therefore assume that there is some choice of rungs that is not saturated."**

The contrapositive, which is the form the proof of 8.4 uses.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 8.4 (printed on PDF page 42).

decls.name: thm_8_5
decls.docstring:
**8.5** (printed p. 42)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, let `J` be a 3-connected graph, and let `(S,N)` be a maximal
`J`-strip system in `G`.  Assume that there is no `J`-enlargement with a nondegenerate
appearance in `G`.  Assume moreover that if `J = K₄` then `(S,N)` is nondegenerate and there
is no overshadowed appearance of `J` in `G`.  Let `F ⊆ V(G) \ V(S,N)` be connected, so that no
member of `F` is major with respect to `(S,N)`.  Then the set of attachments of `F` in
`V(S,N)` is local."*

Notes on the transcription.

* This is the **published** form of the statement.  (The arXiv v1 draft `stripnbrs1` had a
  two-bullet *disjunctive* hypothesis — *"either `(S,N)` is nondegenerate and there is no
  `J`-enlargement with a nondegenerate appearance in `G`, or `J = K₃,₃` and there is no
  `J`-enlargement that appears in either `G` or `Ḡ`"* — and a *disjunctive* conclusion
  — *"either `J = K₄` and there is an overshadowed appearance of `J` in `G`, or the set of
  attachments of `F` in `V(S,N)` is local"*.  Both were replaced in the published version by
  the flat hypotheses and the single conclusion transcribed here.)
* *"A maximal `J`-strip system in `G`"* is both conjuncts `IsJStripSystem G J S N` and
  `MaximalStripSystem G J S N` (the latter is *only* the "no larger system" condition; see
  its doc-comment).
* *"`F ⊆ V(G) \ V(S,N)` be connected"* is `F ⊆ (V(S,N))ᶜ` together with `Core.ConnectedSet`,
  which follows the paper in counting `∅` as connected.
* *"The set of attachments of `F` in `V(S,N)`"* is `Appearances.attachments G F (V(S,N))`,
  i.e. `{k ∈ V(S,N) | k has a neighbour in F}`; *"is local"* is
  `StripSystems.LocalForStripSystem`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 8.5 (printed on PDF page 44).
The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 8.6 (printed on PDF page 47).

decls.name: Thm91_compl_adj_iff
decls.docstring: Complementary adjacency to a vertex off the list.

decls.name: Thm91_vertexComplete_interior
decls.docstring:
PAPER: *"`a₁, b₁, a₂, b₂` are all `Y`-complete, from the last condition in the definition
of a knot"* — the last condition says every nonedge between an antipath and `{aᵢ, bᵢ}` uses an
*end* of the antipath, so the interior is seen completely.

decls.name: Thm91_no_interior_adj
decls.docstring:
Dually: an edge from a path to a vertex that only its two ends can carry misses the
interior of the path.

decls.name: thm_9_1
decls.docstring:
**9.1** (printed p. 48)

PAPER: *"Let `(P₁,P₂,Q₁,Q₂)` be a knot in a Berge graph `G`.  Then all four of `P₁,P₂,Q₁,Q₂`
have odd length; and either both `P₁,P₂` have length 1, or both `Q₁,Q₂` have length 1."*

The lengths are `Core.pathLength` (the number of edges; for an antipath, the number of edges
of its complement — the same number).

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 9.1 (printed on PDF page 49).

decls.name: thm_9_2
decls.docstring:
**9.2** (printed p. 48)

PAPER: *"Let `(P₁,P₂,Q₁,Q₂)` be a knot in a graph `G`, inducing `K`, where `Q₁,Q₂` both have
length 1, and so `K = L(H)` is an appearance of `K₄`.  Let `X ⊆ V(K)`.  Then:*

*• `X` is local with respect to the knot if and only if it is local with respect to `L(H)`*

*• `X` resolves the knot if and only if `X` saturates `L(H)` and `X` meets both `V(P₁)` and
`V(P₂)`."*

(The paper adds: *"The proof is obvious and we omit it."*)

Notes on the transcription.

* *"and so `K = L(H)` is an appearance of `K₄`"* is flagged by the paper as a **consequence**
  of the preceding hypotheses; but the statement needs a name for `H`, so `H` and the
  identification `φ : H.lineGraph ≃g G.induce K` are given as data together with the
  hypothesis `IsAppearance G K₄ H K` that they do form an appearance.  Since that hypothesis
  is implied by the others, this is an equivalent statement.
* The two §5 notions on the right-hand sides — *local with respect to `L(H)`*
  (`Appearances.LocalForLineGraph`) and *saturates `L(H)`*
  (`Appearances.SaturatesLineGraph`) — are conditions on a set of **edges of `H`**, those
  being the vertices of `L(H)`.  Under `φ`, the set `X` of vertices of `G` corresponds to the
  set of edges `e` of `H` with `φ e ∈ X`, which is what they are applied to.
* *"`X` meets both `V(P₁)` and `V(P₂)`"* is nonemptiness of the two intersections.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 9.2 (printed on PDF page 50).

decls.name: thm_9_3
decls.docstring:
**9.3** (printed p. 48)

PAPER: *"Let `(P₁,P₂,Q₁,Q₂)` be a knot in a Berge graph `G`, inducing `K`.  Assume that there
is no appearance in `G` or in `Ḡ` of any `K₄`-enlargement, and there is no overshadowed
appearance of `K₄` in `G` or in `Ḡ`.  Let `F` be a connected subset of `V(G) \ V(K)`, such
that its set of attachments in `K` is not local.  Then either:*

*1. there is a vertex in `F` such that its neighbour set in `K` resolves the knot, or*

*2. (up to symmetry) there is a path `R` in `F` with ends `r₁,r₂` such that `r₁,a₁` have the
same neighbours in `V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₁) ∪ V(Q₂)`, and there are no edges between `R \ r₁` and
`V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₁) ∪ V(Q₂)`, and `r₂` has a neighbour in `P₁ \ a₁`, and there are no edges between
`R \ r₂` and `P₁ \ a₁`, or*

*3. (up to symmetry) there is an odd path `R` in `F` with ends `r₁,r₂` such that `r₁,a₁` have
the same neighbours in `V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₁) ∪ V(Q₂)`, and `r₂,b₁` have the same neighbours in
`V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₁) ∪ V(Q₂)`, and there are no edges between `V(R*)` and
`V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₁) ∪ V(Q₂)`, and no edges between `R` and `P₁` except possibly `r₁a₁` and `r₂b₁`,
or*

*4. there is a vertex `f ∈ F` such that (up to symmetry) `f,x₁` have the same neighbours in
`V(P₁) ∪ V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₂)` and `f` is not adjacent to `y₁`."*

The four outcomes are cited elsewhere as 9.3.1–9.3.4 (in the proofs of 9.4 and 9.5); they are
transcribed below in the printed order, as the four disjuncts of the conclusion.

**How "up to symmetry" is discharged.**  PAPER (printed p. 48): *"(The expression 'up to
symmetry' means here 'possibly after exchanging `P₁` and `P₂` and exchanging `Q₁` and `Q₂`,
and renaming the ends of `P₁,P₂,Q₁,Q₂` accordingly.')"*  Writing `V(K)` as the union of the
four vertex sets, the eight ends form an 8-cycle of adjacencies,
`a₁-x₁-a₂-y₂-b₁-y₁-b₂-x₂-a₁` (this is forced by the third and fourth bullets of the
definition of a knot), in which `{a₁,b₁}`, `{a₂,b₂}`, `{x₁,y₁}`, `{x₂,y₂}` are the four
antipodal pairs.  A relabelling of the kind the paper describes is exactly a symmetry of that
8-cycle preserving the path/antipath classes, and the group generated by the two exchanges is
the resulting dihedral group of order 8 (it contains, for instance, the relabelling that
reverses all four of `P₁,P₂,Q₁,Q₂` simultaneously, being the composite of the two exchanges
performed in the two possible orders).  Since each outcome mentions only some of the labels,
the orbit of each outcome under that group is small, and is written out below as an explicit
choice of the labels involved:

* outcome 2 uses one path `P` with a distinguished end `a` (`P'` being the other path, so
  that `V(P') ∪ V(Q₁) ∪ V(Q₂) = V(K) \ V(P)`), and the orbit is
  `(a,P,P') ∈ {(a₁,P₁,P₂), (b₁,P₁,P₂), (a₂,P₂,P₁), (b₂,P₂,P₁)}`;
* outcome 3 uses one path `P` with *both* its ends `a,b` (matched with `r₁,r₂`), and the orbit
  is `(a,b,P,P') ∈ {(a₁,b₁,P₁,P₂), (b₁,a₁,P₁,P₂), (a₂,b₂,P₂,P₁), (b₂,a₂,P₂,P₁)}`;
* outcome 4 uses one antipath with its two ends in a *fixed order* (`f` copies the
  neighbours of the first and is nonadjacent to the second), together with the other antipath
  `Q'`, and the orbit is
  `(x,y,Q') ∈ {(x₁,y₁,Q₂), (y₁,x₁,Q₂), (x₂,y₂,Q₁), (y₂,x₂,Q₁)}`.

Further notes on the transcription.

* *"There is a path `R` in `F`"*: `R` is a path of `G` (the paper's induced notion) all of
  whose vertices lie in `F`; *"odd path"* is `Odd (pathLength R)`; `V(R*)` is
  `Core.interior R`.
* *"`r₁,a₁` have the same neighbours in `W`"* is `∀ w ∈ W, (G.Adj r₁ w ↔ G.Adj a₁ w)`.
* *"There are no edges between `X` and `Y`"* is `Core.Anticomplete G X Y`; `R \ r₁` is
  `V(R) \ {r₁}` and `P₁ \ a₁` is `V(P₁) \ {a₁}`.
* *"No edges between `R` and `P₁` except possibly `r₁a₁` and `r₂b₁`"*: every edge of `G` with
  one end on `R` and the other on `P₁` is one of those two.
* *"Its set of attachments in `K` is not local"* uses `Appearances.attachments` and the §9
  notion `Knots.LocalForKnot` (`local` *with respect to the knot*), which is the notion in
  force throughout this statement.

decls.name: thm_9_4
decls.docstring:
**9.4** (printed p. 51)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, such that there is no appearance in `G` or in `Ḡ` of any
`K₄`-enlargement, and there is no overshadowed appearance of `K₄` in `G` or in `Ḡ`.  Let `L`
be a maximal striation in `G`.  Let `f ∈ V(G) \ V(L)`, and let `X` be the set of neighbours of
`f` in `V(L)`.  Then either `X` is local with respect to `L`, or `X` resolves `L`."*

Notes on the transcription.

* A *striation* `L` is the pair of families `S : Fin m → Set V × Set V × Set V` (the strips)
  and `T : Fin n → Set V × Set V × Set V` (the antistrips); `V(L)` is
  `Knots.striationVertices S T`, and *maximal* is `Knots.MaximalStriation`, which (unlike
  `MaximalStripSystem` in §8) already includes being a striation.
* *"The set of neighbours of `f` in `V(L)`"* is `G.neighborSet f ∩ V(L)`.
* *"Local with respect to `L`"* and *"resolves `L`"* are `Knots.LocalForStriation` and
  `Knots.ResolvesStriation` — the striation notions, not the knot ones.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 9.4 (printed on PDF page 53).

decls.name: thm_9_5
decls.docstring:
**9.5** (printed p. 52)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, such that there is no appearance in `G` or in `Ḡ` of any
`K₄`-enlargement, and there is no overshadowed appearance of `K₄` in `G` or in `Ḡ`.  Let `L`
be a maximal striation in `G`.  Let `F ⊆ V(G) \ V(L)` be connected, such that for each
`f ∈ F`, the set of its neighbours in `V(L)` is local with respect to `L`.  Then the set of
attachments of `F` in `V(L)` is local with respect to `L`."*

Notes on the transcription.

* *"`F ⊆ V(G) \ V(L)` be connected"* is `F ⊆ (V(L))ᶜ` together with `Core.ConnectedSet`,
  which follows the paper in counting `∅` as connected.
* *"The set of attachments of `F` in `V(L)`"* is `Appearances.attachments G F (V(L))`, i.e.
  `{k ∈ V(L) | k has a neighbour in F}`.

decls.name: thm_9_7
decls.docstring:
**9.7** (printed p. 56)

Preceded by: *"It is convenient to combine three earlier results as follows."*

PAPER: *"Let `G` be a Berge graph, such that there is an appearance of `K₄` in `G`.  Then
either one of `G,Ḡ` is a line graph, or `G` is a double split graph, or one of `G,Ḡ` admits a
proper 2-join, or `G` admits a balanced skew partition."*

(Proof of 9.7 in full: *"This is immediate from 9.6, 5.1 and 5.2."*)

Notes on the transcription.

* *"Is a line graph"* is the paper's standing abbreviation for *"is the line graph of a
  bipartite graph"* (`BasicClasses.IsLineGraphOfBipartite`): 9.7 is deduced from 5.1 and 5.2,
  whose corresponding outcomes are *"`G` is a line graph"* and *"`G = L(K₃,₃)`"*, and 5.1 is
  in turn said to give 1.8.1, whose wording is *"`G` is a line graph of a bipartite graph"*.
* *"There is an appearance of `K₄` in `G`"* is `Appearances.Appears G K₄`.
* The four alternatives are transcribed in the printed order; *"proper"* 2-join is the
  published form.

decls.name: case_two_fwd
decls.docstring:
Claim (2) of the printed proof, after relabelling the three paths by `σ`.

**Orientation.**  In claim (2)'s configuration it is `fₙ`, not `f₁`, that acquires the two
triangle neighbours (*"If `fₙ` is adjacent to both `a₂, a₃` then statement 4 of the theorem
holds"*), so the conclusion delivered is the one for the path traversed the other way round,
`Concl … f.reverse fn f₁`.  See `Thm101ClaimTwo.claim_two`.

decls.name: case_three_fwd

Claim (3) of the printed proof.

**Orientation.**  The printed same-parity branch ends *"either `fₙ` is adjacent to `a₃` or `f₁`
to `b₃`"*, and the two sub-cases land on opposite orientations of the path, so claim (3)
delivers a genuine disjunction, which this lemma simply forwards.  See
`Thm101ClaimThree.claim_three`.

decls.name: step
thm_10_1
decls.docstring:
The five-by-five case analysis on the local types of `X₁` and `X₂`, using claims (2), (3)
and the endgame.  Six of the twenty-five cases need the path traversed the other way round;
that is why the disjunction on the right is there. -/
private theorem step (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : Berge G) (a b : Fin 3 → V)
    (R : Fin 3 → List V) (K F : Set V) (f : List V) (f₁ fn : V)
    (hprism : FormPrism G a b (R 0) (R 1) (R 2))
    (hK : K = {v : V | v ∈ R 0} ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R 1} ∪ {v : V | v ∈ R 2})
    (hFK : F ⊆ Kᶜ) (hf : IsPathFrom G f f₁ fn) (hfF : F = {x : V | x ∈ f})
    (hn : 2 ≤ f.length) (hFmaj : ∀ w ∈ F, ¬ MajorForPrism G a b w)
    (hFloc : ¬ LocalForPrism a b (R 0) (R 1) (R 2) (attachments G F K))
    (hXu : attachments G F K ⊆
      attachments G (F \ {f₁}) K ∪ attachments G (F \ {fn}) K)
    (h1 : LocalForPrism a b (R 0) (R 1) (R 2) (attachments G (F \ {f₁}) K))
    (h2 : LocalForPrism a b (R 0) (R 1) (R 2) (attachments G (F \ {fn}) K)) :
    Thm101Assembly.Concl G a b R K f f₁ fn ∨
      Thm101Assembly.Concl G a b R K f.reverse fn f₁ := by
  have hfr : IsPathFrom G f.reverse fn f₁ := PathBasics.isPathFrom_reverse hf
  have hfFr : F = {x : V | x ∈ f.reverse} := by
    rw [hfF]; ext x; simp
  have hnr : 2 ≤ f.reverse.length := by simpa using hn
  -- Claims (2) and (3) deliver the conclusion for the *reversed* path, so feeding them the
  -- reversed path `f.reverse` (with ends `fn`, `f₁`) delivers it for `f` itself.
  have unrev : Thm101Assembly.Concl G a b R K f.reverse.reverse f₁ fn →
      Thm101Assembly.Concl G a b R K f f₁ fn := fun h => by
    rwa [List.reverse_reverse] at h
  have contra : ∀ S : Set V, attachments G (F \ {f₁}) K ⊆ S →
      attachments G (F \ {fn}) K ⊆ S → LocalForPrism a b (R 0) (R 1) (R 2) S → False :=
    fun S s1 s2 hS => hFloc (local_mono hS (hXu.trans (Set.union_subset s1 s2)))
  rcases h1 with q1 | q1 | q1 | q1 | q1
  · -- X₁ ⊆ V(R 0)
    rcases h2 with q2 | q2 | q2 | q2 | q2
    · exact (contra _ q1 q2 (Or.inl subset_rfl)).elim
    · refine Or.inl (case_endgame G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.swap 0 1) hprism hK hFK hf hfF
        hn hFmaj hFloc ?_ ?_)
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1) 1 = 0 from by decide]; exact q1
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1) 0 = 1 from by decide]; exact q2
    · refine Or.inl (case_endgame G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn
        (Equiv.swap 0 1 * Equiv.swap 0 2) hprism hK hFK hf hfF hn hFmaj hFloc ?_ ?_)
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1 * Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 2) 1 = 0 from by decide]
        exact q1
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1 * Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 2) 0 = 2 from by decide]
        exact q2
    · exact Or.inl (unrev (case_two_fwd G hG a b R K F f.reverse fn f₁ (Equiv.refl (Fin 3))
        hprism hK hFK hfr hfFr hnr hFmaj hFloc q2 q1))
    · exact Or.inl (unrev (case_two_swap G hG a b R K F f.reverse fn f₁ (Equiv.refl (Fin 3))
        hprism hK hFK hfr hfFr hnr hFmaj hFloc q2 q1))
  · -- X₁ ⊆ V(R 1)
    rcases h2 with q2 | q2 | q2 | q2 | q2
    · exact Or.inl (case_endgame G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.refl (Fin 3)) hprism hK hFK hf
        hfF hn hFmaj hFloc q1 q2)
    · exact (contra _ q1 q2 (Or.inr (Or.inl subset_rfl))).elim
    · refine Or.inl (case_endgame G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.swap 0 2) hprism hK hFK hf hfF
        hn hFmaj hFloc ?_ ?_)
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 2) 1 = 1 from by decide]; exact q1
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 2) 0 = 2 from by decide]; exact q2
    · refine Or.inl (unrev (case_two_fwd G hG a b R K F f.reverse fn f₁ (Equiv.swap 0 1) hprism
        hK hFK hfr hfFr hnr hFmaj hFloc q2 ?_))
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1) 0 = 1 from by decide]; exact q1
    · refine Or.inl (unrev (case_two_swap G hG a b R K F f.reverse fn f₁ (Equiv.swap 0 1) hprism
        hK hFK hfr hfFr hnr hFmaj hFloc q2 ?_))
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1) 0 = 1 from by decide]; exact q1
  · -- X₁ ⊆ V(R 2)
    rcases h2 with q2 | q2 | q2 | q2 | q2
    · refine Or.inl (case_endgame G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.swap 1 2) hprism hK hFK hf hfF
        hn hFmaj hFloc ?_ ?_)
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (1 : Fin 3) 2) 1 = 2 from by decide]; exact q1
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (1 : Fin 3) 2) 0 = 0 from by decide]; exact q2
    · refine Or.inl (case_endgame G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn
        (Equiv.swap 0 1 * Equiv.swap 1 2) hprism hK hFK hf hfF hn hFmaj hFloc ?_ ?_)
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1 * Equiv.swap (1 : Fin 3) 2) 1 = 2 from by decide]
        exact q1
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1 * Equiv.swap (1 : Fin 3) 2) 0 = 1 from by decide]
        exact q2
    · exact (contra _ q1 q2 (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl subset_rfl)))).elim
    · refine Or.inl (unrev (case_two_fwd G hG a b R K F f.reverse fn f₁ (Equiv.swap 0 2) hprism
        hK hFK hfr hfFr hnr hFmaj hFloc q2 ?_))
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 2) 0 = 2 from by decide]; exact q1
    · refine Or.inl (unrev (case_two_swap G hG a b R K F f.reverse fn f₁ (Equiv.swap 0 2) hprism
        hK hFK hfr hfFr hnr hFmaj hFloc q2 ?_))
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 2) 0 = 2 from by decide]; exact q1
  · -- X₁ ⊆ A
    rcases h2 with q2 | q2 | q2 | q2 | q2
    · exact Or.inr (case_two_fwd G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.refl (Fin 3)) hprism hK hFK hf
        hfF hn hFmaj hFloc q1 q2)
    · refine Or.inr (case_two_fwd G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.swap 0 1) hprism hK hFK hf
        hfF hn hFmaj hFloc q1 ?_)
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1) 0 = 1 from by decide]; exact q2
    · refine Or.inr (case_two_fwd G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.swap 0 2) hprism hK hFK hf
        hfF hn hFmaj hFloc q1 ?_)
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 2) 0 = 2 from by decide]; exact q2
    · exact (contra _ q1 q2 (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl subset_rfl))))).elim
    · exact case_three_fwd G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn hprism hK hFK hf hfF hn hFmaj hFloc q1 q2
  · -- X₁ ⊆ B
    rcases h2 with q2 | q2 | q2 | q2 | q2
    · exact Or.inr (case_two_swap G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.refl (Fin 3)) hprism hK hFK hf
        hfF hn hFmaj hFloc q1 q2)
    · refine Or.inr (case_two_swap G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.swap 0 1) hprism hK hFK hf
        hfF hn hFmaj hFloc q1 ?_)
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 1) 0 = 1 from by decide]; exact q2
    · refine Or.inr (case_two_swap G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn (Equiv.swap 0 2) hprism hK hFK hf
        hfF hn hFmaj hFloc q1 ?_)
      · rw [show (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 3) 2) 0 = 2 from by decide]; exact q2
    · exact case_three_swap G hG a b R K F f f₁ fn hprism hK hFK hf hfF hn hFmaj hFloc q1 q2
    · exact (contra _ q1 q2 (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr subset_rfl))))).elim

decls.name: thm_10_2
decls.docstring:
**10.2** (printed p. 58)

PAPER: *"Let `R₁, R₂, R₃, K, F` be as in 10.1, and suppose that 10.1.1 holds.  Then either
`R₁` and `R₂` both have length 1, or there is a nondegenerate appearance of `K₄` in `G`."*

The hypotheses inherited from 10.1 are written out in full: `G` is Berge, `R₁, R₂, R₃` form
the prism `K` with triangles `{a₁, a₂, a₃}` and `{b₁, b₂, b₃}`, `F ⊆ V(G) \ V(K)` is
connected, its set of attachments in `K` is not local, and no vertex of `F` is major with
respect to `K`.  *"10.1.1 holds"* is 10.1's first alternative for this very labelling of the
prism (`R₁` and `R₂` being the two paths named in its conclusion), including its final
"(therefore)" clause.

The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 10.3 (printed on PDF page 60).

decls.name: thm_10_4
decls.docstring:
**10.4** (printed p. 59), introduced by *"Another useful corollary of 10.1 is the
following."*

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, such that there is no nondegenerate appearance of `K₄` in `G`.
Let `R₁, R₂, R₃` form a prism `K` in a Berge graph `G`, with triangles `{a₁, a₂, a₃}` and
`{b₁, b₂, b₃}`, where each `Rᵢ` has ends `aᵢ` and `bᵢ`.  Let `F ⊆ V(G) \ V(K)` be connected,
such that if the prism is even then no vertex in `F` is major with respect to `K`.  Assume
that the set of attachments of `F` in `K` is not local, but none are in `V(R₃)`.  Then
`|F| ≥ 2`, and the set of attachments of `F` in `K` is precisely `{a₁, b₁, a₂, b₂}`."*

*"if the prism is even then no vertex in `F` is major"* is transcribed as the implication it
is.  `|F| ≥ 2` is `F.Nontrivial` (`∃ x ∈ F, ∃ y ∈ F, x ≠ y`), and *"none are in `V(R₃)`"*
says that no attachment of `F` in `K` lies on `R₃`.

links.rationale: The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 10.4 (printed on PDF page 61).

decls.name: thm_10_5
decls.docstring:
**10.5** (printed p. 59), introduced by *"The next result is a close relative of 7.5."*

PAPER: *"Let `G` be Berge, such that there is no nondegenerate appearance of `K₄` in `G`.  If
there is an even prism `K` in `G`, such that some vertex of `G` is major with respect to `K`,
then `G` admits a balanced skew partition."*

The even prism and the major vertex are named rather than existentially quantified, which is
the same statement.

The Lean statement of the paper's numbered result 10.6 (printed on PDF page 62).

decls.name: thm_11_1
decls.docstring:
**11.1** (printed p. 64)

PAPER: *"Let `G` be a Berge graph, such that there is no nondegenerate appearance of `K₄` in
`G`.  Let `S = (A, C, B)` be a step-connected strip in `G`, and let `a₀`-`R₀`-`b₀` be a
banister.  Suppose that `v ∈ V(G) \ V(S)` has a neighbour in `A ∪ C`, and has no neighbour in
`B`; and that `P` is a path in `G \ (V(S) ∪ {a₀})` from `v` to `b₀`, such that there are no
edges between `P*` and `V(S)`.  Then `v` is a left-star."*

Notes on the transcription.

* `V(S) = A ∪ B ∪ C`, so `v ∈ V(G) \ V(S)` is `v ∉ A ∪ B ∪ C`.
* *"`P` is a path in `G \ (V(S) ∪ {a₀})` from `v` to `b₀`"* is: `P` is a path of `G` with ends
  `v` and `b₀`, none of whose vertices lies in `V(S) ∪ {a₀}`.
* *"has no neighbour in `B`"* is `VertexAnticomplete G v B`.

decls.name: rung_mem_ABC
decls.docstring: Every vertex of a rung of the strip `(A, C, B)` lies in `V(S) = A ∪ B ∪ C`.

decls.name: banister_rung_edges
decls.docstring:
The paper's *"`R₀`, `R₁`, `R₂` form a prism"*, edge clause between the banister and a
rung: the only edges between a banister `a₀-R₀-b₀` and a rung `a-R-b` are `a₀a` and `b₀b`.

decls.name: not_two_le_ncard
decls.docstring:
If every neighbour of `w` among `x, y, z` equals `c`, then `w` has at most one neighbour
in `{x, y, z}`, so it does not saturate a triangle.
